doc_description: PepsiCo’s Form 8‑K (Item 8.01) dated May 26, 2023 announces the termination of its 2022 $3.8B 364‑day and five‑year revolvers and entry into new unsecured revolving credit facilities—a $4.2B 364‑day line and a $4.2B five‑year line (USD/EUR, upsizeable to $4.95B, annual/term‑loan extension features, including a €750M same‑day swingline)—with Citibank, N.A. as administrative agent, with full agreements filed as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- PepsiCo filed a Form 8-K (Item 8.01 – Other Events) dated May 26, 2023.
- Terminated two existing $3.8 billion unsecured revolving credit facilities dated May 27, 2022 (a 364-day facility and a five-year facility); no borrowings were outstanding at termination.
- Entered into new unsecured revolving credit agreements with Citibank, N.A. as administrative agent:
  - 2023 364-Day Credit Agreement: $4.2 billion capacity in USD and/or EUR; expires May 24, 2024; option to increase total commitments up to $4.95 billion; ability to renew for an additional 364 days or convert outstanding amounts to a term loan of up to one year; borrow, prepay, and reborrow permitted; for general corporate purposes; customary reps/warranties and events of default.
  - 2023 Five-Year Credit Agreement: $4.2 billion capacity in USD and/or EUR; includes a $750 million same-day Euro swingline subfacility; expires May 26, 2028; option to increase total commitments up to $4.95 billion; annual one-year renewal option; borrow, prepay, and reborrow permitted; for general corporate purposes; customary reps/warranties and events of default.
- Notes that lenders and affiliates have or may engage in ordinary-course banking/investment banking relationships with PepsiCo.
- Full agreements filed as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and incorporated by reference.
- Cover page includes PepsiCo’s registrant details and a list of securities registered on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC.

nodes.title: Other Events.
nodes.heading: Item 8.01.Other Events.
nodes.start_phrase: Effective May 26, 2023, PepsiCo, Inc. (“PepsiCo”) terminated the $3,800,000,000 364 day unsecured revolving credit agreement, dated as of May 27, 2022, among PepsiCo, as borrower, the lenders party thereto, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (the “2022 364 Day Credit Agreement”).
nodes.summary:
- On May 26, 2023, PepsiCo terminated its 2022 $3.8 billion 364‑day and $3.8 billion five‑year unsecured revolving credit agreements; there were no outstanding borrowings at termination.
- The same day, PepsiCo entered a new $4.2 billion 364‑day unsecured revolving credit agreement with Citibank, N.A. as administrative agent, available to PepsiCo and its borrowing subsidiaries in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, expiring May 24, 2024. The facility may be upsized to $4.95 billion, renewed for an additional 364 days, or converted to a term loan of up to one year (maturing no later than the anniversary of the then‑effective termination date). Borrowings can be made, prepaid, and reborrowed for general corporate purposes, subject to customary representations, warranties, and events of default. Lenders and their affiliates may have ongoing banking relationships with PepsiCo.
- Also on May 26, 2023, PepsiCo entered a new $4.2 billion five‑year unsecured revolving credit agreement with Citibank, N.A. as administrative agent, available in U.S. Dollars and/or Euros, expiring May 26, 2028. It includes a $750 million Euro‑denominated same‑day swing line subfacility, an option to increase commitments to $4.95 billion, and an annual renewal option for one additional year. Borrowings can be made, prepaid, and reborrowed for general corporate purposes, subject to customary terms; lenders and affiliates may have other banking relationships with PepsiCo.
- The full texts of the new 2023 credit agreements are filed as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 to the Form 8‑K.

nodes.title: Exhibit 99.1
nodes.heading: Exhibit 99.1
nodes.start_phrase: PEPSICO, INC., a North Carolina corporation (the “Company”), the banks, financial institutions and other institutional lenders (the “Initial Lenders”) listed on the signature pages hereof, and Citibank, N.A., as administrative agent (in such capacity, the “Agent”) for the Lenders (as hereinafter defined), agree, as of May 26, 2023, as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Document type and date: Execution copy of a 364-Day Credit Agreement, dated May 26, 2023, filed as Exhibit 99.1.
- Parties: PepsiCo, Inc. as Borrower; a syndicate of lenders; Citibank, N.A. as Administrative Agent; JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. and Bank of America, N.A. as Syndication Agents; Citibank, N.A., JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., and BofA Securities, Inc. as Joint Lead Arrangers and Joint Bookrunners.
- Facility size and tenor: Up to $4.2 billion aggregate principal amount under a 364-day facility, with provisions addressing extension/term loan conversion.
- Purpose and availability: Credit to PepsiCo and designated Borrowing Subsidiaries for general corporate purposes, including working capital, capital investments, and acquisitions.
- Core mechanics (Article II): 
  - Types of advances (Base Rate, Eurocurrency Rate, Term SOFR) and procedures for making borrowings.
  - Fees; commitment termination, reduction, or increase; repayment and possible termination date extension.
  - Interest and rate determination; optional conversion/continuation of advances; prepayments.
  - Increased costs and illegality protections; payment mechanics and evidence of debt; tax provisions; sharing of payments.
  - Use of proceeds; borrowings by Borrowing Subsidiaries (via designation letters); benchmark replacement setting (including Term SOFR and adjustments); defaulting lender provisions.
- Conditions (Article III): Conditions precedent to effectiveness, to each borrowing, and to any term loan conversion, plus related determinations.
- Representations and warranties (Article IV): Company representations supporting the credit.
- Covenants (Article V): Affirmative and negative covenants governing ongoing compliance.
- Events of Default (Article VI): Defined defaults and related remedies.
- Agency provisions (Article VII): Administrative Agent’s appointment/authority, rights, exculpation, reliance, indemnification, delegation, resignation; roles of Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers; ERISA matters; erroneous payments protocol.
- Miscellaneous (Article VIII): Amendments and notices; no waiver/remedies; costs/expenses; set-off; binding effect; assignments/participations; confidentiality; governing law, counterparts, jurisdiction, and jury trial waiver; USA PATRIOT Act notice; no fiduciary duties; bail-in acknowledgment; judgment currency provisions.
- Guarantee (Article IX): An unconditional, continuing guarantee framework with reinstatement, subrogation, and remedies.
- Schedules and Exhibits: Agent’s address; forms of Note, Notice of Borrowing, Assignment and Assumption, Designation Letter (for Borrowing Subsidiaries), and Termination Letter.
- Definitions (Article I): Comprehensive defined terms and accounting/time computation provisions, including definitions such as Adjusted Term SOFR (with a floor), Advance, Affiliate, and references to benchmark rate mechanics.

nodes.title: Certain Defined Terms
nodes.heading: Section 1.01 Certain Defined Terms
nodes.start_phrase: As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the following meanings (such meanings to be equally applicable to both the singular and plural forms of the terms defined):
nodes.summary:
- Parties and purpose: 364‑Day Credit Agreement dated May 26, 2023 among PepsiCo, Inc. (as Company and Borrower/Guarantor), various lenders, and Citibank, N.A. as Administrative Agent; facility supports general corporate purposes (including working capital, capex, and acquisitions).
- Facility size and form: Revolving credit facility up to $4.2 billion, available to the Company and designated Borrowing Subsidiaries.
- Currencies and advance types: Advances in U.S. Dollars and Euros; Types include Base Rate Advances (USD), Term SOFR Advances (USD), and Eurocurrency Rate Advances (EUR tied to EURIBOR).
- Interest benchmarks and pricing mechanics:
  - Base Rate defined as the highest of Citibank base rate, Federal Funds Rate + 0.50%, or 1‑month Adjusted Term SOFR + 1.00%.
  - Term SOFR framework (Term SOFR, Adjusted Term SOFR, Term SOFR Reference Rate, Daily Simple SOFR), with floors at zero where specified and detailed determination conventions.
  - EURIBO Rate (EURIBOR) for Euro advances, floored at zero.
  - Default Rate is applicable margin plus 2% for overdue amounts/advances.
- Borrowing mechanics and minima: “Borrowing,” “Advance,” “Interest Period” rules (1, 3, or 6 months; business day adjustments), Business Day definitions (including TARGET and U.S. Government Securities Business Days), Borrowing Minimums/Multiples ($/€ 10,000,000 minimum; $/€ 1,000,000 multiples).
- Key dates and options: Termination Date of May 24, 2024 (extendable for consenting lenders); optional Term Loan Election converting outstanding advances on the Termination Date into a term loan with a Maturity Date up to one year later.
- Commitments and changes: Definitions for Commitments; mechanisms referenced for commitment reductions, increases (new or existing lenders), and extensions; related roles (Extending Lender, New Lender, Replacement Lender) and notices/dates.
- Parties, roles, and documentation: Definitions of Lenders, Lead Arrangers, Syndication Agents; Agent’s Account/Address; Loan Documents (Agreement, Notes, side letter, Designation/Termination Letters).
- Borrowing Subsidiaries: Ability to add/remove via Designation and Termination Letters; Company acts as guarantor under Article IX (referenced).
- Assignment/participation framework: Eligible Assignee criteria (including rating and size thresholds), Assignment and Assumption, Register/Participant Register, SPV/Granting Lender concepts.
- Defaults and lender status: “Default,” “Events of Default” (cross‑referenced), “Defaulting Lender” criteria and related determinations; “Non‑Defaulting Lender.”
- Financial and corporate definitions: Debt (comprehensive), Consolidated Net Tangible Assets, Material Subsidiary, Restricted/Unrestricted Subsidiary, Subsidiary, Principal Property, Lien, Voting Stock.
- Materiality and adverse effect: Material Adverse Change and Material Adverse Effect definitions.
- Regulatory, sanctions, and compliance: Anti‑Corruption Laws; OFAC‑related terms (Sanctioned Country, SDN List); Environmental Law; ERISA; bail‑in and resolution authority terms for EEA/UK; Write‑Down and Conversion Powers.
- Tax and KYC: FATCA, Excluded Taxes, Other Taxes, Foreign Lender, Beneficial Ownership Certification/Regulation, United States Person.
- Benchmark transition and fallback: Benchmark, Benchmark Replacement (and Adjustment/Date), Benchmark Transition Event/Unavailability Period, Conforming Changes, Relevant Governmental Body, Floor, Unadjusted Benchmark Replacement.
- Administrative and operational provisions: Applicable Lending Offices, Communications/Platform, Confidential Information, Erroneous Payment framework, Indemnified Parties, notices, and agent resignation/removal date terms.
- Accounting and time computation: GAAP as governing accounting standard; rules for computing time periods (“from,” “to,” “until”).

nodes.title: Computation of Time Periods
nodes.heading: Section 1.02 Computation of Time Periods
nodes.start_phrase: In this Agreement in the computation of periods of time from a specified date to a later specified date, the word “from” means “from and including” and the words “to” and “until” each mean “to but excluding”.

It sets out specific defined terms—some by cross-reference to other sections—including Termination Letter, Total Committed Increase, Type (of Advance), UK Financial Institution, UK Resolution Authority, Unadjusted Benchmark Replacement, United States Person, U.S. Government Securities Business Day (using SIFMA guidance), Voting Stock, and Write-Down and Conversion Powers. nodes.title: Accounting Terms
nodes.heading: Section 1.03 Accounting Terms
nodes.start_phrase: All accounting terms not specifically defined herein shall be construed in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States consistent with those applied in the preparation of the financial statements referred to in Section 4.01(e) (“GAAP”).
nodes.summary: This excerpt is from the definitions and interpretive provisions of a financing agreement. It lists and cross‑references several defined terms (e.g., Termination Letter, Total Committed Increase, Type, UK Financial Institution/Resolution Authority, Unadjusted Benchmark Replacement, Write‑Down and Conversion Powers), and provides substantive definitions for: Undisclosed Administration (a non‑public regulatory appointment of an insolvency official over a lender or its parent), United States Person (by reference to IRC §7701), Unrestricted Subsidiary (subsidiaries primarily in financial services, holding companies of such, or board‑designated), U.S. Government Securities Business Day (tied to SIFMA closure recommendations), and Voting Stock (equity with ordinary voting rights). It also sets interpretation rules: “from” is inclusive while “to”/“until” are exclusive for time calculations, and all accounting terms are to be construed under U.S. GAAP consistent with the company’s referenced financial statements.

nodes.title: Divisions
nodes.heading: Section 1.04 Divisions
nodes.start_phrase: For all purposes under the Loan Documents, in connection with any division or plan of division under Delaware law (or any comparable event under a different jurisdiction’s laws), if any asset, right, obligation or liability of any Person becomes the asset, right, obligation or liability of a different Person, then it shall be deemed to have been transferred from the original Person to the subsequent Person.
nodes.summary:
- Defines treatment of corporate “divisions” (e.g., under Delaware law): any asset, right, obligation, or liability allocated to a different Person in a division is deemed transferred from the original Person to the new Person for all purposes under the Loan Documents.
- Disclaims the Agent’s responsibility and liability regarding interest rate benchmarks (Base Rate, Term SOFR, Adjusted Term SOFR, EURIBOR, and any Benchmark/Benchmark Replacement), including their continuation, calculation, administration, replacements, or related Conforming Changes; permits the Agent to choose information sources in its reasonable discretion and notes Agent/affiliates may engage in transactions that could adversely affect such rates; limits liability for errors or damages arising from rate determinations.
- Introduces Article II on the amounts and terms of Advances.
- Provides that each Lender will make USD and/or EUR Advances to the Company and Borrowing Subsidiaries from the Effective Date to the Termination Date, up to its Commitment (with Euro borrowings measured by Dollar Equivalent at the Notice of Borrowing date); each Borrowing must meet minimum/multiple size requirements, be of the same Type and currency, and be funded ratably by Lenders; Borrowers may borrow, prepay (per Section 2.10), and reborrow within Commitments.

nodes.title: Rates
nodes.heading: Section 1.05 Rates
nodes.start_phrase: The Agent does not warrant or accept any responsibility for, and shall not have any liability with respect to, (a) the continuation of, administration of, submission of, calculation of or any other matter related to the Base Rate,
nodes.summary:
- Division mechanics (Section 1.04): For any division or similar legal process (e.g., under Delaware law), if assets, rights, obligations, or liabilities move from one Person to another, they are deemed transferred from the original to the subsequent Person for all Loan Document purposes.
- Benchmark and rate disclaimers (Section 1.05): The Agent disclaims responsibility and liability for the continuation, administration, submission, calculation, or replacement of Base Rate, Term SOFR (including Adjusted Term SOFR and the Term SOFR Reference Rate), the EURIBO Rate, or any Benchmark, including any Benchmark Replacement and Conforming Changes. No assurance is given on similarity, value, liquidity, or economic equivalence of any successor/replacement rate. The Agent and its affiliates may engage in transactions affecting these rates, potentially adversely to Borrowers. The Agent may select information sources in its reasonable discretion and has no liability for errors or damages arising from rate calculations.
- Advances terms (Article II, Section 2.01): Lenders agree to make revolving Advances in Dollars and/or Euros to the Company and Borrowing Subsidiaries from the Effective Date to the Termination Date, up to each Lender’s Commitment (with Euro borrowings counted by Dollar Equivalent at the borrowing notice date). Each borrowing must meet minimum/multiple size requirements, be of the same Type and currency, and be funded ratably by Lenders. Borrowers may borrow, prepay, and reborrow within the commitment limits.

nodes.title: The Advances
nodes.heading: Section 2.01 The Advances
nodes.start_phrase: Each Lender severally agrees, on the terms and conditions hereinafter set forth, to make Advances in Dollars and/or Euros to the Company and any Borrowing Subsidiary from time to time on any Business Day during the period from the Effective Date until the Termination Date in an aggregate amount (based in respect of any Advances to be denominated in Euros by reference to the Equivalent thereof in Dollars determined on the date of delivery of the applicable Notice of Borrowing) not to exceed at any time outstanding such Lender’s Commitment.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies treatment of corporate divisions: any assets, rights, obligations, or liabilities that move to a different person due to a Delaware (or analogous) division are deemed transferred from the original to the new person for all Loan Document purposes.
- Disclaims Agent responsibility and liability regarding interest rate benchmarks (e.g., Base Rate, Term SOFR, EURIBOR) and any replacements or conforming changes; permits the Agent to select data sources and acknowledges the Agent/affiliates may engage in transactions affecting rate calculations, even if adverse to borrowers.
- Introduces Article II (Amounts and Terms of the Advances) and sets out Section 2.01: a revolving credit framework where each Lender agrees severally to make USD and/or EUR advances to the Company and Borrowing Subsidiaries up to its Commitment from the Effective Date to the Termination Date; EUR borrowings are measured by their USD equivalent at the Notice of Borrowing; each borrowing must meet specified minimums/multiples, be of the same type and currency, and be funded pro rata; borrowings may be prepaid and reborrowed within commitments.

nodes.title: Making the Advances
nodes.heading: Section 2.02 Making the Advances
nodes.start_phrase: Each Borrowing shall be made on notice, given not later than (x) 11:00 A.M. (New York City time) on the third U.S. Government Securities Business Day prior to the date of the proposed Borrowing in the case of a Borrowing consisting of Term SOFR Advances,
nodes.summary:
- Section 2.02 (Making the Advances)
  - Borrowing notice deadlines and types:
    - Term SOFR Advances: notice by 11:00 A.M. New York time, 3 U.S. Government Securities Business Days prior.
    - Eurocurrency Rate Advances: notice by 4:00 P.M. London time, 3 Business Days prior.
    - Base Rate Advances: notice by 11:00 A.M. New York time, same day.
  - Notice of Borrowing requirements: emailed (Exhibit B form) specifying date, type, aggregate amount, currency and initial Interest Period (for Term SOFR/Eurocurrency), and the borrower (Company or Borrowing Subsidiary).
  - Funding mechanics: each Lender funds its ratable share to the Agent by 1:00 P.M. New York time on the borrowing date; Agent releases funds to the borrower upon satisfaction of Article III conditions, to the borrower’s account per Section 8.02.
  - Limitations: no Term SOFR/Eurocurrency selection if below Borrowing Minimum or if such obligations are suspended under Sections 2.08 or 2.12; no more than 12 separate Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Borrowings outstanding at any time.
  - Irrevocability and indemnity: Notices of Borrowing are irrevocable; the Company must indemnify Lenders for breakage costs if Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Borrowings fail to close due to unmet Article III conditions.
  - Default funding assumptions: Agent may assume a Lender funded absent contrary notice; if not funded, the borrower and the defaulting Lender must repay the Agent on demand with interest (borrower at the applicable loan rate; lender at Federal Funds Rate for USD or Agent’s euro cost of funds for EUR). Upon repayment, the amount becomes that Lender’s Advance and is made available to the borrower.
  - Lender failures: one Lender’s failure to fund does not relieve others; no Lender is liable for another’s failure.

- Section 2.03: Reserved.

- Section 2.04 (Fees)
  - Commitment fee: 0.025% per annum on each Lender’s unused commitment, calculated daily from the Effective Date (or assignment effective date) until the Termination Date; payable quarterly (last day of June, September, December, March) starting June 30, 2023, and on the Termination Date.
  - Agent’s fees: payable as separately agreed between the Company and the Agent.

- Section 2.05 (Termination, Reduction or Increase of Commitments)
  - Company’s optional reduction/termination: with at least 3 Business Days’ notice, may terminate all or reduce ratably unused commitments; partial reductions must be $25,000,000 and integral multiples of $1,000,000; total commitments cannot be reduced below outstanding Advances.
  - Action against certain Lenders: if a Lender demands compensation under Sections 2.11 or 2.14, or is a Defaulting or Non-Consenting Lender, the Company may, on 3 Business Days’ notice, terminate that Lender’s commitment or require assignment of its interests under Section 8.07; upon termination, the Company must pay all principal, accrued interest, and other amounts owed to that Lender, after which it ceases to be a party.

nodes.title: Fees
nodes.heading: Section 2.04 Fees
nodes.start_phrase: The Company agrees to pay to the Agent for the account of each Lender a commitment fee on the aggregate amount of such Lender’s unused portion of the Commitment from the Effective Date in the case of each Initial Lender and from the effective date specified in the Assignment and Assumption pursuant to which it became a Lender in the case of each other Lender until the Termination Date (on a daily basis) at a rate per annum equal to 0.025%, payable in arrears quarterly on the last day of each June, September, December and March, commencing June 30, 2023, and on the Termination Date.
nodes.summary:
- Funding shortfalls and Agent advances: If the Agent hasn’t received a Lender’s share of a Borrowing but has no notice of non-funding, it may advance the full amount to the Borrower assuming the Lender funded. If a Lender hasn’t actually funded, both that Lender and the Borrower must promptly repay the Agent the corresponding amount on demand, with interest from the date advanced until repaid. Interest: for the Borrower, at the rate applicable to the relevant Advances; for the Lender, at the Federal Funds Rate for Dollar Advances or the Agent’s cost of funds for Euro Advances. If the Lender later pays the Agent, the payment is deemed that Lender’s Advance and is made available to the Borrower in same-day funds.
- Lender funding independence: One Lender’s failure to fund does not relieve other Lenders of their obligations; no Lender is liable for another’s failure.
- Section 2.03 is reserved.
- Fees:
  - Commitment fee: 0.025% per annum on each Lender’s unused Commitment, accruing daily from the Effective Date (or the effective date of an assignment for new Lenders) until the Termination Date, payable quarterly in arrears (June 30, September 30, December 31, March 31) starting June 30, 2023, and on the Termination Date.
  - Agent’s fees: payable as separately agreed between the Company and the Agent.
- Commitments—termination/reduction; lender replacement:
  - The Company may, with at least three Business Days’ notice, terminate entirely or reduce ratably the unused Commitments, provided each partial reduction is at least $25,000,000 and then in $1,000,000 increments, and total Commitments may not be reduced below outstanding Advances.
  - If a Lender demands amounts under Sections 2.11 or 2.14, or is a Defaulting or Non-Consenting Lender, the Company may on three Business Days’ notice terminate that Lender’s Commitment or require it to assign all rights and obligations under Section 8.07. Upon termination, the Company must pay that Lender all outstanding principal, accrued interest, and other amounts due; thereafter the Lender ceases to be a party.

nodes.title: Termination, Reduction or Increase of Commitments
nodes.heading: Section 2.05 Termination, Reduction or Increase of Commitments
nodes.start_phrase: The Company shall have the right, upon at least three Business Days’ notice to the Agent, to terminate in whole or reduce ratably in part the unused portions of the respective Commitments of the Lenders; provided that each partial reduction shall be in the aggregate amount of $25,000,000 or an integral multiple of $1,000,000 in excess thereof and provided, further that the aggregate amount of the Commitments of the Lenders shall not be reduced to an amount that is less than the aggregate principal amount of the Advances then outstanding.
nodes.summary:
- Agent funding assumption and shortfall mechanics: If a Lender doesn’t fund its share of a Borrowing and hasn’t given prior notice, the Agent may advance the funds to the Borrower assuming the Lender funded. The Borrower and the non-funding Lender must promptly repay the Agent with interest (Borrower at the loan’s applicable rate; Lender at the Federal Funds Rate for USD Advances or the Agent’s EUR funding cost for Euro Advances). When the Lender repays, that amount becomes its Advance. Funds are credited to the Borrower’s account at the Agent.
- Independent funding obligations: One Lender’s failure to fund doesn’t relieve others; no Lender is liable for another’s failure.
- Fees:
  - Commitment fee: 0.025% per annum on each Lender’s unused Commitment, calculated daily from each Lender’s effective date to the Termination Date; payable quarterly in arrears (end of June, September, December, March) and on the Termination Date.
  - Agent’s fees: Payable as separately agreed between the Company and the Agent.
- Termination/reduction of Commitments: The Company may, with at least 3 Business Days’ notice, terminate all or reduce unused Commitments ratably, in minimum amounts of $25,000,000 and $1,000,000 increments, but not below outstanding Advances.
- Lender-specific termination/assignment: If a Lender demands certain increased costs/compensation, is a Defaulting Lender, or is Non-Consenting, the Company may on 3 Business Days’ notice terminate that Lender’s Commitment or require it to assign its interests. Upon termination, the Company must pay that Lender all principal, accrued interest, and other amounts due; the Lender then exits the agreement.
- Commitment increases:
  - Parameters: Company may propose increases of at least $25,000,000 (in $1,000,000 increments), subject to (i) no Default on notice and increase dates and (ii) an aggregate Commitment cap of $4,950,000,000.
  - Process: Company delivers an Increase Notice specifying amount, Increase Date (≥30 days out), and any proposed New Lenders. Agent solicits New Lenders first (minimum $25,000,000 each; execution of acceptable documentation; $3,500 processing fee). If undersubscribed, existing Lenders may offer increases.
  - Effectiveness threshold: Increases take effect only if total committed increases reach at least $25,000,000; otherwise, no change.
  - Rebalancing: On the Increase Date, borrowings and/or prepayments are effected so outstanding Advances are held pro rata by all Lenders (including New Lenders) by Type and Interest Period.
  - Allocation: If total commitments exceed the proposed increase, allocation is first to New Lenders up to their offers (as the Company agrees), then pro rata to existing Lenders based on their offered increases; if not oversubscribed, each party receives its offered amount.
  - Conditions precedent: Delivery of Notes if requested and evidence (including updated legal opinions) that the increases and related borrowings are duly authorized.

nodes.title: Repayment of Advances; Extension of Termination Date
nodes.heading: Section 2.06 Repayment of Advances; Extension of Termination Date
nodes.start_phrase: (i) Subject to the next succeeding sentence, each Borrower shall repay to the Agent for the ratable account of the Lenders on the Termination Date the aggregate principal amount of the Advances made to such Borrower then outstanding, and all accrued but unpaid interest in connection therewith and (ii) the Company shall pay to the Agent for the ratable account of the Lenders on the Termination Date all fees and all other amounts due hereunder.
nodes.summary:
- Sets repayment obligations: on the Termination Date, each Borrower must repay all outstanding Advances plus accrued interest to the Agent for the Lenders’ ratable accounts, and the Company must pay all fees and other amounts due.
- Provides an optional Term Loan Election: by notice on or before the Termination Date, the Company may convert all outstanding Advances into a term loan repayable in full on the Maturity Date, if Section 3.03 conditions are satisfied at notice and on the conversion date; converted Advances remain “Advances,” but any prepaid amounts cannot be reborrowed.
- Establishes a procedure to extend the Termination Date by 364 days: Company notice 60–30 days before the current Termination Date; each Lender may, in its sole discretion, agree (Extending Lender) or be deemed to decline if silent (Declining Lender).
- Allows replacement of Declining Lenders before the Extension Date with Eligible Assignees (including Extending Lenders) that accept all rights/obligations and the extension, conditioned on compliance with assignment provisions, full payoff to Declining Lenders, and effectiveness on the Extension Date.
- If all Declining Lenders are replaced and no Default exists immediately before the Extension Date, the Termination Date is extended by 364 days (with a business day adjustment). If some are not replaced, the Company may withdraw the request or, if no Default, pay such Declining Lenders in full on the Extension Date, reduce aggregate Commitments by their amounts, and extend the Termination Date for 364 days at the reduced commitment level.
- The extension option is unavailable if the Term Loan Election has already been made for Advances outstanding on that Termination Date.

nodes.title: Interest on Advances
nodes.heading: Section 2.07 Interest on Advances
nodes.start_phrase: Each Borrower shall pay interest on the unpaid principal amount of each Advance made to such Borrower owing to each Lender from the date of such Advance until such principal amount shall be paid in full, at the following rates per annum:
nodes.summary:
- Interest accrues on each Borrower’s unpaid principal of each Advance from funding until repaid in full.
- Base Rate Advances: interest equals the Base Rate in effect, payable in arrears quarterly on the last Business Day of March, June, September, and December, and upon conversion or repayment.
- Term SOFR Advances: interest equals Adjusted Term SOFR for the applicable Interest Period plus 0.625%, payable in arrears on the last day of the Interest Period (and every three months if the Interest Period exceeds three months), and upon conversion or repayment.
- Eurocurrency Rate Advances: interest equals the EURIBO Rate for the applicable Interest Period plus 0.625%, payable in arrears on the last day of the Interest Period (and every three months if the Interest Period exceeds three months), and upon conversion or repayment.
- Default Rate: upon an Event of Default under Section 6.01(a), principal, accrued interest, and other amounts under the loan documents bear interest at the Default Rate, payable on demand.
- Rate determination: the Agent promptly notifies the Company and Lenders of applicable rates used under Section 2.07.
- Market disruption fallback: if a major interbank funding market disruption causes Adjusted Term SOFR or EURIBO to inadequately reflect Required Lenders’ costs, then:
  - Term SOFR Advances automatically convert to Base Rate Advances at the end of their current Interest Periods.
  - Eurocurrency Rate Advances are exchanged into an equivalent Dollar amount and converted to Base Rate Advances.
  - Lenders’ obligations to make or convert into Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances are suspended until the Agent advises the disruption has ended.

nodes.title: Interest Rate Determination
nodes.heading: Section 2.08 Interest Rate Determination
nodes.start_phrase: The Agent shall give prompt notice to the Company and the Lenders of the applicable interest rate determined by the Agent for purposes of Section 2.07.
nodes.summary:
- Covers how interest accrues and is paid on different types of loan advances and how interest rates are determined and adjusted.
- Interest on Advances (Section 2.07):
  - Interest accrues on each Advance from funding until repaid in full.
  - Base Rate Advances: interest equals the Base Rate; payable quarterly in arrears (last Business Day of March, June, September, December) and upon conversion or full payment.
  - Term SOFR Advances: interest equals Adjusted Term SOFR + 0.625%; payable in arrears on the last day of each Interest Period, every three months for periods longer than three months, and upon conversion or full payment.
  - Eurocurrency Rate Advances: interest equals EURIBO Rate + 0.625%; same payment timing as Term SOFR; converts or is exchanged to dollars upon certain triggers.
  - Default Rate: upon an Event of Default under Section 6.01(a), principal, interest, and other amounts bear interest at the Default Rate, payable on demand.
- Interest Rate Determination (Section 2.08):
  - Agent promptly notifies the Company and Lenders of applicable rates.
  - Market disruption: if Required Lenders determine Term SOFR or EURIBO does not reflect funding costs, Term SOFR Advances convert to Base Rate at period end; Eurocurrency Advances are exchanged to dollars and convert to Base Rate; new Term SOFR/Eurocurrency borrowings or conversions are suspended until resolved.
  - Failure to select Interest Period: deemed one-month Interest Period.
  - Small balance trigger: if a Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Borrowing falls below the Borrowing Minimum, it automatically converts/exchanges into Base Rate (Eurocurrency first exchanged to dollars).
  - Event of Default: upon notice from Agent at Required Lenders’ request, all Term SOFR and Eurocurrency Advances convert/exchange into Base Rate; new Term SOFR/Eurocurrency borrowings or conversions are suspended.
  - Rate unavailability: if Term SOFR cannot be determined or EURIBO is not published, Agent notifies; affected Advances convert/exchange into Base Rate at the end of the current Interest Period (or are prepaid for Eurocurrency); obligations to make/convert into such rate-based Advances are suspended until availability resumes.

nodes.title: Optional Conversion or Continuation of Advances
nodes.heading: Section 2.09 Optional Conversion or Continuation of Advances
nodes.start_phrase: The Company may on any Business Day, upon notice given to the Agent not later than 11:00 A.M. (New York City time) on the third U.S. Government Securities Business Day prior to the date of the proposed Conversion or continuation,
nodes.summary:
- Section 2.09 (Optional Conversion or Continuation): The Company may, on proper advance notice to the Agent (by 11:00 a.m. New York time, three U.S. Government Securities Business Days prior), convert Dollar-denominated Advances between Base Rate and Term SOFR or continue existing Advances, subject to Sections 2.08, 2.12, and 2.18. Conversions from Term SOFR to Base Rate can occur only on the last day of the applicable Interest Period; conversions from Base Rate to Term SOFR must meet the Borrowing Minimum and cannot create more separate Borrowings than allowed under Section 2.02(b). The notice must specify the conversion/continuation date, the Dollar Advances affected, and, for Term SOFR, the initial Interest Period. Notices are irrevocable and binding.

- Section 2.10 (Prepayments of Advances):
  - Optional prepayments: The Company may prepay Base Rate Advances with at least one Business Day’s notice and Term SOFR Advances with at least three U.S. Government Securities Business Days’ notice, in whole or ratably in part within the same Borrowing, plus accrued interest. Partial prepayments must be at least the Borrowing Minimum (or a Borrowing Multiple above it). Prepaying Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances may require reimbursement of Lenders’ breakage/compensation under Section 8.04(c).
  - Mandatory prepayments: If, as of the most recent interest payment date, the sum of (i) outstanding Dollar Advances and (ii) the Dollar Equivalent (measured on the third Business Day before that date) of outstanding Euro Advances exceeds 105% of aggregate Commitments, the Borrowers must, within five Business Days of notice from the Agent, prepay enough Advances to reduce the total to no more than 100% of Commitments. If outstanding Base Rate Advances are less than the required prepayment, the excess portion is deferred to the last day of the next maturing Interest Period for Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances. All mandatory prepayments include accrued interest and, if made mid-Interest Period on Term SOFR/Eurocurrency, any amounts due under Section 8.04(c). The Agent will promptly notify the Company and the Lenders of any required prepayment.

nodes.title: Prepayments of Advances
nodes.heading: Section 2.10 Prepayments of Advances
nodes.start_phrase: The Company may, upon at least one Business Day’s notice, in the case of Base Rate Advances, and three U.S. Government Securities Business Days’ notice, in the case of Term SOFR Advances,
nodes.summary:
- Section 2.09 (Optional conversion/continuation): The Company may, with irrevocable notice to the Agent by 11:00 a.m. New York time three U.S. Government Securities Business Days in advance and subject to other provisions, convert Dollar-denominated Advances between Base Rate and Term SOFR or continue existing Advances. Term SOFR to Base Rate conversions only on the last day of the applicable Interest Period; Base Rate to Term SOFR conversions must meet the Borrowing Minimum; and no conversion may create more separate Borrowings than allowed. Notices must state the effective date, the Advances affected, and, if converting to Term SOFR, the initial Interest Period.
- Section 2.10 (Prepayments):
  - Optional: The Company may prepay with at least one Business Day’s notice for Base Rate Advances and three U.S. Government Securities Business Days’ notice for Term SOFR Advances, paying accrued interest. Partial prepayments must be at least the Borrowing Minimum or a Borrowing Multiple. Prepayment of Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances may require breakage/compensation under Section 8.04(c).
  - Mandatory: If, as of the most recent interest payment date, total Dollar Advances plus the Dollar equivalent of Euro Advances exceed 105% of aggregate Commitments, the Borrowers must prepay within five Business Days after notice to reduce to 100%, paying accrued interest and, if not on an Interest Period end date for Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Advances, any Section 8.04(c) amounts. If outstanding Base Rate Advances are less than the required prepayment, the excess is deferred to the next Interest Period end date for Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Advances. The Agent performs the calculations at each Notice of Borrowing and each interest payment date and notifies the Company and Lenders.
- Section 2.11 (Increased costs): If changes in law/regulation or compliance with applicable guidelines (including Basel III/Dodd-Frank-related measures) materially increase a Lender’s cost to make, fund, or maintain Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Advances, or increase required capital/liquidity allocable to the facility, the Company must pay additional amounts to compensate the Lender. Lender certificates are conclusive absent manifest error, must provide reasonable detail, and certify consistent treatment with similarly situated customers without disclosing confidential information.

nodes.title: Increased Costs
nodes.heading: Section 2.11 Increased Costs
nodes.start_phrase: If, due to either (i) the introduction of or any change in any law or regulation or in the interpretation or administration of any law or regulation by any governmental authority charged with the interpretation or administration thereof or (ii) the compliance with any guideline or request from any central bank or other governmental authority that would be complied with generally by similarly situated banks acting reasonably (whether or not having the force of law and for the avoidance of doubt, including any changes resulting from requests, rules, guidelines or directives concerning capital adequacy or liquidity issued after the date hereof in connection with the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act or promulgated after the date hereof by the Bank for International Settlements, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (or any successor or similar authority) or the United States or foreign regulatory authorities, in each case pursuant to Basel III), there shall be any increase in the cost to any Lender of agreeing to make or making, funding or maintaining Term SOFR Advances or Eurocurrency Rate Advances (except any reserve requirement contemplated by Section 2.11(b) other than as set forth below) by an amount deemed by such Lender to be material, then the Company shall from time to time, upon demand by such Lender (with a copy of such demand to the Agent), pay to the Agent for the account of such Lender additional amounts sufficient to compensate such Lender for such increased cost.
nodes.summary:
- Agent’s calculation and notice duties: On each Notice of Borrowing date and each interest payment date, the Agent must calculate total Dollar exposure by adding (A) all Dollar-denominated Advances and (B) the Dollar Equivalent of all Eurocurrency Rate Advances using the rate from the third Business Day prior to the calculation date. The Agent must promptly notify the Company and Lenders—no later than 30 days—of any prepayment required in connection with an interest payment date under Section 2.10(b).

- Increased Costs (Section 2.11):
  - Cost of funding/maintaining advances: If changes in law, regulation, interpretation, or compliance with governmental/central bank guidelines (including those stemming from Dodd-Frank and Basel III) materially increase a Lender’s cost to make, fund, or maintain Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances (excluding reserve requirements addressed separately), the Company must pay additional amounts on demand to compensate the Lender, via the Agent. The Lender’s certificate of the amount is conclusive absent manifest error.
  - Capital and liquidity requirements: If such regulatory changes effective after the agreement date increase the capital or liquidity a Lender (or its controlling entity) must hold and such increase is allocable to this facility’s Advances or commitments, the Company must compensate the Lender via additional amounts, as requested from time to time. The Lender’s certificate—reasonably detailed and confirming consistent treatment with similarly situated customers—is conclusive absent manifest error, and need not disclose confidential or proprietary information.

nodes.title: Illegality
nodes.heading: Section 2.12 Illegality
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, if any Lender shall notify the Agent (and provide to the Company an opinion of counsel to the effect) that the introduction of or any change in or in the interpretation of any law or regulation makes it unlawful, or any central bank or other governmental authority asserts that it is unlawful, for such Lender or its Eurocurrency Lending Office to perform its obligations hereunder to make Term SOFR Advances or Eurocurrency Rate Advances or to fund or maintain Term SOFR Advances or Eurocurrency Rate Advances hereunder, (a) each Term SOFR Advance or each Eurocurrency Rate Advance, as applicable, made by such Lender will automatically, upon such demand, (i) if such Advance is a Term SOFR Advance, be Converted into a Base Rate Advance and (ii) if such Advance is a Eurocurrency Rate Advance, be exchanged into an Equivalent amount of Dollars and be Converted into a Base Rate Advance and (b) the obligation of the Lenders to make Term SOFR Advances or Eurocurrency Rate Advances, as applicable, or to Convert Advances into Term SOFR Advances shall be suspended until the Agent shall notify the Borrowers and the Lenders that the circumstances causing such suspension no longer exist.
nodes.summary:
- Illegality: If a change in law, its interpretation, or a directive from a central bank/government makes it unlawful for a Lender (or its Eurocurrency Lending Office) to make, fund, or maintain Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances, and the Lender so notifies the Agent with a supporting legal opinion, then: (a) each outstanding Term SOFR Advance is automatically converted to a Base Rate Advance; (b) each outstanding Eurocurrency Rate Advance is exchanged into an equivalent amount of Dollars and converted to a Base Rate Advance; and (c) Lenders’ obligations to make or convert into Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances are suspended until the Agent notifies that the illegality no longer exists.

- Payment mechanics: Borrowers must pay all Dollar-denominated amounts (other than for Euro-denominated Advances) to the Agent in same-day funds by 11:00 a.m. New York time on the due date, without deduction, set-off, or counterclaim (subject to Section 2.14). Euro-denominated principal, interest, and related amounts must be paid in Euros by the same time. The Agent promptly distributes payments: principal, interest, and commitment fees ratably to Lenders (subject to specified exceptions), and other amounts to the applicable Lender.

- Assignment effects: After an Assignment and Assumption is accepted and recorded, the Agent pays the assignee Lender from the effective date, and assignor/assignee handle adjustments between themselves for prior periods.

- Interest and fee calculations: Base Rate-based interest and commitment fees use a 365/366-day year; interest based on Adjusted Term SOFR, the EURIBO Rate, and the Federal Funds Rate uses a 360-day year; all on an actual day count (including the first, excluding the last). The Agent’s interest rate determinations are conclusive absent manifest error.

nodes.title: Payments and Computations; Evidence of Advances
nodes.heading: Section 2.13 Payments and Computations; Evidence of Advances
nodes.start_phrase: The Borrowers shall make each payment hereunder and under the Notes, except with respect to principal or, interest on, and other amounts relating to, Advances denominated in Euros,
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines lender/borrower rights and mechanics under a credit agreement covering illegality, payments/computations, recordkeeping, currency handling, benchmark adjustments, and tax compliance.

- Illegality (Sec. 2.12): If a change in law or its interpretation makes it unlawful for a lender to make or maintain Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances (upon notice and opinion of counsel), such advances automatically convert to Base Rate Advances (Eurocurrency advances first convert into an equivalent amount of Dollars), and lenders’ obligations to make or convert into such advances are suspended until the agent notifies that the restriction no longer applies.

- Payments and Computations; Evidence of Advances (Sec. 2.13):
  - Payment mechanics: Borrowers must pay by 11:00 a.m. New York time—USD payments in Dollars, Euro-denominated obligations in Euros—to the agent, without setoff (subject to Sec. 2.14). The agent distributes principal, interest, and fees to lenders ratably (subject to specified exceptions) and redirects payments post-assignment to the assignee with parties adjusting between themselves for pre-effective periods.
  - Interest/fee calculations: Base Rate (as defined by clause (a)) and commitment fees use a 365/366-day count; Adjusted Term SOFR, EURIBOR, and Federal Funds Rate use a 360-day count; the agent’s rate determinations are conclusive absent manifest error.
  - Business Day convention: Payments due on non-Business Days move to the next Business Day, except Term SOFR/Eurocurrency interest or principal that would roll into the next month, which pay on the preceding Business Day.
  - Payment assumption/clawback: If the agent assumes timely borrower payment and advances funds to lenders but the borrower hasn’t paid, lenders must promptly repay the agent with interest at the Federal Funds Rate (USD) or the agent’s cost of funds (EUR).
  - Evidence of debt: Lenders’ and agent’s records are conclusive absent manifest error; agent’s records control if inconsistent. Borrowers will issue Notes upon request; lenders may annotate them with advance details.
  - Currency conversion: The agent may convert funds between Dollars and Euros as needed for distributions, bears no liability for conversion outcomes or failures, and borrowers indemnify the agent and lenders for related losses/costs.
  - Benchmark administration: The agent may unilaterally implement Conforming Changes for any Benchmark and will notify the company and lenders.

- Taxes (Sec. 2.14):
  - Withholding status: Lenders and the agent represent exemption from U.S. withholding on income under this agreement due to U.S. person status, effectively connected income, or treaty relief (for lenders); the agent is a U.S. person.
  - Documentation: U.S. lenders provide IRS Form W‑9; foreign lenders provide appropriate Form W‑8 (and, if applicable, supporting certifications) to claim exemptions or reduced rates.
  - Withholding and assignments: If a foreign lender’s provided (or missing) form indicates a non-zero U.S. withholding rate when it becomes a party, the borrower may withhold at that rate, and such amounts are excluded from “Taxes” for gross-up purposes. If the assignor previously had gross-up rights for U.S. withholding at the assignment date, those rights carry to that extent; otherwise, borrower obligations are not increased by assignments, except for Taxes imposed due to a post-assignment Change in Law.

nodes.title: Taxes
nodes.heading: Section 2.14 Taxes
nodes.start_phrase: Each Lender is exempt from any withholding tax imposed under the laws of the United States in respect of any fees, interest or other payments to which it is entitled pursuant to this Agreement or the Notes (the “Income”) because (i) the Lender is a United States Person; (ii) the Income is effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United States within the meaning of Section 871 of the Internal Revenue Code; or (iii) the Income is eligible for an exemption by reason of a tax treaty.
nodes.summary:
- Benchmark administration: The Agent may unilaterally make and implement “Conforming Changes” related to any Benchmark’s use or administration without further consent, and must promptly notify the Company and Lenders.

- Tax status representations: Each Lender represents it is exempt from U.S. withholding on “Income” (fees/interest/other payments) because it is a U.S. person, has effectively connected income, or qualifies under a treaty; the Agent is a U.S. person and exempt.

- Tax documentation:
  - U.S. Lenders provide Form W‑9 upon joining and as requested.
  - Foreign Lenders provide appropriate IRS Forms W‑8 (and any required owner certifications) to claim exemption/reduced U.S. withholding.
  - If forms indicate a non‑zero U.S. withholding rate when a Foreign Lender joins (or no form is provided), Borrowers may withhold at that rate and such amounts are excluded from “Taxes,” subject to an assignment proviso preserving certain withholding coverage if the assignor previously received it and for post‑assignment Changes in Law.
  - Borrower tax obligations are not increased by Lender assignments, except for Taxes arising from post‑assignment Changes in Law or as preserved by the proviso.

- Gross‑up and indemnity:
  - Payments by Borrowers are made free of withholding Taxes (excluding Excluded Taxes). If withholding is required, Borrowers gross‑up so Lenders receive the amount as if no withholding, make the deduction, and pay the authority; furnish receipts within 30 days.
  - Lenders/Agent will provide reasonable documentation to help minimize deductions. If a Lender/Agent must pay Taxes directly due to a Borrower’s inability/failure, the Company will indemnify them without duplication.

- Limitations on gross‑up: No gross‑up/indemnity for U.S. federal withholding except where caused by a Change in Law after a Lender joins or where Taxes arise solely due to the 2.14(b) assignment proviso.

- Other Taxes: The Company pays and indemnifies for stamp, documentary, excise, or similar non‑income taxes arising from the loan documents. Upon request and at Company expense, Lenders will use reasonable efforts to change their lending office to avoid/reduce such Other Taxes without incurring material legal/regulatory burdens.

- Cooperation and compliance:
  - Lenders will cooperate by providing forms to substantiate exemptions/reductions from foreign withholding.
  - A Lender that fails to provide required forms under (b) or (f) (absent an unduly burdensome Change in Law) is not entitled to indemnification under 2.14.
  - Upon a Change in Law or imposition of Taxes, Lenders will use reasonable efforts, at the Company’s request/expense, to change their lending office to avoid/reduce Taxes without material burden.

- Consistency certification: Any Lender request for payment under 2.14 must certify that its claim is generally consistent with its treatment of similarly situated customers, without disclosing confidential/proprietary information.

- Tax refunds: If a Lender may claim or receives a refund for Taxes/Other Taxes indemnified or grossed‑up by a Borrower, it will notify, seek the refund upon Company request at Company expense, and remit the refunded amount (plus interest, net of expenses/FX effects) to the Borrower; the Borrower must repay if the refund is later clawed back. Lenders need not disclose tax returns or confidential tax information.

- FATCA: Lenders must provide documentation needed for Borrowers/Agent to comply with FATCA and determine withholding, with FATCA deemed to include future amendments.

- Exclusivity: Section 2.14 exclusively governs when the Company or its Subsidiaries bear any Lender tax costs, broadly defined to include taxes, fees, and related interest/penalties.

nodes.title: Sharing of Payments, Etc.
nodes.heading: Section 2.15 Sharing of Payments, Etc.
nodes.start_phrase: If any Lender shall obtain any payment (whether voluntary, involuntary, through the exercise of any right of set-off, or otherwise) on account of the Advances owing to it (other than pursuant to Section 2.05(b), 2.06(b), 2.11, 2.14, 8.04(c) or 8.07) in excess of its ratable share thereof, such Lender shall forthwith purchase from the other Lenders such participations in the Advances owing to them as shall be necessary to cause such purchasing Lender to share the excess payment ratably with each of them; provided, however, that if all or any portion of such excess payment is thereafter recovered from such purchasing Lender, such purchase from each Lender shall be rescinded and such Lender shall repay to the purchasing Lender the purchase price to the extent of such recovery together with an amount equal to such Lender’s ratable share (according to the proportion of (i) the amount of such Lender’s required repayment to (ii) the total amount so recovered from the purchasing Lender) of any interest or other amount paid or payable by the purchasing Lender in respect of the total amount so recovered.
nodes.summary:
- Section 2.15 (Sharing of Payments): Requires pro rata sharing among Lenders if any Lender receives payments in excess of its ratable share, achieved via participations purchased from other Lenders; includes clawback/rescission if such excess is later recovered, with associated interest/amounts; Borrowers consent to Lenders’ full payment rights (including set-off) regarding such participations.

- Section 2.16 (Use of Proceeds): Advances may be used for general corporate purposes (e.g., working capital, capital investments, acquisitions); prohibits knowing use of proceeds for activities involving SDN-listed parties or Sanctioned Countries, unless licensed by OFAC or otherwise permitted under U.S. law.

- Section 2.17 (Borrowings by Borrowing Subsidiaries): The Company can designate Subsidiaries as Borrowers with at least 10 Business Days’ notice via a Designation Letter (Exhibit D); Agent will notify Lenders; the Company must provide KYC/Beneficial Ownership documentation as requested; upon designation, the Subsidiary becomes a Borrowing Subsidiary authorized to borrow Advances under the Agreement’s terms.

nodes.title: Use of Proceeds
nodes.heading: Section 2.16 Use of Proceeds
nodes.start_phrase: The proceeds of the Advances shall be available (and the Company agrees that such proceeds shall be used) for general corporate purposes of the Company and its Subsidiaries, including but not limited to working capital, capital investments and acquisitions.
nodes.summary:
- Payment sharing among Lenders: If any Lender receives a payment on its Advances in excess of its pro rata share (except as allowed under specified sections), it must purchase participations from other Lenders to equalize payments. If such excess is later recovered (clawed back), the purchases are unwound and reimbursements (including a ratable share of interest/amounts paid by the purchasing Lender) are made. Borrowers agree that a Lender holding such participations may exercise payment and set-off rights as if it were a direct creditor for the participation amount.
- Use of proceeds: Advances may be used for general corporate purposes of the Company and its Subsidiaries, including working capital, capital investments, and acquisitions. Proceeds may not be knowingly used to fund activities with SDN-listed persons or in/with governments of Sanctioned Countries, unless licensed by OFAC or otherwise permitted under U.S. law.
- Borrowings by Subsidiaries: The Company may designate Subsidiaries as Borrowers with at least 10 Business Days’ notice (for post-Effective Date designations) by delivering a Designation Letter (Exhibit D) executed by the Company and the Subsidiary. The Agent will notify Lenders. If the designation triggers KYC/Beneficial Ownership or similar requirements, the Company must promptly provide requested documentation. Once designated, the Subsidiary becomes a Borrowing Subsidiary entitled to borrow Advances under the Agreement’s terms.

nodes.title: Borrowings by Borrowing Subsidiaries
nodes.heading: Section 2.17 Borrowings by Borrowing Subsidiaries
nodes.start_phrase: The Company may, at any time or from time to time upon not less than 10 Business Days’ notice in the case of any Subsidiary so designated after the Effective Date, designate one or more Subsidiaries as Borrowers hereunder by furnishing to the Agent a letter (a “Designation Letter”) in duplicate, in substantially the form of Exhibit D, duly completed and executed by the Company and such Subsidiary.
nodes.summary:
- Payment sharing among Lenders (Section 2.15): If a Lender receives a payment on Advances exceeding its pro rata share (other than specified exceptions), it must purchase participations from other Lenders to equalize payments ratably. If any of that excess is later clawed back, the purchases are unwound proportionally and the purchasing Lender is reimbursed for its share of related interest/amounts. Borrowers agree that a Lender holding such participations may exercise full payment rights, including set-off, as if a direct creditor for the participated amount.

- Use of proceeds (Section 2.16): Advance proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes of the Company and its Subsidiaries (e.g., working capital, capex, acquisitions). Borrowers shall not knowingly use proceeds for activities involving parties on the U.S. SDN List or in/with governments of Sanctioned Countries, except if licensed by OFAC or otherwise permitted under U.S. law.

- Borrowing by Subsidiaries (Section 2.17):
  - Designation process: The Company may designate Subsidiaries as Borrowers with at least 10 Business Days’ notice (post-Effective Date) by delivering a Designation Letter. The Agent/Lenders may require KYC/Beneficial Ownership documentation before effectiveness. Once designated, the Subsidiary may borrow under the Agreement.
  - Non-U.S. Subsidiaries: A Lender may satisfy its Commitment via an Affiliate or branch acting as the Lender for such Subsidiary.
  - Protesting Lenders: If a Lender cannot legally lend to a non-U.S. designated Borrowing Subsidiary (directly or via Affiliate/branch), it must notify within five Business Days. The Company must then either (A) terminate that Lender’s Commitments with full payoff (via assignment or payment) by the effective date, or (B) cancel the designation request.
  - Termination of Borrowing Subsidiary status: After all principal and interest owed by a Borrowing Subsidiary are paid, the Company may terminate its status via a Termination Letter; effectiveness occurs upon Agent’s receipt, with Notes returned upon full payment. Outstanding obligations (e.g., indemnities/expenses) and the Company’s related Article IX obligations survive. If termination follows a sale/transfer of the Subsidiary and the Company so certifies, the Subsidiary is released from obligations and the Company assumes them as primary obligor, subject to payment of principal and interest.

nodes.title: Benchmark Replacement Setting
nodes.heading: Section 2.18 Benchmark Replacement Setting
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein or in any other Loan Document, if a Benchmark Transition Event and its related Benchmark Replacement Date have occurred prior to any setting of any Benchmark, then (x) if a Benchmark Replacement is determined in accordance with clause (a) of the definition of “Benchmark Replacement” for such Benchmark Replacement Date, such Benchmark Replacement will replace such Benchmark for all purposes hereunder and under any Loan Document in respect of such Benchmark setting and subsequent Benchmark settings without any amendment to, or further action or consent of any other party to, this Agreement or any other Loan Document and the definition of “Adjusted Term SOFR” shall be deemed modified to delete clause (b) for any calculation of Term SOFR and (y) if a Benchmark Replacement is determined in accordance with clause (b) of the definition of “Benchmark Replacement” for such Benchmark Replacement Date, such Benchmark Replacement will replace such Benchmark for all purposes hereunder and under any Loan Document in respect of any Benchmark setting at or after 5:00 p.m. (New York City time) on the fifth Business Day after the date notice of such Benchmark Replacement is provided to the Lenders without any amendment to, or further action or consent of any other party to, this Agreement or any other Loan Document so long as the Agent has not received, by such time, written notice of objection to such Benchmark Replacement from Lenders comprising the Required Lenders.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how and when the interest rate Benchmark in the loan agreement is replaced following a Benchmark Transition Event and the related Benchmark Replacement Date.
- Replacement mechanics:
  - If the replacement is determined under clause (a) of “Benchmark Replacement,” it takes effect immediately for all settings without further consent, and the Adjusted Term SOFR definition is deemed modified to delete clause (b).
  - If determined under clause (b), it becomes effective after 5 Business Days’ notice unless Required Lenders object; if Daily Simple SOFR is the replacement, interest is paid monthly.
- Grants the Agent authority to make and implement Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes unilaterally, effective without further consents.
- Requires the Agent to notify the Company and Lenders of: Benchmark Replacement Dates and the selected replacement, effectiveness of Conforming Changes, tenor removals/reinstatements, and start/end of any Benchmark Unavailability Period; Agent/Lender determinations are binding absent manifest error and may be made in sole discretion as permitted.
- Addresses unavailability/non-representativeness of specific tenors for term Benchmarks (e.g., Term SOFR Reference Rate or EURIBO): Agent may remove such tenors from the Interest Period definition and may later reinstate them if they reappear or become representative.
- Sets Borrower rights and automatic outcomes during a Benchmark Unavailability Period:
  - Borrowers may revoke pending requests for affected Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate borrowings/conversions/continuations.
  - If not revoked: affected Term SOFR requests convert to Base Rate; affected Eurocurrency Rate requests are ineffective.
  - Outstanding affected Term SOFR Advances convert to Base Rate at period end; affected Eurocurrency Rate Advances convert to Dollar Base Rate (Dollar Equivalent) or must be prepaid at period end (conversion is deemed if no timely election).
  - Accrued interest and any breakage amounts are payable; Base Rate determinations exclude the unavailable Benchmark component/tenor.
- Defines key terms used in the section:
  - Available Currency: Dollars or Euros.
  - Available Tenor: any then-usable tenor for the Benchmark not removed under this section.
  - Benchmark: initially the Relevant Rate, replaced by the applicable Benchmark Replacement upon a Transition Event.
  - Benchmark Replacement waterfall: (a) for Term SOFR Advances, Daily Simple SOFR + 0.10%; (b) Agent/Company-selected alternative reflecting Relevant Governmental Body recommendations or prevailing market convention plus the Benchmark Replacement Adjustment; for Euro-denominated Advances, only clause (b) applies; subject to a 0.00% Floor.
  - Benchmark Replacement Adjustment: spread/method selected by Agent and Company consistent with official recommendations or market convention.
  - Benchmark Replacement Date: the earliest of specified cessation or non-representativeness triggers tied to public statements by administrators/supervisors.
  - Benchmark Transition Event: defined cessation/no-successor or supervisor statements of cessation or non-representativeness across all Available Tenors.
  - Benchmark Unavailability Period: the period after a Replacement Date until a replacement is implemented.
  - Floor: 0.00%.
  - Relevant Governmental Body: defined bodies for USD and non-USD currencies (e.g., Federal Reserve/NY Fed/endorsed committees; relevant central banks/FSB).
  - Relevant Rate: Term SOFR Reference Rate for Term SOFR Advances; EURIBO Rate for Eurocurrency Rate Advances.
  - Unadjusted Benchmark Replacement: the selected replacement rate before adding the Adjustment.

nodes.title: Defaulting Lenders
nodes.heading: Section 2.19 Defaulting Lenders
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, if any Lender becomes a Defaulting Lender, then, until such time as such Lender is no longer a Defaulting Lender, to the extent permitted by applicable law:
nodes.summary:
- Section 2.19 (Defaulting Lenders):
  - Voting/consent limitations: A Defaulting Lender’s right to approve amendments, waivers, or consents is restricted per the “Required Lenders” definition.
  - Payment waterfall for funds otherwise payable to a Defaulting Lender: 
    1) first to amounts owed by the Defaulting Lender to the Agent; 
    2) second, at the Company’s request (if no Default), to fund missed portions of Advances; 
    3) third, if determined by the Agent and Company, to a deposit account to cover potential future funding obligations; 
    4) fourth, if no Default, to satisfy any court judgment in favor of the Company arising from the Defaulting Lender’s breach; 
    5) fifth, to the Defaulting Lender or as a court directs. 
    - Principal payments on Advances not fully funded by the Defaulting Lender (when Section 3.02 conditions were met/waived) go first to Non-Defaulting Lenders pro rata until Advances are held pro rata by all Lenders.
    - Such applications are deemed paid to and redirected by the Defaulting Lender; all Lenders irrevocably consent.
  - Commitment Fees: A Defaulting Lender is not entitled to Commitment Fees during its defaulting period, and the Company need not pay them.
  - Cure: Upon written agreement by the Company and Agent that a Lender is cured, the Agent notifies parties; the Lender must purchase at par portions of outstanding Advances or take actions to restore pro rata holdings per Commitments. No retroactive fee/payment adjustments; no waiver/release of prior claims unless expressly agreed.

- Article III (Conditions to Effectiveness and Lending), Section 3.01 (Conditions Precedent to Effectiveness):
  - The Agreement becomes effective on the “Effective Date” when all conditions are met, including:
    - No Material Adverse Change since December 31, 2022 that has not been publicly disclosed.
    - No pending or, to the Company’s knowledge, threatened actions likely to have a Material Adverse Effect not previously disclosed, or to affect the legality, validity, enforceability of the Agreement/Notes or consummation of the transactions.
    - All required governmental and third‑party consents/approvals obtained, with no unacceptable conditions, and remaining in effect.
    - Payment by the Company of all reasonable accrued fees/expenses of the Agent, Syndication Agents, Lead Arrangers, and Lenders (including one counsel to the Agent).
    - Delivery of an officer’s certificate (for each Lender) stating Section 4.01 representations/warranties are true on the Effective Date and no Default is continuing.
    - Delivery of Notes to each Lender that requested them at least three Business Days prior to the Effective Date.

nodes.title: Conditions Precedent to Effectiveness
nodes.heading: Section 3.01 Conditions Precedent to Effectiveness
nodes.start_phrase: This Agreement shall become effective on and as of the first date (the “Effective Date”) on which the following conditions precedent have been satisfied:
nodes.summary:
- Defaulting Lender cure mechanics: If the Company and Agent agree a Lender has cured its defaulting status, the Agent notifies parties and the Lender must purchase at par portions of other Lenders’ outstanding advances or take other actions so advances are held pro rata by Commitments. The Lender then ceases to be “Defaulting,” with no retroactive fee or payment adjustments and no waiver of prior claims unless expressly agreed.

- Article III—Conditions to Effectiveness (Effective Date):
  - No undisclosed Material Adverse Change since December 31, 2022.
  - No pending/threatened actions likely to cause a Material Adverse Effect (undisclosed) or impair the legality/enforceability of the agreement/notes or consummation of the transactions.
  - All required governmental/third‑party consents obtained on acceptable terms.
  - Payment of reasonable accrued fees/expenses of the Agent, Syndication Agents, Lead Arrangers, Lenders (including Agent’s counsel).
  - Officer’s certificate confirming Section 4.01 representations are true and no Default exists.
  - Required deliverables: requested Notes; certified board resolutions and corporate documents (articles/bylaws); secretary’s certificate with authorized signatories; favorable legal opinions; executed agreement; requested KYC/AML documentation (including PATRIOT Act) and Beneficial Ownership Certifications within specified pre‑closing timeframes.
  - Evidence of termination of commitments and full payoff under existing credit agreements; Lenders party to those agreements waive prior notice of termination.

- Conditions to Each Borrowing (post‑effectiveness):
  - Effective Date has occurred.
  - On the borrowing date, by delivering a Notice of Borrowing and accepting proceeds, the Company/Borrower represent that specified Section 4.01 representations (with stated carve‑outs) are true before and after giving effect to the borrowing, and that no Default exists or would result from the borrowing or use of proceeds.

nodes.title: Conditions Precedent to Each Borrowing
nodes.heading: Section 3.02 Conditions Precedent to Each Borrowing
nodes.start_phrase: The obligation of each Lender to make an Advance on the occasion of each Borrowing shall be subject to the conditions precedent that the Effective Date shall have occurred and on the date of such Borrowing:
nodes.summary:
- Closing conditions for the Effective Date:
  - Delivery of certified board resolutions approving the agreement and notes, and other requisite corporate/governmental approvals, including articles of incorporation and bylaws.
  - Secretary’s certificate identifying authorized signatories.
  - Favorable legal opinions for the Company.
  - Fully executed copies of the agreement.
  - KYC/AML documentation (including PATRIOT Act) if requested in advance.
  - Beneficial Ownership Certifications for any Borrower qualifying as a “legal entity customer.”
  - Evidence of termination of commitments and full payoff under existing credit agreements; lenders under those agreements waive prior notice of termination.

- Conditions precedent to each borrowing:
  - Effective Date has occurred.
  - Bring-down of representations and warranties (with limited carve-outs) true as of borrowing date; no Default results from the borrowing.
  - Agent receives Notice of Borrowing; for a first borrowing by any Borrowing Subsidiary, delivery of requested notes, corporate documents, resolutions, and legal opinions.

- Conditions for Term Loan Conversion:
  - No Default on the Term Loan Election date and the Term Loan Conversion Date.
  - Payment of a 0.50% fee on aggregate principal amount of Advances outstanding on the Term Loan Conversion Date.

- Determination of satisfaction of closing conditions:
  - Lenders are deemed to have approved required documents unless the Agent receives a written objection before the Effective Date; Agent will notify parties of the Effective Date.

- Representations and warranties of the Company:
  - Duly organized and validly existing North Carolina corporation.
  - Due authorization and corporate power to execute, deliver, and perform the agreement and notes; such actions do not contravene corporate charter/bylaws or, in any material respect, applicable law or material contractual restrictions.

nodes.title: Conditions Precedent to Term Loan Conversion Date
nodes.heading: Section 3.03 Conditions Precedent to Term Loan Conversion Date
nodes.start_phrase: The Term Loan Election shall be subject to the conditions precedent that on the date of the Term Loan Election and on the Term Loan Conversion Date:
nodes.summary:
- Conditions precedent to borrowings by a Borrowing Subsidiary: the Agent must receive a Notice of Borrowing and, for the first such borrowing, any requested Notes (per Section 2.13(e)), along with required corporate documents, resolutions, and legal opinions.
- Conditions precedent to a Term Loan Election and Term Loan Conversion Date: (i) no Default has occurred, is continuing, or would result from the election; and (ii) the Agent must receive, for the Lenders, a fee equal to 0.50% of the aggregate principal amount of Advances outstanding on the Conversion Date.
- Determination of satisfaction of initial conditions (Section 3.01): each Lender is deemed to have approved required documents unless the Agent receives a written objection before the proposed Effective Date; the Agent will promptly notify parties of the Effective Date.
- Company representations and warranties: the Company is duly organized and validly existing under North Carolina law; its execution, delivery, and performance of the agreement and any Notes are duly authorized, within corporate powers, and do not materially contravene its charter/bylaws, applicable law, or any material contractual restrictions.

nodes.title: Determinations Under Section 3.01
nodes.heading: Section 3.04 Determinations Under Section 3.01
nodes.start_phrase: For purposes of determining compliance with the conditions specified in Section 3.01, each Lender shall be deemed to have consented to, approved or accepted or to be satisfied with each document or other matter required thereunder to be consented to or approved by or acceptable or satisfactory to the Lenders unless an officer of the Agent responsible for the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall have received written notice from such Lender prior to the proposed Effective Date, as notified by the Company to the Lenders, specifying its objection thereto.
nodes.summary:
- Sets conditions for initial Borrowing by a Borrowing Subsidiary: Agent must receive a Notice of Borrowing and, for the first such borrowing, requested Notes, corporate documents, resolutions, and legal opinions reasonably required by the Agent.
- Establishes conditions precedent to a Term Loan Election and the Term Loan Conversion Date: (a) no Default is continuing or would result from the election, and (b) payment to the Agent, for the Lenders, of a 0.50% fee on the aggregate principal amount of Advances outstanding on the Conversion Date.
- Provides a deemed-consent mechanism for Lender approvals under Section 3.01: Lenders are deemed to consent/approve unless the Agent receives a written objection from a Lender before the Effective Date; the Agent must promptly notify parties of the Effective Date.
- States key Company representations and warranties: the Company is duly organized and validly existing under North Carolina law; has authority and proper corporate authorization to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement and any Notes; and such actions do not materially contravene its charter documents, applicable law, or any material contractual restrictions.

nodes.title: Representations and Warranties of the Company
nodes.heading: Section 4.01 Representations and Warranties of the Company
nodes.start_phrase: The Company represents and warrants as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Conditions precedent for a Borrowing Subsidiary’s borrowing: Agent must receive a Notice of Borrowing; for the first borrowing by a Borrowing Subsidiary, Agent must also receive requested Notes (per Section 2.13(e)), and reasonably required corporate documents, resolutions, and legal opinions.
- Conditions to Term Loan Election and Term Loan Conversion Date: (a) no Default exists or would result; (b) Agent receives a fee for the Lenders equal to 0.50% of the aggregate principal amount of Advances outstanding on the Conversion Date.
