- Determinations under Section 3.01: Lenders are deemed to have approved required documents unless the Agent receives a written objection before the Effective Date; Agent will promptly notify Lenders and the Company of the Effective Date.
- Representations and Warranties of the Company: (a) duly organized and validly existing in North Carolina; (b) due authorization, no material contravention of organizational documents, law, or material contracts; (c) required approvals obtained; (d) agreement and notes are duly executed, delivered, and enforceable; (e) audited GAAP financials as of Dec 31, 2022 (KPMG) fairly present results; no undisclosed Material Adverse Change since then; (f) no pending/threatened actions likely to cause a Material Adverse Effect or impair legality/enforceability; (g) no use of proceeds to purchase/carry margin stock in violation of Regulation U; (h) not an investment company; (i) no Borrower is on the SDN List or in a Sanctioned Country; (j) Beneficial Ownership Certification is accurate as of the Effective Date.
- Affirmative Covenants: (a) comply with applicable laws (including ERISA, Environmental, and Anti-Corruption Laws) and maintain compliance policies; (b) timely pay taxes and claims subject to good-faith contest and materiality/Lien limitations; (c) preserve corporate existence and, for Material Subsidiaries, preserve rights and franchises subject to permitted mergers and board determinations of no material disadvantage; (d) reporting: deliver to the Agent (i) quarterly consolidated financials within 5 days after SEC filing due date (10-Q), CFO-certified; and (ii) annual audited consolidated financials within 15 days after SEC filing due date (10-K), with KPMG or other independent auditors; SEC filings on sec.gov satisfy delivery.

nodes.title: Affirmative Covenants.
nodes.heading: Section 5.01 Affirmative Covenants.
nodes.start_phrase: So long as any Advance shall remain unpaid or any Lender shall have any Commitment hereunder, the Company will:
nodes.summary:
- Article V sets out the Company’s covenants while any Advances are outstanding or any Lender commitments remain.

- Affirmative covenants (Section 5.01):
  - Compliance with laws: Company and Subsidiaries will comply in all material respects with applicable laws, including ERISA, Environmental Laws, and Anti-Corruption Laws, and maintain/enforce policies to ensure such compliance, except where noncompliance would not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.
  - Payment of taxes and claims: Pay and discharge taxes, assessments, governmental charges, and claims before delinquency unless being contested in good faith with appropriate reserves; no requirement to pay contested items unless a Lien attaches and becomes enforceable and the failure to pay would likely have a Material Adverse Effect.
  - Preservation of existence and rights: Maintain corporate existence (subject to permitted mergers) and preserve rights and franchises of the Company and its Material Subsidiaries, except where the governing body determines loss is not materially disadvantageous.
  - Reporting requirements to the Agent:
    - Quarterly financials (Form 10-Q equivalent) within 5 days after SEC filing deadline.
    - Annual audited financials (Form 10-K equivalent) within 15 days after SEC filing deadline.
    - Default notices within 5 days of occurrence, with details and remediation steps.
    - Copies of shareholder reports, proxy solicitations, and Forms 8-K when filed/sent.
    - Provide KYC/anti–money laundering information upon request.
    - Delivery deemed satisfied by posting on the Company’s or SEC website accessible without charge.

- Negative covenants (Section 5.02):
  - Secured Debt/ Liens: No Debt secured by Liens on Principal Property, or on stock or Debt of Restricted Subsidiaries, unless the Advances and obligations hereunder are secured equally and ratably, subject to:
    - A general basket permitting such secured Debt up to 15% of Consolidated Net Tangible Assets.
    - Permitted Liens, including: existing Liens; Liens existing when an entity becomes a Restricted Subsidiary; intercompany Liens; governmental Liens securing progress/advance payments; acquisition, construction, or purchase-money Liens (including those incurred within 120 days of acquisition/completion/operation); and extensions, renewals, or refundings of permitted Liens.

nodes.title: Negative Covenants.
nodes.heading: Section 5.02 Negative Covenants.
nodes.start_phrase: So long as any Advance shall remain unpaid or any Lender shall have any Commitment hereunder, the Company will not:
nodes.summary:
- Ongoing reporting obligations:
  - CFO must deliver, within five days of any continuing Default, a statement detailing the Default and remedial actions.
  - Prompt delivery of copies of annual reports, proxy materials sent to security holders, and Forms 8-K filed by the Company or any Subsidiary.
  - Prompt provision of information/documents requested by the Agent or any Lender for “know your customer” and anti–money laundering compliance (PATRIOT Act and similar laws).
  - Reports/financial statements are deemed delivered when posted on the Company’s website, the SEC’s website, or another designated free-access site.

- Negative covenants (while any Advances are outstanding or Commitments exist):
  - Secured Debt: Restrictions on creating or permitting Liens on Principal Property, stock or Debt of Restricted Subsidiaries, unless the Advances and other obligations are equally and ratably secured; exception for a basket up to 15% of Consolidated Net Tangible Assets and specific permitted Liens (pre-existing Liens; Liens existing when an entity becomes a Restricted Subsidiary; intra-group Liens; governmental progress-payment Liens; acquisition/construction/purchase-money Liens within defined timing; and related extensions/renewals/refundings).
  - Limitation on securing more than 65% of the stock or assets of any controlled foreign corporation unless other Company/Restricted Subsidiary Debt is similarly secured.
  - Mergers/Consolidations/Asset Transfers: Prohibited unless the Company remains the survivor or the successor meets ratings thresholds (A-/A3), is a U.S. entity, and assumes obligations to the Agent’s satisfaction, and no Default exists before/after the transaction. Carve-out for reincorporation mergers with Affiliates into qualifying jurisdictions. KYC information must be provided to Lenders upon request in such cases.

- Events of Default (partial list provided):
  - Payment default: failure by any Borrower to pay principal, interest, or other amounts within five Business Days of due date.
  - Misrepresentation: any material inaccuracy when made in representations or warranties by the Company or any Borrower (including by a Borrowing Subsidiary via a Designation Letter).

nodes.title: Events of Default.
nodes.heading: Section 6.01 Events of Default.
nodes.start_phrase: If any of the following events (“Events of Default”) shall occur and be continuing:
nodes.summary:
- Limitation on collateral involving foreign subsidiaries: Neither the Company nor any Restricted Subsidiary must secure the facility with more than 65% of the voting or value of stock (or any assets) of a “controlled foreign corporation” (IRC §957(a)), unless other Company/Restricted Subsidiary Debt is similarly secured.

- Mergers, consolidations, and asset transfers: Prohibited unless:
  - The Company remains the surviving entity, or the successor/acquirer:
    - Is a U.S./D.C. corporation,
    - Has long-term debt ratings of at least A- (S&P) and A3 (Moody’s),
    - Expressly assumes this Agreement to the Agent’s reasonable satisfaction; and
  - No Default exists immediately before and after the transaction.
  - Exception for mergers with an Affiliate solely for reincorporation in a permitted U.S./D.C. jurisdiction.
  - KYC: In any permitted merger/consolidation, the Company must provide information reasonably requested by Lenders to satisfy “know your customer” and similar requirements.

- Events of Default (EoD):
  - Payment default: Failure by any Borrower to pay principal, interest, or any other amount under the Agreement/Notes within 5 Business Days of due date.
  - Misrepresentation: Any material inaccuracy in representations or warranties when made by the Company or any Borrower (including in a Designation Letter).
  - Covenant defaults:
    - Immediate EoD for breaches of Sections 5.01(d) or 5.02.
    - Other breaches if not cured within 30 days after written notice from the Agent or any Lender.
  - Cross-default/cross-acceleration: Failures or accelerations relating to Company or Material Subsidiary Debt (excluding this facility) aggregating at least $500,000,000, including required prepayments/redemptions/defeasance or required offers to do so.
  - Insolvency/bankruptcy events: Inability to pay debts, assignments for benefit of creditors, bankruptcy/insolvency proceedings (30-day unstayed/undismissed threshold for involuntary cases), or related corporate authorizations.
  - Large judgments: Money judgments/orders over $500,000,000 with commenced enforcement or with no stay for 10 consecutive days; carve-out if fully covered by non-disputed insurance from an insurer rated at least “A” by A.M. Best.
  - ERISA: Certain Title IV ERISA events causing penalties or actions that have a Material Adverse Effect.

- Remedies upon EoD:
  - At the request/with consent of Required Lenders, the Agent may terminate Lenders’ obligations to make Advances and accelerate all obligations.
  - Automatic termination and acceleration upon an actual or deemed bankruptcy order for relief with respect to the Company.

- Agency provisions:
  - Citibank, N.A. appointed as Administrative Agent with authority to act as provided in the Loan Documents; “agent” is an administrative role, not a fiduciary duty.
  - Agent will promptly relay Company notices to Lenders.
  - The Agent, in its individual capacity, has the same rights as any Lender and may conduct business with the Company and its Affiliates without duty to account to other Lenders.

nodes.title: Appointment and Authority.
nodes.heading: Section 7.01 Appointment and Authority.
nodes.start_phrase: Each of the Lenders hereby irrevocably appoints Citibank, N.A. to act on its behalf as the Agent hereunder and under the other Loan Documents and authorizes the Agent to take such actions on its behalf and to exercise such powers as are delegated to the Agent by the terms hereof or thereof, together with such actions and powers as are reasonably incidental thereto.
nodes.summary:
- Defines an event of default tied to ERISA: any penalty, action, or condition under a Company employee benefit plan subject to ERISA Title IV that has a Material Adverse Effect.
- Upon such default, the Agent, at the request or with consent of the Required Lenders, may terminate all Lenders’ commitments to make Advances and accelerate all outstanding Advances, interest, and other amounts, with all presentment, demand, and notice waived by the Company.
- Provides for automatic termination of commitments and automatic acceleration of all amounts due upon an actual or deemed order for relief under the Federal Bankruptcy Code, without notice.
- Article VII establishes the Agent:
  - Lenders irrevocably appoint Citibank, N.A. as Agent under the Agreement and other Loan Documents, authorizing it to take actions and exercise delegated and incidental powers.
  - Clarifies the Agent’s role as administrative only, not fiduciary; provisions benefit only the Agent and Lenders, not the Borrowers as third-party beneficiaries.
  - Requires the Agent to promptly notify each Lender of notices received from the Company.
- Confirms the Agent’s rights as a Lender in its individual capacity and permits the Agent and its Affiliates to conduct other business with the Company and its Affiliates without duty to account to the Lenders.

nodes.title: Rights as a Lender.
nodes.heading: Section 7.02 Rights as a Lender.
nodes.start_phrase: The Person serving as the Agent hereunder shall have the same rights and powers in its capacity as a Lender as any other Lender and may exercise the same as though it were not the Agent, and the term “Lender” or “Lenders” shall, unless otherwise expressly indicated or unless the context otherwise requires, include the Person serving as the Agent hereunder in its individual capacity.
nodes.summary:
- Event of default: Any ERISA Title IV event, action, or condition causing penalties or actions with a Material Adverse Effect triggers remedies.
- Remedies upon default: At the request or with consent of Required Lenders, the Agent may terminate lenders’ obligations to make advances and accelerate all outstanding advances, interest, and other amounts; all notices, presentment, and protest are waived by the Company.
- Automatic bankruptcy consequences: Upon an actual or deemed order for relief under the Federal Bankruptcy Code, lender commitments automatically terminate and all obligations automatically become due without notice or presentment.
- Article VII – The Agent:
  - Section 7.01 (Appointment and Authority): Lenders irrevocably appoint Citibank, N.A. as Agent with authority under the loan documents; “agent” is an administrative role, not a fiduciary; provisions benefit only the Agent and Lenders (no third-party beneficiary rights for Borrowers); the Agent will promptly notify Lenders of Company notices.
  - Section 7.02 (Rights as a Lender): The Agent, in its individual capacity, has the same rights and powers as any Lender and “Lender” includes the Agent unless context requires otherwise; the Agent and its Affiliates may conduct other business with the Company without any duty to account to the Lenders.

nodes.title: Exculpatory Provisions.
nodes.heading: Section 7.03 Exculpatory Provisions.
nodes.start_phrase: The Agent shall not have any duties or obligations except those expressly set forth herein and in the other Loan Documents, and its duties hereunder shall be administrative in nature.
nodes.summary:
- Defines the Agent’s role as purely administrative with duties limited to those expressly stated in the Loan Documents; no fiduciary or implied duties even during a Default.
- Limits the Agent’s obligation to take discretionary actions to those expressly required and directed in writing by the Required Lenders (or other specified lender thresholds), and allows the Agent to refuse actions that could create liability or violate law/Loan Documents (including debtor relief laws and automatic stay concerns).
- Disclaims any duty to disclose, or liability for failing to disclose, information about the Company or its Affiliates obtained by the Agent or its Affiliates in any capacity.
- Shields the Agent from liability for actions taken at the direction or with the consent of the Required Lenders, or for actions/inactions absent gross negligence, bad faith, or willful misconduct as finally determined by a court; the Agent is deemed unaware of Defaults unless given written notice by the Company or a Lender.
- States the Agent has no responsibility to verify statements, documents, covenant performance, occurrence of Defaults, validity/enforceability of documents, or satisfaction of conditions (other than confirming receipt of items expressly required to be delivered to it).
- Authorizes the Agent to rely on written, electronic, oral, or telephonic communications believed genuine and from proper persons without liability; may presume lender satisfaction of conditions to Advances unless notified otherwise before funding.
- Permits the Agent to consult counsel (including Company’s counsel), accountants, and experts, and protects the Agent when acting in accordance with their advice.

nodes.title: Reliance by Agent.
nodes.heading: Section 7.04 Reliance by Agent.
nodes.start_phrase: The Agent shall be entitled to rely upon, and shall not incur any liability for relying upon, any notice, request, certificate, consent, statement, instrument, document or other writing (including any electronic message, Internet or intranet website posting or other distribution) believed by it to be genuine and to have been signed, sent or otherwise authenticated by the proper Person.
nodes.summary:
- The Agent’s role is purely administrative with duties limited to those expressly stated in the Loan Documents; it has no fiduciary or implied duties, even during a Default.
- The Agent need not take discretionary actions unless expressly required and directed in writing by the Required Lenders (or another specified lender threshold), and it is not required to act if doing so could create liability or conflict with law or the Loan Documents (including respecting bankruptcy automatic stay and avoiding forfeiture of a Defaulting Lender’s property).
- The Agent has no duty to disclose information about the Company or its Affiliates obtained in any capacity unless expressly required.
- The Agent is not liable for actions taken or omitted with the consent or at the request of the Required Lenders, or absent its own gross negligence, bad faith, or willful misconduct (as finally determined by a court). It is deemed unaware of Defaults unless it receives written notice from the Company or a Lender.
- The Agent has no responsibility to verify statements, warranties, document contents, covenant performance, Default occurrence, document validity/enforceability, or satisfaction of conditions precedent, beyond confirming receipt of items expressly required to be delivered to it.
- The Agent may rely, without liability, on any written or electronic communication believed genuine and properly authorized, as well as oral or telephone statements believed to be from the proper person.
- For conditions to Advances that must satisfy a Lender, the Agent may presume satisfaction unless that Lender notifies otherwise before the Advance.
- The Agent may consult counsel (including Company’s counsel), accountants, and experts, and is not liable for actions taken or omitted in accordance with their advice.

nodes.title: Indemnification.
nodes.heading: Section 7.05 Indemnification.
nodes.start_phrase: The Lenders agree to indemnify the Agent (to the extent not reimbursed by the Company), ratably according to the respective outstanding principal amounts of the Advances then made by each of them (or if no Advances are at the time outstanding, ratably according to the respective amounts of their Commitments), from and against any and all liabilities, obligations, losses, damages, penalties, actions, judgments, suits, costs, expenses or disbursements of any kind or nature whatsoever that may be imposed on, incurred by, or asserted against the Agent in any way relating to or arising out of this Agreement or any action taken or omitted by the Agent under this Agreement; provided that no Lender shall be liable for any portion of such liabilities, obligations, losses, damages, penalties, actions, judgments, suits, costs, expenses or disbursements resulting from the Agent’s gross negligence, willful misconduct or material breach of this Agreement in bad faith.
nodes.summary:
- Indemnification of Agent by Lenders: Lenders must indemnify the Agent, pro rata by outstanding Advances (or by Commitments if no Advances are outstanding), for liabilities, losses, costs, and expenses arising from the Agreement or the Agent’s actions/omissions under it, except to the extent caused by the Agent’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad-faith material breach. Lenders must also promptly reimburse the Agent, pro rata, for out-of-pocket expenses (including legal fees) related to the preparation, execution, delivery, administration, amendment, enforcement, or related legal advice under the Agreement when not reimbursed by the Company.
- Delegation of duties: The Agent may delegate duties and exercise rights through approved sub-agents and act through its and their Related Parties. Exculpatory protections extend to sub-agents and Related Parties. The Agent is not liable for a sub-agent’s negligence or misconduct unless a final, non-appealable judgment finds the Agent was grossly negligent or engaged in willful misconduct in selecting the sub-agent.
- Resignation and removal of Agent: 
  - Resignation: The Agent may resign by notice. Required Lenders, with Company approval, appoint a qualified successor (U.S. bank or affiliate). If no successor accepts within 30 days (or earlier agreed date), the retiring Agent may appoint one; resignation becomes effective on the stated Resignation Effective Date regardless.
  - Removal: If the Agent becomes a Defaulting Lender under clause (e), Required Lenders may remove it (subject to law) and appoint a Company-approved successor. If none accepts within 30 days (or earlier agreed date), the removal is effective on the stated Removal Effective Date.

nodes.title: Delegation of Duties.
nodes.heading: Section 7.06 Delegation of Duties.
nodes.start_phrase: The Agent may perform any and all of its duties and exercise its rights and powers hereunder or under any other Loan Document by or through any one or more sub-agents appointed by the Agent and approved by the Company.
nodes.summary:
- Indemnification of Agent: Lenders must indemnify the Agent, pro rata by outstanding Advances (or, if none, by Commitments), against liabilities and costs arising from the Agreement or the Agent’s actions/omissions, excluding those caused by the Agent’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad-faith material breach. Lenders must also promptly reimburse their pro rata share of the Agent’s out-of-pocket expenses (including counsel fees) related to preparing, administering, amending, or enforcing the Agreement, to the extent not reimbursed by the Company.

- Delegation of duties: The Agent may delegate to sub‑agents approved by the Company and act through its and their Related Parties. Exculpatory protections extend to sub‑agents and Related Parties. The Agent is not liable for a sub‑agent’s negligence or misconduct except for the Agent’s gross negligence or willful misconduct in selecting the sub‑agent, as determined by a final, nonappealable judgment.

- Resignation and removal of Agent: The Agent may resign on notice; the Required Lenders may appoint a successor (approved by the Company) that is a U.S. bank or its Affiliate. If no successor accepts within 30 days (or earlier agreed), the retiring Agent may appoint a qualified successor; resignation is effective on the stated Resignation Effective Date regardless. If the Agent becomes a Defaulting Lender under clause (e), the Required Lenders may remove it and appoint a successor approved by the Company; removal is effective on the Removal Effective Date even if a successor has not yet accepted.

nodes.title: Resignation of Agent.
nodes.heading: Section 7.07 Resignation of Agent.
nodes.start_phrase: The Agent may at any time give notice of its resignation to the Lenders and the Company.
nodes.summary:
- Indemnification: Lenders must indemnify and reimburse the Agent, on a ratable basis (by outstanding Advances or, if none, by Commitments), for liabilities and out-of-pocket expenses related to the Agreement, except to the extent arising from the Agent’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad-faith material breach; reimbursement covers preparation, administration, amendments, enforcement, and related legal advice when not paid by the Company.
- Delegation of duties: The Agent may delegate to approved sub-agents and act through Related Parties; exculpatory protections extend to sub-agents and Related Parties; the Agent is only responsible for gross negligence or willful misconduct in sub-agent selection as finally adjudicated.
- Resignation/removal of Agent: Procedures for Agent resignation (with Required Lenders appointing a Company-approved successor; the retiring Agent may appoint if none within 30 days) and removal if the Agent is a Defaulting Lender; effectiveness upon stated dates; interim direct dealings by Lenders if no successor; successors inherit rights/duties and fees (unless otherwise agreed); indemnities and protections survive for the retiring/removed Agent and its Related Parties for prior actions.
- Non-reliance: Each Lender confirms it makes independent credit analyses and decisions, without reliance on the Agent, other Lenders, or their Related Parties, and will continue to do so.
- Syndication/Lead roles: The Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers have no duties or responsibilities under the Agreement in those capacities.
- ERISA matters (partial): Each Lender represents and covenants that at least one specified condition applies, including that it is not using “plan assets” of Benefit Plans in connection with its participation (only the first condition is shown in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Non-Reliance on Agent and Other Lenders.
nodes.heading: Section 7.08 Non-Reliance on Agent and Other Lenders.
nodes.start_phrase: Each Lender acknowledges that it has, independently and without reliance upon the Agent or any other Lender or any of their Related Parties and based on such documents and information as it has deemed appropriate, made its own credit analysis and decision to enter into this Agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Procedures upon Agent resignation or removal: as of the effective date, the Agent is discharged from duties under the Agreement and other Loan Documents; until a successor is appointed by the Required Lenders, payments, communications, and determinations flow directly between the Company and each Lender; upon acceptance, a successor Agent assumes all rights and obligations, and the predecessor is fully released; successor’s fees match the predecessor’s unless otherwise agreed with the Company; indemnities and protections in this Article (and, as to the Agent, Section 8.04) survive for the benefit of the former Agent, its sub-agents, and Related Parties for actions taken while it served as Agent.
- Non-reliance: each Lender represents it has made, and will continue to make, its own independent credit analysis and decisions without reliance on the Agent, other Lenders, or their Related Parties, based on documents and information it deems appropriate.
- Roles of Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers: in those capacities they have no duties, obligations, or responsibilities under the Agreement, without prejudice to the Agent’s obligations.
- ERISA-related representations: each Lender represents and covenants to the Agent and Lead Arrangers (not to the Borrower) that at least one condition is and will remain true, including that the Lender is not using “plan assets” of one or more Benefit Plans (as defined under ERISA) in connection with entering into, participating in, administering, or performing the Advances, Commitments, or the Agreement.

nodes.title: Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers.
nodes.heading: Section 7.09 Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers.
nodes.start_phrase: Without prejudice to the obligations of the Agent hereunder, the Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers, in their capacities as such, have no duties, obligations or responsibilities under this Agreement.
nodes.summary:
- Effects of Agent resignation or removal: upon the effective date, the retiring/removed Agent is discharged from duties under the credit agreement and other loan documents; until a successor is appointed by the Required Lenders, payments, communications, and determinations otherwise made by/through the Agent are handled directly by each Lender; once a successor accepts, it assumes all rights, powers, privileges, and duties; fee terms for the successor match the predecessor unless the Company and successor agree otherwise; indemnities and protections in this Article (and Section 8.04 as to the Agent) survive for the retiring/removed Agent, its sub-agents, and Related Parties for actions taken while it served as Agent.

- Non-reliance: each Lender confirms it has independently assessed credit and decided to enter the agreement without relying on the Agent, other Lenders, or their Related Parties, and will continue to make independent decisions regarding actions under the agreement and related documents.

- Roles of Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers: in those capacities, they have no duties, obligations, or responsibilities under the agreement (without affecting the Agent’s obligations).

- ERISA matters: each Lender makes initial and ongoing representations/covenants, for the benefit of the Agent and Lead Arrangers (not the Borrower), that at least one specified ERISA-related condition is true; one stated condition is that the Lender is not using “plan assets” of Benefit Plans (as defined under ERISA) in connection with entering into, participating in, administering, or performing the advances, commitments, or the agreement.

nodes.title: Certain ERISA Matters.
nodes.heading: Section 7.10 Certain ERISA Matters.
nodes.start_phrase: Each Lender (x) represents and warrants, as of the date such Person became a Lender party hereto, to, and (y) covenants, from the date such Person became a Lender party hereto to the date such Person ceases being a Lender party hereto, for the benefit of, the Agent and each Lead Arranger, and not, for the avoidance of doubt, to or for the benefit of any Borrower, that at least one of the following is and will be true:
nodes.summary:
- Describes the consequences of the Agent’s resignation or removal: upon the effective date, the departing Agent is discharged from duties under the agreement and other loan documents; payments/communications/determinations are made directly between Lenders until a successor is appointed; the successor inherits all rights and duties; fees remain the same unless otherwise agreed; protections and provisions benefiting the departing Agent and its related parties survive for actions taken while acting as Agent.
- Establishes a non-reliance clause: each Lender independently conducts credit analysis and makes ongoing decisions without relying on the Agent, other Lenders, or their related parties.
- Clarifies that the Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers, in those capacities, have no duties, obligations, or responsibilities under the agreement (without affecting the Agent’s obligations).
- Sets out ERISA-related representations, warranties, and covenants by each Lender for the benefit of the Agent and Lead Arrangers: the Lender either (i) is not using “plan assets,” (ii) relies on specified prohibited transaction exemptions (PTEs) such as 84-14, 95-60, 90-1, 91-38, or 96-23, (iii) qualifies under the QPAM framework of PTE 84-14, or (iv) provides another agreed representation; and, unless (i) or (iv) applies, the Lender further represents that neither the Agent, any Lead Arranger, nor their affiliates is a fiduciary with respect to the Lender’s assets in connection with the facility.
- Provides definitions of “Benefit Plan” and “PTE.”

nodes.title: Erroneous Payments.
nodes.heading: Section 7.11 Erroneous Payments.
nodes.start_phrase: If the Agent notifies a Lender, or any Person who has received funds on behalf of a Lender (any such Lender or other recipient, a “Payment Recipient”) that the Agent has determined in its sole discretion (whether or not after receipt of any notice under immediately succeeding clause (b)) that any funds received by such Payment Recipient from the Agent or any of its Affiliates were erroneously transmitted to, or otherwise erroneously or mistakenly received by, such Payment Recipient (whether or not known to such Lender or other Payment Recipient on its behalf) (any such funds, whether received as a payment, prepayment or repayment of principal, interest, fees, distribution or otherwise, individually and collectively, an “Erroneous Payment”) and demands the return of such Erroneous Payment (or a portion thereof), such Erroneous Payment shall at all times remain the property of the Agent and shall be segregated by the Payment Recipient and held in trust for the benefit of the Agent, and such Lender shall (or, with respect to any Payment Recipient who received such funds on its behalf, shall cause such Payment Recipient to) promptly, but in no event later than two Business Days thereafter, return to the Agent the amount of any such Erroneous Payment (or portion thereof) as to which such a demand was made, in same day funds (in the currency so received), together with interest thereon in respect of each day from and including the date such Erroneous Payment (or portion thereof) was received by such Payment Recipient to the date such amount is repaid to the Agent in same day funds at the greater of the Federal Funds Rate and a rate determined by the Agent in accordance with banking industry rules on interbank compensation from time to time in effect.
nodes.summary:
- Erroneous Payments framework (Section 7.11):
  - Defines “Erroneous Payment” and gives the Agent sole discretion to determine errors; Agent’s notice is conclusive absent manifest error.
  - Any erroneous funds remain Agent’s property, must be segregated/held in trust, and returned within two Business Days in same-day funds, with interest at the greater of the Federal Funds Rate or the Agent’s interbank compensation rate.
  - Lenders/recipients must presume an error when payment details differ from Agent notices or no notice preceded payment, and must notify the Agent within one Business Day upon knowledge of an error.
  - Agent may set off amounts otherwise payable to a Lender against amounts the Lender owes the Agent related to erroneous payments or indemnities.
  - If unrecovered after demand, the Lender is deemed to assign to the Agent an amount of its Advances (not Commitments) equal to the deficiency at par plus accrued interest (assignment fee waived); Agent becomes a Lender for those Advances, may record ownership, and may sell such Advances (with Company consent not unreasonably withheld). Commitments remain unaffected. Agent obtains contractual subrogation rights with respect to the deficiency.
  - Erroneous Payments do not satisfy Borrower obligations except to the extent comprised of funds actually received from a Borrower for that purpose; no increase or acceleration of Borrower obligations results from the error.
  - Payment recipients waive claims and defenses (including “discharge for value,” setoff, and recoupment) regarding retention of erroneous funds.
  - All obligations/waivers under this section survive changes in Agent/Lenders, termination of Commitments, and repayment of Borrower obligations.

- Amendments and waivers (Section 8.01):
  - General rule: require written agreement by the Company and Required Lenders, effective only for the specified instance/purpose.
  - Unanimous (all affected Lenders) consent required to: waive Section 3.01 conditions; increase/extend a Lender’s Commitment or obligations; reduce principal/interest/fees/amounts; postpone payment dates; change voting thresholds; release the guarantee in Section 9.01; modify pro rata treatment (Section 2.15 or related provisions); or amend Section 8.01.
  - Agent’s separate written consent required for changes affecting its rights or duties.
  - Agent and Company may unilaterally cure ambiguities/omissions/typos/defects; such amendment becomes effective unless the Required Lenders object in writing within five Business Days after notice.

- Notices and communications (Section 8.02(a)):
  - Permitted methods: written (including email/telecopy), mail, hand delivery, overnight courier, or as allowed under Section 8.02(b).
  - Specifies delivery addresses for the Company (including email/fax), Lenders (their Domestic Lending Offices), and the Agent, with procedures for updating addresses.
  - Deemed delivery: mail/hand/courier upon receipt; email/telecopy when sent (or next business day if outside recipient’s business hours).
  - Company and Agent may agree on electronic notice procedures; certain materials under Section 5.01(d) must be delivered as specified therein.

nodes.title: Amendments, Etc.
nodes.heading: Section 8. 01 Amendments, Etc.
nodes.start_phrase: No amendment or waiver of any provision of this Agreement or the Notes, nor consent to any departure by any Borrower therefrom, shall in any event be effective unless the same shall be in writing and signed by the Company and the Required Lenders, and then such waiver or consent shall be effective only in the specific instance and for the specific purpose for which given; provided, however, that no amendment, waiver or consent shall, unless in writing and signed by all the Lenders affected thereby, do any of the following: (a) waive any of the conditions specified in Section 3.01, (b) increase or extend the Commitment of a Lender or subject a Lender to any additional obligations, (c) reduce the principal of, or rate of interest on, the Advances or any fees or other amounts payable hereunder, (d) postpone any date fixed for any payment of principal of, or interest on, the Notes or any fees or other amounts payable hereunder, (e) change the percentage of the Commitments or of the aggregate unpaid principal amount of the Notes, or the number of Lenders, that shall be required for the Lenders or any of them to take any action hereunder, (f) release the guarantee as set forth in Section 9.01, (g) modify Section 2.15 or any other provision of this Agreement that relates to the pro rata treatment of the Lenders hereunder or (h) amend this Section 8.01; and provided, further that no amendment, waiver or consent shall, unless in writing and signed by the Agent in addition to the Lenders required above to take such action, affect the rights or duties of the Agent under this Agreement or any Note.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article VIII (Miscellaneous) covering amendments/waivers and notice provisions in a loan agreement.
- Amendments and waivers (Section 8.01):
  - Must be in writing and signed by the Company and Required Lenders; effective only for the specific instance/purpose.
  - Certain changes require consent of all affected Lenders: waiving Section 3.01 conditions; increasing/extending a Lender’s commitment or adding obligations; reducing principal/interest/fees; postponing payment dates; changing voting thresholds/percentages or number of Lenders needed for action; releasing the guarantee in Section 9.01; modifying pro rata provisions (Section 2.15) or Section 8.01 itself.
  - Any change affecting the Agent’s rights/duties also requires the Agent’s written consent.
  - Streamlined corrections: the Agent and Company may fix ambiguities, omissions, mistakes, typos, or defects in any Loan Document; such amendments become effective unless the Required Lenders object in writing within five Business Days after notice.
- Notices and communications (Section 8.02(a)):
  - Permitted methods: written (mail, hand, overnight courier), e-mail, telecopier; electronic methods per agreed procedures.
  - Designated recipients/addresses: Company (700 Anderson Hill Road, Purchase, NY; Assistant Treasurer email; copy to General Counsel fax); Initial Lenders at their Domestic Lending Office per Administrative Questionnaire; other Lenders per their Assignment and Assumption; Agent at its designated address.
  - Address changes by written notice to the Company and Agent (or generally, as applicable).
  - Delivery/receipt timing: mail/hand/courier deemed given when received; e-mail/telecopy when sent (or next business day if sent outside recipient’s normal business hours).
  - Materials required by Section 5.01(d) must be delivered to the Agent as specified there.

nodes.title: Notices, Etc.
nodes.heading: Section 8.02 Notices, Etc.
nodes.start_phrase: All notices and other communications provided for hereunder shall be either (x) in writing (including e-mail or telecopier communication) and mailed, e-mailed, telecopied or delivered or (y) as and to the extent set forth in Section 8.02(b) and in the proviso to this Section 8.02(a), if to any Borrower, to the Company at its address at 700 Anderson Hill Road, Purchase, New York 10577, Attention: Assistant Treasurer, E-Mail: PEPTreasuryCapitalMarkets@pepsico.com, with a copy to General Counsel, Telecopier No. (914) 253-3808; if to any Initial Lender, at its Domestic Lending Office set forth in its Administrative Questionnaire; if to any other Lender, at its Domestic Lending Office specified in the Assignment and Assumption pursuant to which it became a Lender; and if to the Agent, at the Agent’s Address; or, as to the Company or the Agent, at such other address as shall be designated by such party in a written notice to the other parties and, as to each other party, at such other address as shall be designated by such party in a written notice to the Company and the Agent, provided that materials required to be delivered pursuant to Section 5.01(d) shall be delivered to the Agent as specified in the last sentence of Section 5.01(d).
nodes.summary:
- Amendments and waivers: Must be in writing signed by the Company and Required Lenders; certain changes require consent of all affected Lenders (including waiving Section 3.01 conditions, increasing/extending a Lender’s Commitment or obligations, reducing principal/interest/fees, postponing payment dates, altering voting thresholds/required percentages or number of Lenders, releasing the Section 9.01 guarantee, modifying pro rata provisions like Section 2.15, or amending Section 8.01). Any change affecting the Agent’s rights/duties also requires the Agent’s consent.
- Error-correction amendments: The Agent and the Company may unilaterally amend Loan Documents to cure ambiguities, omissions, mistakes, or typos; such amendments become effective unless the Required Lenders object in writing within five Business Days after notice.
- Notices and communications: Permitted via mail, courier, e‑mail, or telecopier; delivery is effective when received (or when sent for e‑mail/fax, subject to business hours). Addresses specified for the Company, Lenders (per Administrative Questionnaire or Assignment), and the Agent; materials under Section 5.01(d) must be delivered as specified therein. The Company and Agent may agree on electronic procedures.
- Electronic platform: The Agent may post “Communications” to Intralinks or a similar platform; Company acknowledges security/confidentiality risks; the platform and materials are provided “as is” without warranties, and the Agent disclaims liability for errors/omissions.
- Lender receipt via platform: A Notice to a Lender during business hours that Communications were posted constitutes effective delivery; upon request, the Agent will send copies by e‑mail or fax. Lenders must provide and maintain a valid e‑mail address for Notices.
- No waiver; remedies: Failure or delay to exercise rights is not a waiver; partial exercise does not preclude further exercise; remedies are cumulative.
- Costs and expenses: The Company must pay on demand all reasonable enforcement costs and expenses of the Agent and Lenders, including reasonable legal fees and expenses related to enforcing the Agreement, Notes, and other Loan Documents.

nodes.title: No Waiver; Remedies.
nodes.heading: Section 8.03 No Waiver; Remedies.
nodes.start_phrase: No failure on the part of any Lender or the Agent to exercise, and no delay in exercising, any right hereunder or under any other Loan Document shall operate as a waiver thereof; nor shall any single or partial exercise of any such right preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right.
nodes.summary:
- Authorizes the Agent to distribute Company-provided written materials to Lenders via an electronic Platform (e.g., Intralinks), with the Company acknowledging security risks and accepting extensive “as is”/“as available” disclaimers and no warranties (including accuracy, completeness, merchantability, fitness, non-infringement, or virus-free).
- Establishes that a Notice to Lenders during normal business hours stating that materials are posted on the Platform constitutes effective delivery; upon request, the Agent will also send copies by email or fax. Lenders must provide and maintain a valid email address for such Notices.
- No Waiver; Remedies: Failure or delay in exercising rights does not waive them; partial exercise doesn’t preclude further or other exercises; remedies are cumulative and not exclusive.
- Costs and Expenses: The Company must pay on demand all reasonable costs and expenses of the Agent and Lenders, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, incurred in enforcing the agreement and related documents, whether through negotiations, legal proceedings, or otherwise.

nodes.title: Costs and Expenses.
nodes.heading: Section 8.04 Costs and Expenses.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company agrees to pay on demand all reasonable costs and expenses of the Agent and the Lenders, if any (including, without limitation, reasonable counsel fees and expenses), in connection with the enforcement (whether through negotiations, legal proceedings or otherwise) of this Agreement, the Notes and the other documents to be delivered hereunder, including, without limitation, reasonable fees and expenses of counsel for the Agent and each Lender in connection with the enforcement of rights under this Section 8.04(a).
nodes.summary:
- Electronic communications: The Agent may post company-provided written materials (“Communications”) to Intralinks or a similar platform; the Company acknowledges security/confidentiality risks; the Platform is provided “as is/as available”; the Agent/Affiliates make no warranties (including merchantability, fitness, non-infringement, or virus-free) and disclaim liability for errors/omissions.
- Notice of delivery: A Notice to a Lender during its normal business hours that Communications were posted to the Platform constitutes effective delivery; upon request, the Agent will e-mail or fax copies; each Lender must provide and keep current an e-mail address for such Notices, and consents to Notice by e-mail.
- No waiver; cumulative remedies: Failure or delay to exercise rights is not a waiver; partial exercise does not preclude further exercises; remedies are cumulative and nonexclusive.
- Costs and expenses: The Company must pay on demand all reasonable enforcement costs of the Agent and Lenders, including reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses.
- Indemnification and liability limits: The Company indemnifies the Agent, Lenders, their Affiliates, and their officers/directors/employees/agents/advisors against claims, losses, and expenses arising out of the agreement, notes, transactions, or use of proceeds (including investigations/litigation), whether or not consummated, except to the extent finally determined to result from an Indemnified Party’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad-faith material breach. No liability for damages from others’ use of information via IntraLinks or similar systems; no indirect, punitive, or consequential damages among the parties (except to the extent such damages are paid by an Indemnified Party to a third party).
- Breakage/compensation: If a Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Advance is paid, converted, accelerated, or assigned on a day other than the last day of its Interest Period, the Company must compensate the affected Lender for reasonable additional losses/costs (including liquidation or reemployment of funds).
- Survival: Obligations under Sections 2.11, 2.14, and 8.04 survive full payment and termination of the agreement.
- Right of set-off: Upon an Event of Default and authorization to accelerate, each Lender and its Affiliates may set off deposits/obligations they owe a Borrower against the Borrower’s obligations, whether or not due; special handling for Defaulting Lenders (immediate payment over to the Agent per Section 2.19, segregation, and prompt statement to the Agent); Lenders must notify the Company after set-off (failure to notify does not affect validity); rights are in addition to other set-off rights.

nodes.title: Right of Set-off.
nodes.heading: Section 8.05 Right of Set-off.
nodes.start_phrase: Upon (i) the occurrence and during the continuance of any Event of Default and (ii) the making of the request or the granting of the consent specified by Section 6.01 to authorize the Agent to declare the Advances due and payable pursuant to the provisions of Section 6.01, each Lender and each of its Affiliates is hereby authorized at any time and from time to time, to the fullest extent permitted by law, to set off and apply any and all deposits (general or special, time or demand, provisional or final) at any time held and other indebtedness at any time owing by such Lender or such Affiliate to or for the credit or the account of any Borrower against any and all of the obligations of such Borrower now or hereafter existing under this Agreement and the Note held by such Lender, whether or not such Lender shall have made any demand under this Agreement or such Note and although such obligations may be unmatured, provided that in the event that any Defaulting Lender shall exercise any such right of setoff, (x) all amounts so set off shall be paid over immediately to the Agent for further application in accordance with the provisions of Section 2.19 and, pending such payment, shall be segregated by such Defaulting Lender from its other funds and deemed held in trust for the benefit of the Agent and the Lenders, and (y) the Defaulting Lender shall provide promptly to the Agent a statement describing in reasonable detail the obligations owing to such Defaulting Lender as to which it exercised such right of setoff.
nodes.summary:
- Indemnification: The Company must indemnify and hold harmless the Agent, each Lender, and their Affiliates and personnel against all claims, losses, liabilities, and expenses (including reasonable legal fees) arising from the Notes, the Agreement, related transactions, or the use of loan proceeds, regardless of who brings the action or whether the transactions close. Carve-out applies for an Indemnified Party’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad-faith material breach as determined by a final, non-appealable judgment.
- Limitation of liability: Lender-Related Parties are not liable for damages from others’ use of information via IntraLinks or similar systems. No party is liable to another for indirect, punitive, or consequential damages related to the Agreement or other Loan Documents or related activities; however, this does not limit recovery of such damages paid by an Indemnified Party to a third party.
- Breakage/compensation: If a Borrower pays or converts a Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Advance, or if such Advance is assigned, on a day other than the last day of its Interest Period (including due to prepayment, conversion, acceleration, or at the Company’s request), the Company must, upon the Lender’s demand (copied to the Agent), reimburse the Lender for reasonably incurred additional losses, costs, or expenses (e.g., from liquidating or reemploying funding).
- Survival: The Company’s obligations under Sections 2.11, 2.14, and 8.04 survive full repayment of the loans and termination of the Agreement.
- Right of set-off (Section 8.05): Upon an Event of Default and authorization to accelerate under Section 6.01, each Lender and its Affiliates may set off any deposits or obligations they owe to any Borrower against that Borrower’s obligations, even if unmatured and without demand. If a Defaulting Lender exercises set-off, it must immediately remit the amounts to the Agent for application under Section 2.19, segregate such funds in trust pending payment, and promptly provide the Agent a detailed statement. Lenders must promptly notify the Company after set-off; failure to notify does not affect validity. These rights are in addition to other set-off or remedial rights.

nodes.title: Binding Effect.
nodes.heading: Section 8.06 Binding Effect.
nodes.start_phrase: This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and thereafter shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Company, each Borrowing Subsidiary (if any), the Agent and each Lender and their respective successors and assigns, except that other than in accordance with Section 5.02(b), the Company shall not assign its rights and obligations hereunder or any interest herein without the prior written consent of all of the Lenders.
nodes.summary:
- Section 8.06 (Binding Effect): The agreement is effective on the Effective Date and binds the Company, any Borrowing Subsidiaries, the Agent, each Lender, and their successors and assigns. The Company may not assign its rights or obligations (other than as permitted under Section 5.02(b)) without the prior written consent of all Lenders.

- Section 8.07(a) (Assignments by Lenders):
  - Lenders may assign all or part of their rights and obligations (including Commitments, Advances, and Notes) to Eligible Assignees with 10 days’ notice to the Agent and the Company’s prior consent (not unreasonably withheld or delayed).
  - If the Company demands an assignment under Sections 2.05(b) or 2.06(b), at least 20 Business Days’ notice to the Lender and Agent is required.
  - Conditions:
    - Assignments must be of a constant (not varying) percentage of all rights and obligations.
    - Minimum assigned Commitment is $10,000,000 unless to an existing Lender/affiliate or a full assignment.
    - Assignee must be an Eligible Assignee.
    - Company-arranged, company-demanded assignments must cover all of the assigning Lender’s rights/obligations (alone or with concurrent assignments).
    - No Lender must assign under a company demand until it receives payment in full of principal, accrued interest, and all other amounts due.
    - Parties must execute an Assignment and Assumption, deliver any requested Note, pay a $3,500 processing/recordation fee, and the assignee must provide required tax forms under Section 2.14.
  - Effect of assignment: Upon execution, acceptance, and recording, the assignee becomes a Lender to the extent assigned; the assignor is released correspondingly and, if fully assigned, ceases to be a party. The assignor’s rights to indemnification/reimbursement under Section 8.04 and its rights/obligations under Sections 2.11 and 2.14 survive.

nodes.title: Assignments and Participations.
nodes.heading: Section 8.07 Assignments and Participations.
nodes.start_phrase: Each Lender may, upon ten days’ notice to the Agent and with the prior consent of the Company (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed) and, if demanded by the Company pursuant to Section 2.05 (b) or 2.06(b), upon at least 20 Business Days’ notice to such Lender and the Agent, will assign to one or more Persons all or a portion of its rights and obligations under this Agreement (including, without limitation, all or a portion of its Commitment, the Advances owing to it and the Note or Notes held by it); provided, however, that (i) each such assignment shall be of a constant, and not a varying, percentage of all rights and obligations under this Agreement, (ii) except in the case of an assignment to a Person that, immediately prior to such assignment, was a Lender or an affiliate of a Lender, or an assignment of all of a Lender’s rights and obligations under this Agreement, the amount of the Commitment of the assigning Lender being assigned pursuant to each such assignment (determined as of the date of the Assignment and Assumption with respect to such assignment) shall in no event be less than $10,000,000, (iii) each such assignment shall be to an Eligible Assignee, (iv) each such assignment made as a result of a demand by the Company pursuant to this Section 8.07(a) shall be arranged by the Company after consultation with the Agent and shall be either an assignment of all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Lender under this Agreement or an assignment of a portion of such rights and obligations made concurrently with another such assignment or other such assignments that together cover all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Lender under this Agreement, (v) no Lender shall be obligated to make any such assignment as a result of a demand by the Company pursuant to this Section 8.07(a) unless and until such Lender shall have received one or more payments from either the Company or one or more Eligible Assignees in an aggregate amount at least equal to the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Advances owing to such Lender, together with accrued interest thereon to the date of payment of such principal amount and all other amounts payable to such Lender under this Agreement, (vi) the parties to each such assignment shall execute and deliver to the Agent, for its acceptance and recording in the Register (as defined in clause (d) below), an Assignment and Assumption, together with any Note requested pursuant to Section 2.13(e) subject to such assignment and a processing and recordation fee of $3,500, and (vii) the Eligible Assignee shall complete, execute and deliver to the Borrowers and Agent the appropriate tax form pursuant to Section 2.14.
nodes.summary:
- Binding Effect (Section 8.06): The agreement is effective as of the Effective Date and binds/benefits the Company, any Borrowing Subsidiary, the Agent, each Lender, and their successors/assigns. The Company may not assign its rights/obligations (except as permitted by Section 5.02(b)) without prior written consent of all Lenders.

- Assignments by Lenders (Section 8.07(a), (b), (c), (d)):
  - Lenders may assign all or part of their rights/obligations (Commitments, Advances, Notes) with 10 days’ notice to the Agent and the Company’s prior consent (not unreasonably withheld/delayed). If the Company demands replacement under Sections 2.05(b) or 2.06(b), at least 20 Business Days’ notice applies.
  - Conditions: assignment must be a constant percentage; minimum assigned Commitment of $10,000,000 (with exceptions for existing Lenders/affiliates or full assignments); assignee must be an Eligible Assignee; Company-arranged replacements must cover all of the assigning Lender’s position; assigning Lender need not assign under a Company demand until it receives full payoff of principal, accrued interest, and other amounts due; parties must execute an Assignment and Assumption (Exhibit C), deliver any subject Notes, pay a $3,500 processing fee, and the assignee must provide required tax forms under Section 2.14.
  - Effect: upon execution, delivery, Agent’s acceptance/recording, and tax compliance, the assignee becomes a Lender with corresponding rights/obligations and the assignor is released to the extent assigned; the assignor’s indemnification and certain tax-related rights/obligations under Sections 2.11, 2.14, and 8.04 survive.
  - Agent maintains a conclusive Register (as nonfiduciary agent for the Borrower) of Lenders, Commitments, and loan amounts; available for inspection by the Company and Lenders upon reasonable notice. Company issues replacement Notes as needed.

- SPV Funding Option (within Section 8.07(a)):
  - A Lender (Granting Lender) may permit its identified SPV to fund Advances using the Granting Lender’s Commitment. No SPV funding commitment is created; the Granting Lender must fund if the SPV does not.
  - Borrowers may enforce rights against either the Granting Lender or the SPV. SPVs are not liable for payments so long as the Granting Lender performs.
  - Non-petition: parties agree not to initiate insolvency proceedings against an SPV until one year and one day after all its commercial paper or senior debt is repaid.
  - An SPV may assign interests in its Advances to its Granting Lender or approved liquidity/credit support providers without Company/Agent consent or fees; SPVs may share confidential information with rating agencies, CP dealers, and support providers on a confidential basis.
  - This SPV paragraph cannot be amended without consent of any SPV then holding Advances.

- Participations (Section 8.07(e), (f)):
  - Lenders may sell participations with the Company’s prior consent (not unreasonably withheld) and notice to the Agent. The Lender remains lender of record, retains obligations, and the Borrowers/Agent/Lenders deal solely with that Lender.
  - Participants have no voting rights on amendments/waivers except those directly reducing amounts payable to them, postponing payment dates for amounts payable to them, or releasing the Company (including under Article IX) as to their participations.
  - Each Lender must maintain a conclusive Participant Register (as nonfiduciary agent for the Borrower) recording participant details; disclosure of the register is only as needed to establish “registered form” under Treasury Reg. § 5f.103-1(c).
  - Lenders may share Borrower information with assignees/participants (or prospective ones) subject to confidentiality undertakings.

- Pledges to Central Banks (Section 8.07(g)): Lenders may create security interests in their rights (including loans/Notes) in favor of a Federal Reserve Bank or other relevant central bank.

- Confidentiality (Section 8.08):
  - Agent and Lenders must keep Borrowers’ Confidential Information confidential, with permitted disclosures to: affiliates and their personnel/advisors and actual/prospective assignees/participants (on a confidential basis); as required by law/regulation/judicial process; rating agencies (subject to confidentiality); bank and other regulators/examiners; in connection with exercising remedies or related proceedings; and customary data service providers (e.g., league tables) limited to facility identity, type, amount, maturity, and arranger/agent roles, excluding confidential business information of the Company.

nodes.title: Confidentiality.
nodes.heading: Section 8.08 Confidentiality.
nodes.start_phrase: Neither the Agent nor any Lender shall disclose any Confidential Information to any Person without the consent of the Company, other than (a) to the Agent’s or such Lender’s Affiliates and their officers, directors, employees, agents and advisors and to actual or prospective assignees and participants, and then only on a confidential basis, (b) as required by any law, rule or regulation or judicial process, (c) to any rating agency when required by it, provided that, prior to any such disclosure, such rating agency shall undertake to preserve the confidentiality of any Confidential Information relating to the Borrowers received by it from such Lender, (d) as requested or required by any state, federal or foreign authority or examiner regulating banks or banking or any regulatory authority (including any self-regulatory authority), (e) in connection with the exercise of any remedies hereunder or any suit, action or proceeding relating to this Agreement or the enforcement of rights hereunder and (f) disclosures of information pertaining to this Agreement of the sort routinely provided by arrangers to data service providers, including league table providers, that serve the lending industry; provided that such disclosure is limited to information identifying the Company, the type, amount and maturity of the credit facility established hereby and the roles and titles of the Lead Arrangers, Agent and Syndication Agent named on the cover hereof (and excluding any confidential information relating to the business of the Company).
nodes.summary:
- Lender participations:

  - Original Lender’s obligations and relationship with Agent/Borrowers remain unchanged; Borrowers, Agent, and other Lenders deal solely with the original Lender.
  - Participants have no consent rights over amendments/waivers except those directly affecting their economics (reductions of principal/interest/fees, payment date extensions on amounts subject to the participation) or releasing the Company (including Article IX obligations).
  - Each Lender must maintain a U.S.-based Participant Register, acting as a nonfiduciary agent of the Borrower; entries are conclusive absent manifest error. Disclosure of the register is only as needed to prove “registered form” under Treasury Reg. §5f.103-1(c).

- Information sharing for assignments/participations:
  - Lenders may disclose Borrower information to (prospective) assignees/participants conditioned on confidentiality undertakings.

- Pledges to central banks:
  - Lenders may create security interests in their rights (including advances and notes) in favor of Federal Reserve Banks or other relevant central banks under Regulation A.

- Confidentiality:
  - Agent and Lenders must keep Confidential Information confidential, with permitted disclosures to:
    - Affiliates, officers, employees, agents, advisors, and (prospective) assignees/participants on a confidential basis.
    - As required by law, regulation, judicial process, or regulatory authorities/examiners.
    - Rating agencies subject to confidentiality.
    - In exercising remedies or in related proceedings.
    - Routine industry data service disclosures limited to non-business-confidential deal metadata (company identity, facility type/amount/maturity, roles/titles).
  - Agent may provide basic facility data (and if requested, the agreement) to numbering agencies for unique loan identifiers, with confidentiality expectations.

  - New York law governs the Agreement, other Loan Documents (unless otherwise stated), and related claims in contract, tort, or otherwise.

- Execution and electronic signatures:
  - Agreement may be executed in counterparts; emailed/faxed signature pages are effective.
  - Electronic signatures, electronic assignment platforms, and digital copies are valid and enforceable under E-SIGN, New York ESRA, and similar UETA-based laws.

- Jurisdiction and enforcement:
  - Exclusive forum for disputes related to the Agreement/Loan Documents: New York State courts in New York County and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, including appellate courts.
  - Parties submit to such jurisdiction; final judgments are conclusive and enforceable elsewhere. Right preserved to bring actions to enforce judgments in other jurisdictions.

nodes.title: Governing Law.
nodes.heading: Section 8.09 Governing Law.
nodes.start_phrase: This Agreement and the other Loan Documents and any claims, controversy, dispute or cause of action (whether in contract or tort or otherwise) based upon, arising out of or relating to this Agreement or any other Loan Document (except, as to any other Loan Document, as expressly set forth therein) and the transactions contemplated hereby and thereby shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the law of the State of New York.
nodes.summary: The excerpt permits the Agent to disclose basic loan-facility information (and, if requested, a copy of the Agreement) to organizations that assign standard identification numbers, with confidentiality safeguards and limited public release. It establishes New York law as the governing law for the Agreement, the other Loan Documents, and related claims. It allows execution in counterparts and recognizes electronic signatures, electronic delivery, and electronic records as legally effective under E‑SIGN, New York’s ESRA, and similar laws. It includes a forum-selection and jurisdiction clause requiring any actions relating to the Agreement or other Loan Documents against the Agent, Lenders, or their Related Parties to be brought exclusively in New York County state courts or the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, with parties submitting to such jurisdiction and allowing enforcement of judgments in other jurisdictions.

nodes.title: Execution in Counterparts.
nodes.heading: Section 8.10 Execution in Counterparts.
nodes.start_phrase: This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts and by different parties hereto in separate counterparts, each of which when so executed shall be deemed to be an original and all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same agreement.
nodes.summary:

- Execution and signatures: The Agreement may be executed in counterparts; emailed or faxed signature pages are effective; electronic signatures, digital copies, and electronic records are valid and enforceable under applicable e-signature laws (E-SIGN, NY ESRA, UETA-like statutes) and approved electronic platforms.
- Jurisdiction and venue: Parties agree to bring any actions relating to the Agreement or Loan Documents exclusively in New York state courts in New York County or the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; they submit to those courts’ jurisdiction; final judgments there are conclusive and may be enforced elsewhere; parties may still bring actions in other courts to enforce such judgments.

nodes.title: Jurisdiction, Etc.
nodes.heading: Section 8.11 Jurisdiction, Etc.
nodes.start_phrase: Each of the parties hereto hereby irrevocably and unconditionally agrees that it will not commence any action, litigation or proceeding of any kind or description, whether in law or equity, whether in contract or in tort or otherwise, against the Agent, any Lender or any Related Party of the foregoing in any way relating to this Agreement or any other Loan Document or the transactions relating hereto or thereto, in any forum other than the courts of the State of New York sitting in New York County, and of the United States District Court of the Southern District of New York, and any appellate court from any thereof, and each of the parties hereto irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the jurisdiction of such courts and agrees that all claims in respect of any such action, litigation or proceeding may be heard and determined in such New York State court or, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, in such federal court.
nodes.summary:
- Permitted disclosure: The Agent may share basic loan facility information with agencies that assign standard identification numbers (and provide the Agreement if requested), with confidentiality safeguards and limited public release typical for such agencies.
- Governing law: The Agreement and related Loan Documents are governed by New York law.
- Execution and signatures: The Agreement may be executed in counterparts; electronic delivery and electronic/digital signatures are valid and enforceable under applicable e-signature laws.
- Jurisdiction and venue: Parties agree to bring related actions exclusively in New York state courts in New York County or the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; they submit to such courts’ jurisdiction and agree to enforcement of judgments; objections to venue and claims of inconvenient forum are waived; service of process may be made as per the notice provisions.
- Jury trial waiver: All parties waive the right to trial by jury for disputes related to the Agreement or Loan Documents.
- USA PATRIOT Act notice: Lenders and the Agent must obtain and verify identifying information about the Company to comply with the Act.
- No fiduciary duties: The Agent, Lenders, and their Affiliates may have conflicting economic interests and do not owe fiduciary duties to the Company or its Subsidiaries in connection with the transactions or related communications.
- Bail-in acknowledgment: Parties acknowledge and consent that unsecured liabilities of any Affected Financial Institution under the Agreement may be subject to write-down and conversion by an applicable Resolution Authority, and agree to be bound by such actions.

nodes.title: WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL.
nodes.heading: Section 8.12 WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL.
nodes.start_phrase: EACH BORROWER, THE AGENT AND THE LENDERS HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVE ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION, PROCEEDING OR COUNTERCLAIM (WHETHER BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE) ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR ANY OTHER LOAN DOCUMENT OR THE ACTIONS OF THE AGENT OR ANY LENDER IN THE NEGOTIATION, ADMINISTRATION, PERFORMANCE OR ENFORCEMENT HEREOF OR THEREOF.
nodes.summary:
- Venue and forum: Parties irrevocably waive objections to venue and the defense of inconvenient forum for actions related to the agreement in specified courts, and consent to service of process as provided in the notice section, without limiting other lawful service methods.
- Jury trial waiver: Borrowers, the Agent, and the Lenders waive the right to a jury trial for any disputes (contract, tort, or otherwise) arising from or relating to the agreement, any loan document, or related actions by the Agent or any Lender.

- No fiduciary duties: The relationship between the Company and the Agent/Lenders is arm’s length; the Agent and Lenders may have conflicting economic interests; no fiduciary duties arise from the transactions or communications.
- Bail-in acknowledgment: Parties acknowledge that unsecured liabilities of any Affected Financial Institution under the agreement may be subject to a Resolution Authority’s write-down and conversion powers and agree to be bound by the application of those powers.

nodes.title: USA PATRIOT Act Notice.
nodes.heading: Section 8.13 USA PATRIOT Act Notice.
nodes.start_phrase: Each Lender and the Agent (for itself and not on behalf of any Lender) hereby notifies the Company that pursuant to the requirements of the USA Patriot Act (Title III of Pub. L. 107-56 (signed into law October 26, 2001)) (the “Act”), it is required to obtain, verify and record information that identifies the Company, which information includes the name and address of the Company and other information that will allow such Lender or the Agent, as applicable, to identify the Company in accordance with the Act.
nodes.summary:
- Venue and forum: Parties irrevocably waive objections to venue and the defense of inconvenient forum for actions related to the Agreement or other Loan Documents in specified courts, and consent to service of process as provided in the notice section (without limiting other lawful methods).
- Jury trial waiver: Borrowers, Agent, and Lenders waive the right to a jury trial for any claims (contract, tort, or otherwise) arising from or relating to the Agreement, Loan Documents, or the Agent’s/Lenders’ actions.
- USA PATRIOT Act notice: Lenders and the Agent must obtain, verify, and record identifying information about the Company (e.g., name, address) to comply with the Act.
- No fiduciary duties: The relationship among the Company, the Agent, the Lenders, and their Affiliates is purely commercial; no fiduciary duties arise, and potential economic conflicts are acknowledged.
- Bail-in acknowledgment: Parties agree that unsecured liabilities of any Affected Financial Institution under the Agreement may be subject to Write-Down and Conversion Powers by a Resolution Authority and consent to the application of those powers, including to liabilities payable to or by such institutions (as reflected in subsection (a)).

nodes.title: No Fiduciary Duties.
nodes.heading: Section 8.14 No Fiduciary Duties.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company acknowledges that the Agent, the Lenders and their respective Affiliates may have economic interest that conflict with those of the Company and its Subsidiaries.
nodes.summary:
- Venue and forum: Parties irrevocably waive any objection to venue and the defense of inconvenient forum for suits arising out of or relating to the Agreement or other Loan Documents in the courts designated in Section 8.11(a), and consent to service of process as provided in Section 8.02 (without limiting any other lawful methods of service).
- Jury trial waiver: Borrowers, the Agent, and the Lenders irrevocably waive the right to a jury trial for any action, proceeding, or counterclaim (contract, tort, or otherwise) related to the Agreement, any Loan Document, or the Agent’s/Lenders’ actions in negotiation, administration, performance, or enforcement.
