nodes.title: Acknowledgement and Consent to Bail-In of Affected Financial Institutions.
nodes.heading: Section 8.15 Acknowledgement and Consent to Bail-In of Affected Financial Institutions.
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, any Note or in any other agreement, arrangement or understanding among any such parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, each party hereto acknowledges that any liability of any Affected Financial Institution arising under this Agreement, to the extent such liability is unsecured, may be subject to the Write-Down and Conversion Powers of the applicable Resolution Authority and agrees and consents to, and acknowledges and agrees to be bound by:
nodes.summary:
- Venue and service of process: Parties irrevocably waive objections to venue and forum non conveniens for actions related to the agreement and consent to service of process as provided in the notice section, without limiting other lawful service methods.
- Waiver of jury trial: Borrowers, the Agent, and Lenders waive the right to a jury trial for any claims arising from or related to the agreement, other loan documents, or the Agent’s/Lenders’ actions in negotiation, administration, performance, or enforcement.
- USA PATRIOT Act notice: Lenders and the Agent must obtain, verify, and record identifying information about the Company to comply with the Act’s customer identification requirements.
- No fiduciary duties: The parties acknowledge potential economic conflicts and agree the relationship is arm’s length; no fiduciary duties are owed by the Agent, Lenders, or their affiliates.
- Bail-in acknowledgment: Parties agree that unsecured liabilities of “Affected Financial Institutions” may be subject to resolution authorities’ write-down and conversion powers, including reduction/cancellation, conversion to equity or ownership instruments, or variation of terms; Lenders must notify the Agent (who notifies the Company) if subject to a potential bail-in. Definitions provided for Affected Financial Institution, Bail-In Action/Legislation, EEA/UK institutions and authorities, and Write-Down and Conversion Powers.
- Judgment and currency conversion: Sets exchange-rate mechanics for converting Dollar or Euro obligations for judgment purposes using Citibank London rates on the business day before judgment; establishes that obligations are discharged only to the extent primary currency can be repurchased with the judgment currency the next business day, with borrower indemnifying for shortfalls and lender remitting any excess.

nodes.title: Judgment.
nodes.heading: Section 8.16 Judgment.
nodes.start_phrase: If for the purposes of obtaining judgment in any court it is necessary to convert a sum due hereunder in Dollars into another currency, the parties hereto agree, to the fullest extent permitted under applicable law, that the rate of exchange used shall be that at which in accordance with normal banking procedures the Agent could purchase Dollars with such other currency at Citibank’s principal office in London at 11:00 A.M. (London time) on the Business Day preceding that on which final judgment is given.
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms related to EU/UK bank resolution regimes, including EU Bail-In Legislation Schedule, Resolution Authority (EEA and UK), UK Financial Institution (by reference to PRA Rulebook and FCA Handbook IFPRU 11.6), UK Resolution Authority (Bank of England or equivalent), and Write-Down and Conversion Powers (scope of authorities to cancel, reduce, convert, or suspend liabilities).
- Sets judgment currency provisions: specifies exchange rates for court judgments converting (i) Dollars into another currency and (ii) Euros into Dollars, using Citibank London’s rate at 11:00 A.M. (London time) on the Business Day prior to judgment.
- Establishes Primary Currency vs. Judgment Currency mechanics: borrower must indemnify lenders/agent for any shortfall caused by currency conversion after judgment; any excess must be returned to the borrower.
- Introduces Article IX Guarantee: the parent company unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees prompt payment of principal, interest, and all amounts owed by designated Borrowing Subsidiaries under the agreement, including upon acceleration, prepayment, extensions, or renewals.
- Clarifies the guarantee is absolute and unconditional: not affected by validity, modifications, extensions, waivers, release of other guarantees/security, or any other circumstance that might otherwise discharge a guarantor.
- Waiver of defenses and procedural requirements: the company waives diligence, presentment, demand, protest, and notices; lenders/agent need not exhaust remedies against subsidiaries or others before enforcing the guarantee.
- Confirms the guarantee is a guarantee of payment (not collection) and notes inclusion of any obligations assumed under Section 2.17(b).

nodes.title: Guarantee.
nodes.heading: Section 9.01 Guarantee.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company hereby unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees to each Lender and the Agent and their respective successors and assigns the prompt payment in full when due (whether at stated maturity, by acceleration, by optional prepayment or otherwise) of the principal of and interest on the Advances to and the Notes of (to the extent of the principal of and interest on Advances made to) each Borrowing Subsidiary and all other amounts whatsoever from time to time now or hereafter owing to the Lenders or the Agent or any of them by any Borrowing Subsidiary under this Agreement pursuant to such Borrowing Subsidiary’s Designation Letter, in each case strictly in accordance with the terms thereof (such obligations being herein collectively called the “Guaranteed Obligations”).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes an Article IX “Guarantee” under which the Company unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees to the Agent and each Lender (and their successors/assigns) the prompt, full payment of all “Guaranteed Obligations” of each Borrowing Subsidiary.
- Scope of Guaranteed Obligations: principal and interest on Advances and Notes (to the extent relating to Advances to that Borrowing Subsidiary) and all other amounts owed under the Agreement pursuant to the Borrowing Subsidiary’s Designation Letter.
- Payment commitment: if any Borrowing Subsidiary fails to pay when due (at maturity, upon acceleration, mandatory/optional prepayment, or otherwise), the Company must promptly pay in full without demand or notice; this applies equally to extensions or renewals.
- Nature of guarantee: it is a guarantee of payment, not collection.
- Unconditional obligations: the Company’s obligations (including any assumed under Section 2.17(b)) are absolute and unaffected by:
  - the validity, enforceability, or regularity of the underlying obligations,
  - any modifications, amendments, additions, extensions, or waivers,
  - any failure to enforce, or extensions of time for performance,
  - any exchange, surrender, release of other guarantees or security,
  - or any circumstance that might otherwise discharge a surety/guarantor.
- Express waivers by the Company: diligence, presentment, demand, protest, all notices, and any requirement that the Agent/Lenders first exhaust remedies or proceed against the Borrowing Subsidiary, other obligors, or collateral.

nodes.title: Obligations Unconditional.
nodes.heading: Section 9.02 Obligations Unconditional.
nodes.start_phrase: The obligations of the Company under this Article IX, and the obligations (if any) of the Company assumed pursuant to Section 2.17(b), are unconditional irrespective of (i) the value, genuineness, legality, validity, regularity or enforceability of any of the Guaranteed Obligations, (ii) any modification, amendment or variation in or addition to the terms of any of the Guaranteed Obligations or any covenants in respect thereof or any security therefor, (iii) any extension of time for performance or waiver of performance of any covenant of any Borrowing Subsidiary or any failure or omission to enforce any right with regard to any of the Guaranteed Obligations, (iv) any exchange, surrender, release of any other guaranty of or security for any of the Guaranteed Obligations, or (v) any other circumstance whatsoever which may or might constitute a legal or equitable discharge or defense of a surety or guarantor, it being the intent hereof that the obligations of the Company under this Article IX shall be absolute and unconditional under any and all circumstances.
nodes.summary:
- Article IX establishes a comprehensive, unconditional, and irrevocable guarantee by the Company in favor of each Lender and the Agent (and their successors/assigns).
- The Company guarantees prompt, full payment when due of: (i) principal and interest on Advances and related Notes of each designated Borrowing Subsidiary, and (ii) all other amounts owed under the Agreement pursuant to such Borrowing Subsidiary’s Designation Letter—strictly per their terms and including payments due at maturity, upon acceleration, and upon optional or mandatory prepayment, as well as during any extensions or renewals.
- If any Borrowing Subsidiary fails to pay, the Company must promptly pay in full without demand or notice; this obligation applies equally to extended or renewed obligations.
- The guarantee obligations (including any assumed under Section 2.17(b)) are absolute and unconditional regardless of: validity or enforceability of underlying obligations; any modifications, amendments, additions, or covenants; extensions, waivers, or failures to enforce; exchanges, releases, or surrenders of other guarantees or collateral; or any other circumstance that might otherwise discharge a guarantor.
- The Company expressly waives diligence, presentment, demand, protest, and all notices, and any requirement that the Agent or Lenders first pursue or exhaust remedies against any Borrowing Subsidiary, other guarantors, or collateral.
- The guarantee is a guarantee of payment, not of collection.

nodes.title: Reinstatement.
nodes.heading: Section 9.03 Reinstatement.
nodes.start_phrase: The guarantee in this Article IX shall be automatically reinstated if and to the extent that for any reason any payment by or on behalf of any Borrowing Subsidiary in respect of the Guaranteed Obligations is rescinded or must be otherwise restored by any holder(s) of any of the Guaranteed Obligations, whether as a result of any proceedings in bankruptcy or reorganization or otherwise.
nodes.summary:
- Reinstatement: The Company’s guarantee is automatically reinstated if any payment by a Borrowing Subsidiary on Guaranteed Obligations is clawed back or must be restored (e.g., due to bankruptcy or reorganization).
- Waiver of subrogation: Until commitments terminate and all amounts to the Agent/Lenders are paid in full, the Company irrevocably waives all subrogation and contribution rights (including those under the Bankruptcy Code).
- Remedies/acceleration: Notwithstanding any bankruptcy stay or similar prohibition affecting a Borrowing Subsidiary, the Lenders/Agent may accelerate or deem accelerated the subsidiary’s obligations for purposes of enforcing the Company’s guarantee, making them immediately due from the Company.
- Continuing guarantee: The guarantee is continuing and applies to all Guaranteed Obligations whenever they arise.

nodes.title: Subrogation.
nodes.heading: Section 9.04 Subrogation.
nodes.start_phrase: Until the termination of the Commitments and the payment in full of the principal of and interest on the Advances and all other amounts payable to the Agent or any Lender hereunder, the Company hereby irrevocably waives all rights of subrogation or contribution, whether arising by operation of law (including, without limitation, any such right arising under the Federal Bankruptcy Code) or otherwise, by reason of any payment by it pursuant to the provisions of this Article IX.
nodes.summary:
- Reinstatement: The Company’s guarantee is automatically reinstated if any payment made by a Borrowing Subsidiary on the Guaranteed Obligations is rescinded or must be restored (e.g., due to bankruptcy or reorganization).
- Waiver of subrogation/contribution: Until all commitments are terminated and all amounts (principal, interest, and other sums) are paid in full, the Company irrevocably waives any rights of subrogation or contribution arising from payments it makes under the guarantee.
- Remedies and acceleration: For purposes of enforcing the guarantee, the obligations of any Borrowing Subsidiary may be declared or deemed accelerated under Article VI notwithstanding any stay or injunction (including in bankruptcy) against the Subsidiary; upon such declaration or automatic acceleration, those obligations become immediately due and payable by the Company under the guarantee.
- Continuing nature: The guarantee is continuing and applies to all Guaranteed Obligations whenever they arise.

nodes.title: Remedies.
nodes.heading: Section 9.05 Remedies.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company agrees that, as between the Company on the one hand and the Lenders and the Agent on the other hand, the obligations of any Borrowing Subsidiary guaranteed under this Agreement may be declared to be forthwith due and payable, or may be deemed automatically to have been accelerated, as provided in Article VI, for purposes of Section 9.01 hereof notwithstanding any stay, injunction or other prohibition (whether in a bankruptcy proceeding affecting such Borrowing Subsidiary or otherwise) preventing such declaration as against such Borrowing Subsidiary and that, in the event of such declaration or automatic acceleration such obligations (whether or not due and payable by such Borrowing Subsidiary) shall forthwith become due and payable by the Company for purposes of said Section 9.01.
nodes.summary:
- Reinstatement: The parent company’s guarantee automatically revives to the extent any payment by a Borrowing Subsidiary on the guaranteed obligations is rescinded or must be restored, including due to bankruptcy or reorganization.
- Subrogation waiver: Until all commitments are terminated and all amounts (principal, interest, and other sums) are paid in full, the company irrevocably waives any rights of subrogation or contribution arising from payments it makes under the guarantee, whether by law (including under the Bankruptcy Code) or otherwise.
- Remedies and acceleration: For purposes of enforcing the guarantee, the Borrowing Subsidiary’s obligations may be declared immediately due and payable, or deemed automatically accelerated, as provided in Article VI, despite any stay or injunction (including in bankruptcy) that would prevent such declaration against the subsidiary; upon such declaration/acceleration, those obligations become immediately due from the company under the guarantee.
- Continuing guarantee: The guarantee is continuing and applies to all guaranteed obligations whenever they arise.

nodes.title: Continuing Guarantee.
nodes.heading: Section 9.06 Continuing Guarantee.
nodes.start_phrase: The guarantee in this Article IX is a continuing guarantee and shall apply to all Guaranteed Obligations whenever arising.
nodes.summary:
- Article IX Guarantee Provisions:
  - Reinstatement: The parent guarantee automatically reinstates if any payment by a Borrowing Subsidiary on guaranteed obligations is rescinded or must be restored (e.g., in bankruptcy or reorganization).
  - Subrogation Waiver: Until commitments terminate and all obligations are paid in full, the Company irrevocably waives rights of subrogation or contribution arising from payments made under the guarantee.
  - Remedies: Guaranteed obligations may be declared due and payable, or deemed accelerated, for purposes of enforcing the Company’s guarantee notwithstanding any stay or injunction affecting the Borrowing Subsidiary; upon such declaration/acceleration, the Company’s obligations become immediately due and payable.
  - Continuing Nature: The guarantee is continuing and applies to all guaranteed obligations whenever arising.

- Execution/Signature Pages:
  - Evidence of due execution and delivery of the 364-Day Credit Agreement by PepsiCo, Inc. (with named officers), Citibank, N.A. as Agent, and a roster of initial lenders (including major U.S. and international banks), each with authorized signatories.

- Exhibit A – Form of Note:

If, after a reduction, Swing Line Commitments exceed Revolving Credit Commitments, Swing Line Commitments are automatically reduced to eliminate the excess.
  - Company may, with similar notice to the Agent and each Swing Line Lender, terminate or permanently reduce Swing Line Commitments ratably, in $25,000,000 minimum plus $1,000,000 increments.
  - If a Lender demands compensation under Sections 2.11 or 2.14, or is a Defaulting or Non-Consenting Lender, the Company may terminate that Lender’s Commitments or require assignment of its position under Section 8.07. Upon termination, the Company must pay all outstanding principal, accrued interest, and other amounts owed to that Lender; the Lender then ceases to be a party.
  - Commitment increases: The Company may propose increases to aggregate Revolving Credit Commitments by at least $25,000,000 plus $1,000,000 increments, subject to no Default on the Increase Notice Date and Increase Date, and an aggregate cap of $4,950,000,000.

structure.title: Termination, Reduction or Increase of Commitments
structure.summary:
- Agent’s fees: The Company will pay the Agent fees as separately agreed.
- Borrower’s right to reduce/terminate commitments:
  - Revolving Credit Commitments: With at least 3 Business Days’ notice, the Company may terminate or ratably reduce unused commitments in amounts of $25,000,000 and $1,000,000 multiples; cannot reduce below outstanding Advances; Swing Line Commitments automatically reduced if they would exceed aggregate Revolving Commitments post-reduction.
  - Swing Line Commitments: With at least 3 Business Days’ notice to the Agent and each Swing Line Lender, the Company may terminate or permanently reduce, in $25,000,000 and $1,000,000 multiples.
- Lenders subject to demand/Default/non-consent:
  - If a Lender demands compensation under Sections 2.11 or 2.14, or is a Defaulting or Non-Consenting Lender, the Company may on 3 Business Days’ notice terminate that Lender’s Commitments or require assignment of its position under Section 8.07.
  - Upon termination, the Company must pay that Lender all outstanding principal, accrued interest, and other amounts due; the Lender then ceases to be a party.
- Increases to Revolving Credit Commitments:
  - Parameters and conditions: Increases must be in $25,000,000 and $1,000,000 multiples; no Default on the Increase Notice Date or Increase Date; post-increase aggregate cap of $4,950,000,000.
  - Process:
    - Company delivers an Increase Notice to the Agent specifying amount, an Increase Date at least 30 days out, and any proposed New Lenders; Agent notifies all Lenders.
    - Agent invites identified New Lenders within 5 days; New Lenders have until 10 days after the notice to make irrevocable commitments of at least $25,000,000, execute satisfactory documentation, and pay a $3,500 processing fee.
    - If New Lender commitments are insufficient, Agent offers the remainder to existing Lenders by day 15; existing Lenders respond no later than 5 days before the Increase Date.
  - Effectiveness and mechanics:
    - If total committed increase is at least $25,000,000, the aggregate commitments increase (subject to the $4.95B cap) on the Increase Date.
    - On the Increase Date, outstanding Revolving Credit Advances are rebalanced via borrowings/prepayments so holdings are ratable to new commitments; Swing Line participations are deemed reallocated ratably.
    - If total committed increase is less than $25,000,000, no change occurs.
  - Allocation:
    - If not oversubscribed: New Lenders receive their Proposed New Commitments; existing Lenders receive their Proposed Increased Commitments.
    - If oversubscribed: First allocate to New Lenders up to their proposals as agreed by the Company; then allocate the remainder to existing Lenders pro rata to their proposed increases.
  - Conditions precedent: Agent must receive requested updated Revolving Credit Notes and satisfactory evidence (including an updated legal opinion) that the increase and related borrowings are duly authorized.

structure.title: Repayment of Advances; Extension of Termination Date
structure.summary:
- Repayment obligations:
  - Each Borrower must repay, on the Termination Date applicable to each Lender, the outstanding principal of all Revolving Credit Advances, plus all accrued but unpaid interest, fees, and other amounts.
  - Each Borrower must repay Swing Line Advances to the Agent for the ratable account of the Swing Line Lenders and participating Lenders on the earlier of the applicable Termination Date or seven days after the Swing Line Advance is made.

- Extension of Termination Date:
  - The Company may request a one-year extension of the then-current Termination Date by written notice to the Agent 60–30 days before each anniversary of the agreement date, up to two times total. The Agent promptly notifies the Lenders.
  - Each Lender may, in its sole discretion, agree to extend by notifying the Agent 30–20 days before the Extension Date; no response is deemed a decline.
  - Lenders agreeing to extend are Extending Lenders; those declining are Declining Lenders.

- Replacement of Declining Lenders:
  - The Company may require a Declining Lender to assign all its rights and obligations to an Eligible Assignee (which may include an Extending Lender) that agrees to the extension, subject to:
    - Compliance with Section 8.07;
    - Full payment to the Declining Lender of principal, accrued interest, and all other amounts due;
    - Assignment effectiveness on the Extension Date.

- Effectiveness and consequences if no Default exists immediately before the Extension Date:
  - The Termination Date for Extending and Replacement Lenders is extended by one year (adjusted to the preceding Business Day if needed); the Agent promptly notifies the Company.
  - Declining Lenders not replaced retain the Existing Termination Date; all amounts owed to them become due on that date.
  - Total Revolving Credit Commitments are reduced by the commitments of such Declining Lenders on the Existing Termination Date; if a Declining Lender is a Swing Line Lender, total Swing Line Commitments are reduced accordingly.

- Interest on Advances:
  - Each Borrower must pay interest on the unpaid principal of each Revolving Credit Advance from funding until paid in full, at specified per annum rates (details to follow in the document).

structure.title: Interest on Advances
structure.summary:
- Repayment obligations
  - On each Lender’s applicable Termination Date, each Borrower must repay all outstanding Revolving Credit principal, accrued but unpaid interest, fees, and other amounts.
  - Swing Line Advances must be repaid to the Agent for the account of the Swing Line Lenders and participating Lenders on the earlier of the applicable Termination Date or seven days after the Swing Line Advance is made.

- Extension of Termination Date
  - The Company may request up to two one-year extensions of the Termination Date by written notice 60–30 days before each anniversary of the agreement.
  - Lenders may, at their discretion, agree to extend (becoming “Extending Lenders”) by notifying the Agent 30–20 days before the Extension Date; silence is deemed a refusal (“Declining Lenders”).
  - The Company may require Declining Lenders to assign their interests to Eligible Assignees/Replacement Lenders (which may include Extending Lenders), effective on the Extension Date, subject to assignment rules, full payoff of Declining Lenders, and no existing Default.
  - If no Default exists immediately before the Extension Date:
    - Extending and Replacement Lenders’ Termination Date is extended by one year (adjusted to prior Business Day if needed).
    - Declining Lenders keep the Existing Termination Date; all amounts owed to them are due then.
    - Total Revolving Credit Commitments are reduced by the non-extended amounts; if a Declining Lender is a Swing Line Lender, total Swing Line Commitments are reduced accordingly.

- Interest on Advances
  - Revolving Credit Advances:
    - Base Rate Advances: interest at the Base Rate; payable quarterly in arrears and upon conversion or repayment.
    - Term SOFR Advances: Adjusted Term SOFR + 0.625% per Interest Period; payable at period end, every three months for periods >3 months, and upon conversion or repayment.
    - Eurocurrency Rate Advances: EURIBO Rate + 0.625% per Interest Period; same payment timing as Term SOFR.
  - Swing Line Advances: Overnight Rate + 0.625%; interest payable on the date the Swing Line Advance is or must be paid in full. Until Lenders fund participations, interest is for the Swing Line Lenders’ sole account.
  - Default Rate: Upon an Event of Default under Section 6.01(a), principal, interest, and other amounts bear interest at the Default Rate, payable on demand.

- Interest rate determination and fallback
  - The Agent promptly notifies the Company and Lenders of applicable rates used under Section 2.07.
  - If a major interbank market disruption causes Adjusted Term SOFR or EURIBO to inadequately reflect Required Lenders’ costs:
    - Term SOFR Advances convert to Base Rate Advances at the end of their current Interest Period.
    - Eurocurrency Rate Advances are exchanged into an equivalent Dollar amount and converted to Base Rate Advances.
    - Lenders’ obligations to make or convert into Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances are suspended until the Agent announces conditions have normalized.

structure.title: Interest Rate Determination
structure.summary:
- Sets interest terms for Revolving Credit Advances by rate type:
  - Base Rate Advances accrue at the Base Rate, payable quarterly in arrears and upon conversion or payoff.
  - Term SOFR Advances accrue at Adjusted Term SOFR + 0.625%, payable at the end of each Interest Period (and every three months for longer periods) and upon conversion or payoff.
  - Eurocurrency Rate Advances accrue at EURIBO + 0.625% with the same payment timing as Term SOFR Advances.
- Swing Line Advances accrue at the Overnight Rate + 0.625%, payable when the advance is (or must be) paid in full; until lender participations are funded, such interest is for the Swing Line Lenders’ sole account.
- Default Rate: upon an Event of Default under Section 6.01(a), principal, interest, and other amounts under the loan documents bear interest at the Default Rate, payable on demand.
- Agent responsibilities: promptly notifies the Company and Lenders of applicable interest rates used under Section 2.07.
- Market disruption: if Required Lenders determine Adjusted Term SOFR or EURIBO does not reflect funding costs, existing Term SOFR Advances convert to Base Rate at period end; Eurocurrency Advances are exchanged into dollars and convert to Base Rate; new/converted Term SOFR or Eurocurrency borrowings are suspended until conditions normalize.
- Interest Period selection: if the Company fails to choose, a one-month Interest Period is deemed selected.
- Borrowing size floor: if the outstanding amount of a Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Borrowing falls below the Borrowing Minimum, it automatically converts (and, for Eurocurrency, is exchanged into dollars) to a Base Rate Advance.
- Events of Default: upon notice from the Agent at Required Lenders’ request, all Term SOFR and Eurocurrency Advances automatically convert (Eurocurrency first exchanged into dollars) to Base Rate; making/converting to such rate types is suspended while the default continues.
- Benchmark/Rate unavailability: if Term SOFR, EURIBO (as displayed on customary sources), or the Overnight Rate cannot be determined, the Agent notifies parties; affected advances convert at the end of their current periods to Base Rate (Eurocurrency may be prepaid or exchanged into dollars and converted); Lenders’ obligations to make or convert into Term SOFR, Eurocurrency, or Swing Line Advances are suspended until restored.

structure.title: Optional Conversion or Continuation of Advances
structure.summary:
- Section 2.09 (Optional Conversion or Continuation of Revolving Credit Advances):
  - The Company may convert or continue Dollar-denominated Revolving Credit Advances between Types (e.g., Base Rate and Term SOFR) or continue Advances of the same Type/currency.
  - Requires irrevocable notice to the Agent by 11:00 a.m. (NYC time) on the third U.S. Government Securities Business Day before the conversion/continuation date.
  - Restrictions:
    - Term SOFR to Base Rate conversions only on the last day of the applicable Interest Period.
    - Base Rate to Term SOFR conversions must meet the Borrowing Minimum.
    - Conversions cannot create more separate Revolving Credit Borrowings than permitted under Section 2.02(b).
  - Notice must specify: (i) date, (ii) the Dollar Advances to be converted/continued, and (iii) if converting into Term SOFR, the initial Interest Period.
  - Subject to Sections 2.08, 2.12, and 2.18; notice is irrevocable and binding.

- Section 2.10 (Prepayments of Revolving Credit Advances):
  - Optional prepayments:
    - Notice requirements: Term SOFR Advances—3 U.S. Government Securities Business Days; Eurocurrency Rate Advances—3 Business Days; Base Rate Advances—1 Business Day; Swing Line Advances—1 Business Day to the Sub-Agent.
    - Prepayments must be of an entire Borrowing or ratable portions thereof; accrued interest is due on the prepaid principal.
    - Minimum amounts: Borrowing Minimum or a Borrowing Multiple for Revolving Credit Advances; €10,000,000 for Swing Line Advances.
    - Prepayment of Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances may require lender reimbursement/indemnity under Section 8.04(c).
  - Mandatory prepayments:
    - If, as of the most recent interest payment date, Dollar Advances plus the Dollar Equivalent of Euro Advances exceed 105% of aggregate Revolving Credit Commitments (FX measured on the third Business Day prior to that date), the Company must prepay within five Business Days after notice to reduce to ≤100% of Commitments.
    - If Base Rate Advances outstanding are less than the required prepayment, the excess is deferred until the last day of the next maturing Interest Period for Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Advances.
    - Agent provides prompt notice of required prepayments to the Company and the Lenders.

structure.title: Prepayments of Advances
structure.summary:
- Section 2.09 – Optional conversion or continuation of Dollar-denominated Revolving Credit Advances:
  - Company may convert all or part of a Dollar advance from one Type (Base Rate, Term SOFR) to another, or continue advances of the same Type/currency, by irrevocable notice to the Agent by 11:00 A.M. (NYC) three U.S. Government Securities Business Days before the effective date, subject to Sections 2.08, 2.12, 2.18 and the borrowing limits in Section 2.02(b).
  - Term SOFR to Base Rate conversions only on the last day of the relevant Interest Period; Base Rate to Term SOFR must meet the Borrowing Minimum.
  - Notice must specify conversion/continuation date, the advances affected, and, for conversions into Term SOFR, the initial Interest Period.

- Section 2.10 – Prepayments of Revolving Credit Advances:
  - Optional prepayments: Company may prepay with prior notice—3 U.S. Government Securities Business Days for Term SOFR, 3 Business Days for Eurocurrency Rate, and 1 Business Day for Base Rate; Swing Line prepayments noticed to the Sub-Agent.
  - Partial prepayments must be at least the Borrowing Minimum or a Borrowing Multiple for Revolving Credit Advances, and at least €10,000,000 for Swing Line Advances.
  - Prepayments must be in whole or ratable part of the applicable borrowing and include accrued interest; prepayment of Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Rate Advances may require breakage compensation under Section 8.04(c).
  - Mandatory prepayments: If, as of the most recent interest payment date, the sum of (A) Dollar advances outstanding plus (B) Dollar-equivalent of Euro advances exceeds 105% of aggregate Revolving Credit Commitments, the Borrowers must prepay within five Business Days after Agent notice to reduce to 100%.
  - If Base Rate Advances outstanding are less than the required prepayment, the excess is deferred to the last day of the next maturing Interest Period of Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Rate Advances.
  - Mandatory prepayments include accrued interest and any breakage for non-Interest Period dates; Agent calculates exposure at each Notice of Borrowing and each interest payment date and gives prompt (no later than 30 days) notice of any required prepayment.

- Section 2.11 – Increased Costs:
  - If changes in law/regulation, interpretations, or broadly applicable governmental guidelines/requests (including Dodd-Frank, Basel III, BIS/BCBS directives) materially increase a Lender’s cost to make, fund, or maintain Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances (excluding ordinary reserve requirements except as noted), the Company must pay additional amounts to compensate the Lender upon demand.
  - If such changes increase required capital or liquidity for a Lender or its controlling entity attributable to its commitments/advances hereunder, the Company must similarly compensate the Lender.
  - Lender certificates stating the amount are conclusive absent manifest error; must be in reasonable detail and consistent with treatment of similarly situated customers; no obligation to disclose confidential/proprietary information.

structure.title: Increased Costs
structure.summary:
- Prepayments: Any prepayment must include accrued interest to the prepayment date and, if a Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advance is prepaid before the end of its Interest Period, any breakage/indemnity amounts reimbursable under Section 8.04(c). The Agent will, on each Notice of Borrowing date and each interest payment date, calculate total Dollar-denominated Advances plus the Dollar-equivalent (set using rates from the third Business Day prior) of Eurocurrency Rate Advances and give prompt notice (in any event within thirty days) of any prepayment required in connection with that interest payment date.

- Increased costs (Section 2.11):
  - Cost increases: If post-signing changes in law, regulation, interpretation, or broadly applicable governmental guidelines/requests (including those tied to Dodd-Frank or Basel III) materially increase a Lender’s cost of agreeing to make, making, funding, or maintaining Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances (excluding reserve requirements addressed elsewhere), the Company must pay additional amounts on demand via the Agent. The Lender’s certificate of the amount is conclusive absent manifest error.
  - Capital/liquidity requirements: If such changes increase the capital or liquidity a Lender or its controlling entity must maintain and the increase is allocable to the Lender’s Advances or commitments, the Company must compensate the Lender on demand via the Agent, from time to time as specified. The Lender’s certificate (in reasonable detail, consistent with treatment of similarly situated customers, and not requiring disclosure of confidential information) is conclusive as to the calculations absent manifest error.

structure.title: Illegality
structure.summary:
- Section 2.12 (Illegality): If a lender, supported by an opinion of counsel, notifies the Agent that a change in law, regulation, or its interpretation (or a directive from a central bank/authority) makes it unlawful to make, fund, or maintain Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances, then:
  - Any outstanding Term SOFR Advance from that lender automatically converts to a Base Rate Advance upon demand.
  - Any outstanding Eurocurrency Rate Advance is exchanged into an equivalent amount of Dollars and converted to a Base Rate Advance upon demand.
  - Lenders’ obligations to make Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances, or to convert advances into Term SOFR, are suspended until the Agent confirms the illegality no longer applies.

- Section 2.13(a) (Payments and Computations; Evidence of Advances): 
  - Borrowers must make payments by 11:00 A.M. New York time in same-day funds: Dollars for Dollar-denominated obligations and Euros for Euro-denominated advances, to the Agent’s designated account, without deduction, set-off, or counterclaim (except as allowed by Section 2.14).
  - The Agent promptly distributes received funds: principal, interest, and commitment fees ratably to Lenders (except amounts under Sections 2.02(c), 2.05(b), 2.06(b), 2.11, 2.14, or 8.04(c)); other amounts are paid to the relevant Lender.
  - After an Assignment and Assumption is accepted and recorded, payments are redirected to the assignee from the effective date, with any pre-effective date adjustments settled directly between assignor and assignee.

structure.title: Payments and Computations; Evidence of Advances
structure.summary:
- Illegality: If law changes or authorities deem it unlawful for a Lender to make, fund, or maintain Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances, such Advances automatically convert to Base Rate Advances (Eurocurrency Rate Advances first exchanged into Dollars), and obligations to make/convert Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances are suspended until lifted by notice.
- Payments mechanics: Borrowers must pay by 11:00 A.M. New York time in the applicable currency (Dollars or Euros) to the Agent’s Account, without deduction/offset except as under Section 2.14; the Agent distributes principal, interest, and fees ratably (subject to specified exceptions) to Lenders’ Applicable Lending Offices; post-assignment payments are made to assignees from the stated effective date.
- Interest/fee calculations: Base Rate and commitment fees use a 365/366-day year; Adjusted Term SOFR, EURIBO Rate, Overnight Rate, and Federal Funds Rate use a 360-day year; actual days accrued; the Agent’s rate determinations are conclusive absent manifest error.
- Business Day adjustments: Payments due on non-Business Days move to the next Business Day, with interest adjustment; for Term SOFR/Eurocurrency Rate Advances, if that would push into the next calendar month, payment occurs on the preceding Business Day.
- Provisional payments: If the Agent assumes timely Borrower payment and distributes to Lenders but the Borrower hasn’t paid, Lenders must promptly return amounts with interest (Federal Funds Rate for Dollar Advances; Agent’s cost of funds for Euro Advances).
- Evidence of indebtedness: Advances are evidenced by Lender and Agent records, which are conclusive absent manifest error; Agent’s records control in conflicts; upon request, Borrowers issue Revolving Credit Notes; Lenders may attach schedules noting Advance details.
- Currency conversion: The Agent may convert funds between Dollars and Euros to make distributions; the Agent is not liable for conversion losses or failures; Borrowers indemnify the Agent and Lenders for losses, costs, and expenses arising from such conversions.
- Benchmark administration: The Agent may make Conforming Changes related to any Benchmark without further consent and will notify the Company and Lenders when effective.
- Taxes and forms: Lenders and the Agent are exempt from U.S. withholding on “Income” if they are U.S. Persons, have ECI, or qualify under a treaty; U.S. Lenders provide IRS Form W‑9; Foreign Lenders provide appropriate IRS Forms W‑8 (and related certifications) to claim exemption/reduced rates.
- Withholding and assignments: If a Foreign Lender’s forms (or failure to provide them) indicate a non‑zero U.S. withholding rate upon becoming a party, the Borrower may withhold at that rate, and such amounts are excluded from “Taxes” under Section 2.14(c); following an assignment, “Taxes” can include existing U.S. withholding applicable to the assignee to the extent the assignor was entitled to Section 2.14(c) payments, and Borrower obligations are not increased by assignments except for Taxes from a post‑assignment Change in Law.

structure.title: Taxes
structure.summary:
- Agent currency conversions and benchmark changes:
  - Agent may convert funds between Dollars and Euros as needed to distribute payments; not liable for conversion losses or failures; Borrowers indemnify Agent and Lenders for related losses/costs.
  - Agent may make and implement Conforming Changes related to any Benchmark without further consent, with prompt notice to Company and Lenders.

- Comprehensive tax regime (Section 2.14):
  - Withholding exemptions: Lenders/Agent exempt from U.S. withholding on “Income” if U.S. Person, ECI, or treaty-exempt.
  - Documentation: U.S. Lenders provide IRS Form W‑9; Foreign Lenders provide appropriate W‑8 (and supporting forms) upon joining and when requested. If forms indicate a non‑zero U.S. withholding rate (or are not provided), Borrowers may withhold accordingly.
  - Assignments: Borrowers’ tax obligations not increased by assignments except for specified cases, including Change in Law or limited carryover under 2.14(b).
  - Gross-up: Payments made free of withholding Taxes (excluding Excluded Taxes). If withholding is required, Borrowers gross up, withhold, and remit Taxes, and provide receipts within 30 days; indemnity if Lender/Agent pays Taxes directly (no duplication).
  - Limits: No gross-up/indemnity for U.S. withholding unless due to post‑onboarding Change in Law or the specific proviso in 2.14(b).
  - Other Taxes: Company pays and indemnifies for stamp, documentary, excise, property-type taxes; Lenders to use reasonable efforts to change lending office to reduce such taxes if no material burden and at Company’s expense.
  - Cooperation: Lenders provide forms to obtain foreign withholding reductions/exemptions; failure to provide forms (absent undue burden from Change in Law) forfeits indemnity.
  - Change in Law mitigation: Upon request/at Company expense, Lenders use reasonable efforts to change lending office to reduce Taxes if no material burden.
  - Consistency: Any tax-compensation claim must be consistent with Lender’s treatment of similarly situated customers (no disclosure of confidential info required).
  - Refunds: Lenders notify Borrower of refundable Taxes/Other Taxes for which Borrower paid or indemnified; seek refunds upon request; remit net refunds (plus interest, net of expenses/FX effects) within 30 days, with clawback if later repaid to authorities; no obligation to share tax returns.
  - FATCA: Lenders provide FATCA documentation as required to determine compliance/withholding.
  - Exclusivity: Section 2.14 exclusively governs all tax cost-bearing obligations of Company and Subsidiaries.

- Sharing of payments (Section 2.15):
  - If a Lender receives more than its pro rata share on Revolving Credit Advances or Swing Line participations, it must purchase participations from other Lenders to equalize; purchases unwind if the excess is later recovered; purchasing Lender may exercise set-off rights with respect to purchased participations.

- Use of proceeds (Section 2.16):
  - Advances used for general corporate purposes, including working capital, capital investments, and acquisitions.
  - Sanctions compliance: No use of proceeds for or with SDN List parties or Sanctioned Countries/governments, unless licensed by OFAC or otherwise permitted by U.S. law.

structure.title: Sharing of Payments, Etc.
structure.summary:
- Lender FATCA compliance: If payments to a Lender could be subject to FATCA withholding due to the Lender’s noncompliance, the Lender must provide all required and reasonably requested documentation to the Company and Agent to enable FATCA compliance and proper withholding determinations; “FATCA” includes future amendments.
- Tax cost allocation: Only Section 2.14 governs instances where the Company or its Subsidiaries must bear taxes otherwise borne by a Lender; “taxes” broadly includes all taxes, fees, assessments, withholdings, interest, penalties, and additions.
- Sharing of payments: If a Lender receives payments on Revolving Credit Advances or Swing Line participations exceeding its pro rata share (except as permitted under specified sections), it must purchase participations from other Lenders to equalize; any later recovery triggers a proportional unwind and repayment with associated interest/amounts; purchasing Lenders may exercise direct creditor rights, including set-off, against Borrowers for such participations.
- Use of proceeds: Advances may be used for general corporate purposes (working capital, capital investments, acquisitions). Borrowers shall not knowingly use proceeds for activities involving SDN-listed parties or sanctioned countries/governments, unless licensed by OFAC or otherwise lawful under U.S. law.

structure.title: Use of Proceeds
structure.summary:
- Lenders must provide FATCA-related documentation to the Company and Agent as required by law and upon reasonable request to enable compliance and determine any required withholding; “FATCA” includes future amendments.
- Only Section 2.14 requires the Company or its Subsidiaries to bear taxes otherwise borne by Lenders; “taxes” is broadly defined to include withholding, interest, penalties, and additions to tax.
- Payment sharing among Lenders (Section 2.15): if a Lender receives payments on Revolving Credit Advances or Swing Line participations exceeding its ratable share (except in specified cases), it must purchase participations from other Lenders to equalize; if such excess is later recovered from the purchasing Lender, the purchases are unwound proportionally with associated interest/amounts; Lenders may exercise set-off and other payment rights against Borrowers for such participations.
- Use of proceeds (Section 2.16): Advances may be used for general corporate purposes (including working capital, capital investments, and acquisitions); proceeds may not be knowingly used for activities involving SDN List parties or Sanctioned Countries unless licensed by OFAC or otherwise permitted under U.S. law.

structure.title: Borrowings by Borrowing Subsidiaries
structure.summary:
- Establishes how the Company may designate one or more Subsidiaries as Borrowing Subsidiaries (and Borrowers) via a Designation Letter, with at least 10 Business Days’ prior notice for post-Effective Date designations.
- Requires the Agent to notify all Lenders of any pending designation and the identity of the Subsidiary.
- Imposes “know your customer”/Beneficial Ownership compliance: the Company must promptly provide requested documentation so the Agent/Lenders can satisfy applicable identification checks.
- Permits a Lender, when the Borrowing Subsidiary is non-U.S., to fulfill its commitments through an Affiliate or branch acting as the Lender for that Subsidiary.
- Defines “Protesting Lenders” (those legally unable to lend to or do business with a non-U.S. Borrowing Subsidiary) and requires them to notify within five Business Days of the designation notice.
- Gives the Company two options regarding each Protesting Lender: (A) terminate that Lender’s Commitments (with required payoff of principal, interest, fees, and other amounts), or (B) cancel the designation of the proposed Borrowing Subsidiary.
- Provides for terminating a Subsidiary’s Borrower status once all its Advances (principal and interest) are paid, via a Termination Letter; the Agent notifies Lenders and Lenders return any Notes after full payment.
- Clarifies that termination does not discharge unpaid obligations of the Subsidiary (including those arising under Sections 2.11 and 2.14) or the Company’s obligations under Article IX relating to such unpaid amounts.
- If termination occurs because the Company sold/transferred its interest in the Subsidiary and so certifies: (A) the Subsidiary ceases to have obligations under the Agreement/Notes upon effectiveness, and (B) the Company unconditionally assumes, as primary obligor, all such obligations.

structure.title: Benchmark Replacement Setting
structure.summary:
- Establishes procedures for replacing interest rate benchmarks upon a Benchmark Transition Event and Benchmark Replacement Date, including automatic replacement without amendments:
  - If replacement is per clause (a) of “Benchmark Replacement,” it applies immediately to all settings; Adjusted Term SOFR is deemed modified to remove clause (b) for Term SOFR calculations.
  - If replacement is per clause (b), it applies to settings at or after 5:00 p.m. (NYC) on the fifth Business Day after notice unless Required Lenders timely object; if Daily Simple SOFR is used, interest is paid monthly.
- Authorizes the Agent to make Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes unilaterally; such amendments become effective without further consent.
- Requires the Agent to notify the Company and Lenders of benchmark replacement dates and choices, conforming changes, tenor removals/reinstatements, and benchmark unavailability periods; notices may be consolidated; Agent/Lender determinations are conclusive absent manifest error and may be made in sole discretion as permitted.
- Allows the Agent to remove or reinstate specific tenors of a term benchmark (e.g., Term SOFR Reference Rate, EURIBOR) if a tenor is not published or deemed non-representative, by modifying the Interest Period definition.
- Sets rules during a Benchmark Unavailability Period:
  - Borrowers may revoke pending requests for affected benchmark borrowings; otherwise, Term SOFR requests convert to Base Rate; Eurocurrency Rate or Swing Line requests are ineffective.
  - Outstanding Term SOFR Advances convert to Base Rate at period end; Eurocurrency Rate Advances must be converted to Dollar Base Rate (Dollar Equivalent) or prepaid at period end (conversion is the default if no election).
  - Accrued interest and any breakage costs must be paid; the Base Rate excludes any component tied to the unavailable benchmark or tenor.
- Defines key terms:
  - Available Currency: USD or EUR; Available Tenor: usable tenors not removed.
  - Benchmark: initially the Relevant Rate, replaced by the applicable Benchmark Replacement upon a transition.
  - Benchmark Replacement waterfall: (a) for Term SOFR Advances, Daily Simple SOFR + 0.10%; (b) Agent/Company-selected alternative aligned with Relevant Governmental Body guidance or market convention plus the Benchmark Replacement Adjustment; subject to a 0.00% floor.
  - Benchmark Replacement Adjustment: spread or method selected considering official recommendations or market convention.
  - Benchmark Replacement Date: earliest of specified cessation/non-representativeness triggers across all Available Tenors.
  - Benchmark Transition Event: administrator/regulator statements of cessation or non-representativeness across all Available Tenors.
  - Benchmark Unavailability Period: gap between the Replacement Date and implementation of a replacement.
  - Relevant Governmental Body: defined by currency (e.g., Federal Reserve/NY Fed for USD).
  - Relevant Rate: Term SOFR Reference Rate (Term SOFR Advances), EURIBOR (Eurocurrency Rate Advances), €STR (Swing Line Advances).
  - Unadjusted Benchmark Replacement: replacement rate before the spread adjustment.
- Addresses Defaulting Lenders:
  - Voting rights limited as per “Required Lenders.”
  - Payment waterfall for amounts received for a Defaulting Lender: first to amounts owed to the Agent; second to fund missed Advances; third to a reserve for future funding obligations; fourth to amounts owed to the Company from judgments; fifth to the Defaulting Lender or as a court directs.
  - Principal payments on Advances where a Defaulting Lender failed to fund are first applied to Non-Defaulting Lenders pro rata until holdings realign with commitments; payments applied (or held) are deemed paid to and redirected by the Defaulting Lender with irrevocable consent.

structure.title: Defaulting Lenders
structure.summary:
- Key definitions:
  - Relevant Rate: Term SOFR Reference Rate for Term SOFR Advances; EURIBO Rate for Eurocurrency Rate Advances; €STR for Swing Line Advances.
  - Unadjusted Benchmark Replacement: The Benchmark Replacement excluding any related adjustment spread.

- Defaulting Lenders (Section 2.19):
  - Voting: A Defaulting Lender’s amendment/waiver/consent rights are restricted per “Required Lenders.”
  - Payment waterfall: Amounts received for a Defaulting Lender are applied (1) to amounts owed to the Agent; (2) at the Company’s request (if no Default) to fund missed Advances; (3) to a deposit to cover potential future funding; (4) if no Default, to judgments owed to the Company for the Defaulting Lender’s breach; (5) to the Defaulting Lender or as a court directs. Principal on unfunded Advances is first applied pro rata to Non-Defaulting Lenders until holdings match commitments.
  - Fees: Defaulting Lenders forfeit Commitment Fees during the defaulting period; the Company need not pay such fees.
  - Swing Line participations: A Defaulting Lender’s participations are reallocated among Non-Defaulting Lenders up to their Revolving Credit Commitments; no waiver of claims arises from reallocation.
  - If reallocation is insufficient, Borrowers must prepay all outstanding Swing Line Advances.
  - Cure: Upon written agreement of the Company, Agent, and Swing Line Lenders, a cured lender must purchase par portions to rebalance holdings pro rata; no retroactive fee/payment adjustments; no waiver of prior claims.

- Swing Line Advances (Section 2.20):
  - Availability and limits: Each Swing Line Lender provides euro-denominated Swing Line Advances from the Effective Date to its Termination Date, subject to (i) its Swing Line Commitment, its overall Revolving Credit Commitment (inclusive of its own advances and participations), and the Swing Line Sublimit, and (ii) aggregate Unused Revolving Credit Commitments at the time of borrowing.
  - Ratable risk participations: Upon any Swing Line Advance, all Lenders automatically and irrevocably purchase risk participations equal to their ratable shares.
  - Borrowing mechanics: Borrower notice to Sub-Agent by 9:30 a.m. London time for same-day funding; Sub-Agent coordinates funding upon satisfaction of Article III conditions.
  - Funding failures: One Swing Line Lender’s failure does not relieve others. On written demand, each Lender must purchase its ratable portion of outstanding Swing Line Advances; this obligation is absolute, unaffected by Defaults or Commitment changes, and without setoff. Non-funding Lenders owe the Agent amounts plus interest at the higher of the Overnight Rate or Agent’s cost of funds and related fees.
  - Payment distributions: Swing Line Lenders distribute received payments to Lenders pro rata.
  - Sub-Agent assumptions: Absent notice of non-funding, Sub-Agent may fund in reliance on a Swing Line Lender’s presumed funding; the Borrower owes interest at the Swing Line rate, and a non-funding Swing Line Lender owes interest at the Overnight Rate to the Sub-Agent.

- Conditions to Effectiveness (Article III, Section 3.01):
  - Effective Date occurs when:
    - No Material Adverse Change has occurred since December 31, 2022 that has not been publicly disclosed.
    - No pending or, to the Company’s knowledge, threatened actions, suits, investigations, or proceedings that could reasonably be likely to (i) have a Material Adverse Effect not publicly disclosed or (ii) impair the legality, validity, enforceability of the agreement or consummation of the transactions.

structure.title: CONDITIONS TO EFFECTIVENESS AND LENDING
structure.summary:

- Sub-Agent funding reliance and shortfall remedy: Absent prior notice that a Swing Line Lender will not fund its share of a Swing Line Borrowing, the Sub-Agent may assume funding and advance the amount to the Borrower. If a Swing Line Lender fails to fund, both that Lender and the Borrower must promptly repay the Sub-Agent with interest (Borrower at the Swing Line Advance rate; Lender at the Overnight Rate). A Lender’s repayment becomes its Swing Line Advance for that borrowing.

structure.title: Conditions Precedent to Effectiveness
structure.summary:

Repayment by the Swing Line Lender recharacterizes the amount as its Swing Line Advance.

structure.title: COVENANTS OF THE COMPANY
structure.summary:

structure.title: Affirmative Covenants
structure.summary:
The excerpt sets out Article V covenants the Company must observe while any advances are outstanding or any lender has a commitment.

Affirmative covenants (Section 5.01):
- Compliance with laws: The Company and its subsidiaries must comply in all material respects with applicable laws and regulations, expressly including ERISA, Environmental Laws, and Anti-Corruption Laws, and maintain/enforce policies reasonably designed to ensure such compliance; immaterial noncompliance that would not reasonably be likely to have a Material Adverse Effect (MAE) is carved out.

Reports are deemed delivered when posted on the Company’s website or on sec.gov (or another designated, free-access site).

Negative covenants (Section 5.02):

Carve-outs include, among others, liens existing prior to the agreement’s date (with additional carve-outs presumably following).

structure.title: Negative Covenants
structure.summary:

Delivery is deemed made when reports are posted on the Company’s or SEC website and accessible without charge.

  - Secured Debt: no Liens on Principal Property, stock or Debt of Restricted Subsidiaries unless the Advances and other obligations are secured equally and ratably, subject to a basket allowing secured Debt up to 15% of Consolidated Net Tangible Assets and standard permitted Liens (pre‑existing Liens; Liens existing when an entity becomes a Restricted Subsidiary; intercompany Liens; governmental progress payment Liens; acquisition/construction/purchase‑money Liens within 120 days; and extensions/renewals of permitted Liens). Cap on securing more than 65% of a controlled foreign corporation’s stock or assets unless other Company/Restricted Subsidiary Debt is similarly secured.

Exception for mergers solely to reincorporate domestically. Provide KYC information requested by Lenders.

- Events of Default: payment defaults (principal, interest, or other amounts) persisting more than five Business Days; material misrepresentations by the Company or any Borrower; covenant breaches—immediate default for Sections 5.01(d) (reporting) and 5.02 (negative covenants), 30‑day cure after notice for others; cross‑default/cross‑acceleration for Company or Material Subsidiary Debt of at least $500,000,000; and bankruptcy/insolvency events (including inability to pay debts, assignments, relevant proceedings, receivership), with a 30‑day dismissal/stay period for involuntary cases and coverage of authorizing actions.

structure.title: EVENTS OF DEFAULT

structure.title: Events of Default

structure.title: Rights as a Lender

structure.title: Reliance by Agent
structure.summary:
