- Defines the Agent’s right to rely in good faith on documents, electronic communications, and oral/telephone statements believed genuine and from proper persons, without liability; presumes Lenders’ satisfaction of conditions to Advances unless notified otherwise; and permits consultation with counsel, accountants, and experts with no liability for actions taken in reliance on their advice.
- Establishes Lenders’ ratable indemnification of the Agent (if not reimbursed by the Company) for liabilities, losses, and expenses arising from the Agreement or the Agent’s actions/omissions, excluding cases of the Agent’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad-faith material breach; requires prompt ratable reimbursement of the Agent’s out-of-pocket expenses, including legal fees, not covered by the Company.
- Authorizes the Agent to delegate duties to approved sub-agents and act through Related Parties; extends exculpatory protections to sub-agents and Related Parties; limits the Agent’s responsibility for sub-agent misconduct to cases of the Agent’s gross negligence or willful misconduct in selecting them; and confirms the Sub-Agent’s obligations, rights, and benefits under the Agreement as they relate to its specified duties.

structure.title: Resignation of Agent
structure.summary:
- Establishes procedures for the Agent’s resignation: Agent may resign by notice; Required Lenders have 30 days (or earlier agreed) to appoint a successor approved by the Company, which must be a U.S. bank or its U.S. affiliate. If none is appointed and accepts, the retiring Agent may appoint a qualified successor. Resignation is effective on the stated Resignation Effective Date regardless of successor appointment.
- Provides for removal of the Agent if it becomes a Defaulting Lender: Required Lenders may remove by written notice and appoint a successor approved by the Company. If no successor accepts within 30 days (or earlier agreed), removal is still effective on the Removal Effective Date.
- Sets effects of resignation/removal: from the effective date, the retiring/removed Agent is discharged from duties under the Loan Documents; payments, communications, and determinations are handled directly by each Lender until a successor is appointed.
- Successor Agent terms: upon acceptance, the successor inherits all rights, powers, and duties; the predecessor is fully discharged. Company pays the same fees to the successor unless otherwise agreed.
- Survival/indemnity: Article protections (and Section 8.04 as to the Agent) continue for the benefit of the former Agent, its sub-agents, and Related Parties for actions taken while acting as Agent.
- Swing Line provisions: a resigning Agent is relieved of obligations to fund Swing Line Advances on or after the effective date unless it notifies otherwise. Upon successor’s acceptance, the successor becomes Swing Line Lender; the predecessor is discharged, and the successor purchases outstanding Swing Line Advances at par plus accrued interest via an Assignment and Assumption.

structure.title: Non-Reliance on Agent and Other Lenders
structure.summary:
- Section 7.08: Each Lender confirms it has independently evaluated and will continue to independently evaluate the credit and actions under the Agreement and Loan Documents, without relying on the Agent, other Lenders, or their Related Parties.
- Section 7.09: The Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers, in those capacities, have no duties, obligations, or responsibilities under the Agreement, without affecting the obligations of the Agent and Sub-Agent.
- Section 7.10 (ERISA): Each Lender represents, warrants, and covenants (for the benefit of the Agent and Lead Arrangers, not the Borrowers) from becoming a Lender until ceasing to be one, that it satisfies one of the following regarding ERISA/plan asset rules: (i) it is not using plan assets; (ii) a Prohibited Transaction Exemption (e.g., PTE 84-14, 95-60, 90-1, 91-38, 96-23) applies; (iii) it is a QPAM-managed fund meeting PTE 84-14 conditions; or (iv) another written representation acceptable to the Agent. These provisions ensure ERISA compliance for participation in the Advances, Commitments, and the Agreement.

structure.title: Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers
structure.summary:
- Section 7.08 (Non-Reliance on Agent and Other Lenders): Each Lender confirms it has independently conducted its credit analysis and decided to enter the Agreement without relying on the Agent, other Lenders, or their related parties, and will continue to make independent decisions regarding actions under the Agreement and related documents.

- Section 7.09 (Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers): The Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers, in those capacities, have no duties, obligations, or responsibilities under the Agreement, without prejudice to the obligations of the Agent and Sub-Agent.

- Section 7.10 (Certain ERISA Matters): Each Lender represents, warrants, and covenants (for the benefit of the Agent and Lead Arrangers, not the Borrowers) that, throughout its participation, at least one of the following is true: it is not using ERISA “plan assets”; a Prohibited Transaction Exemption (e.g., PTE 84-14, 95-60, 90-1, 91-38, 96-23) applies; it qualifies under the QPAM exemption with specified conditions satisfied; or another ERISA representation/warranty/covenant acceptable to the Agent has been agreed in writing.

structure.title: Certain ERISA Matters
structure.summary:
- Section 7.08 (Non-Reliance): Lenders confirm they have independently conducted their own credit analysis and decision-making to enter into and act under the Agreement and related documents, without relying on the Agent, other Lenders, or their Related Parties.
- Section 7.09 (Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers): In their named capacities, the Syndication Agent and Lead Arrangers have no duties, obligations, or responsibilities under the Agreement (separate from the Agent/Sub-Agent’s obligations).
- Section 7.10 (ERISA Matters): Each Lender represents, warrants, and covenants (for the benefit of the Agent and Lead Arrangers, not the Borrower) that at least one ERISA-related condition is met: it is not using “plan assets”; or a DOL prohibited transaction exemption (e.g., PTE 84-14, 95-60, 90-1, 91-38, 96-23) applies; or it qualifies under QPAM conditions; or another agreed representation applies. Unless certain conditions are met, the Lender also affirms the Agent, Lead Arrangers, and their Affiliates are not fiduciaries with respect to the Lender’s assets in connection with the facility. Defines “Benefit Plan” and “PTE.”
- Section 7.11(a) (Erroneous Payments): If the Agent determines funds were erroneously transmitted to a Lender or its designee (“Payment Recipient”), such amounts (“Erroneous Payments”) remain the Agent’s property, must be segregated and held in trust, and must be returned in same-day funds within two Business Days with specified interest. The Agent’s notice is conclusive absent manifest error.

structure.title: Erroneous Payments
structure.summary:
- Lender fiduciary disclaimer: Unless certain prior conditions apply, each Lender represents, warrants, and covenants (for the benefit of the Agent and Lead Arrangers only) that neither the Agent, any Lead Arranger, nor their Affiliates is a fiduciary with respect to the Lender’s assets in connection with entering into, participating in, administering, or performing under the Advances, Commitments, and the Agreement.
- Defined terms:
  - Benefit Plan: Includes ERISA Title I employee benefit plans, plans subject to Internal Revenue Code Section 4975, and entities holding plan assets for ERISA/4975 purposes.
  - PTE: A Department of Labor prohibited transaction class exemption (as amended from time to time).
- Erroneous Payments (Section 7.11):
  - Ownership/return: Any mistakenly transmitted funds from the Agent to a Lender or recipient on its behalf remain the Agent’s property; must be segregated and returned within two Business Days with interest (at the greater of Federal Funds Rate and interbank compensation rate). Agent’s notice is conclusive absent manifest error.
  - Recipient duties on anomalies: If payment timing/amount differs from notice, lacks notice, or is known/suspected erroneous, error is presumed or deemed; recipient must notify the Agent within one Business Day with details.
  - Setoff: Agent may set off any amounts otherwise payable to a Lender against amounts owed back to the Agent for erroneous payments or indemnities.
  - Failure to return—deficiency assignment: If not recovered, the Lender is deemed to assign to the Agent a portion of its Advances (not Commitments) equal to the unrecovered amount at par plus accrued interest, without assignment fee; Agent becomes Lender for that portion and may sell such Advances, applying net proceeds to reduce the deficiency; Commitments are unaffected. Agent is contractually subrogated to the Lender’s rights with respect to the deficiency.
  - Borrower obligations unaffected: Erroneous Payments do not satisfy Borrower obligations unless comprised of Borrower-originated funds intended for such payment; no increase or acceleration of Borrower obligations results.
  - Waivers: Recipients waive rights/defenses to retain erroneous funds, including “discharge for value” and similar doctrines.
  - Survival: All obligations/waivers survive changes in Agent, Lenders, termination of Commitments, and repayment of Borrower obligations.
- Amendments and waivers (Section 8.01):
  - General rule: Must be in writing signed by the Company and Required Lenders; effective only for the specific instance/purpose.
  - Unanimous Lender consent required to: waive Section 3.01 conditions; increase/extend a Lender’s Commitments or add obligations; reduce principal/interest/fees; postpone payment dates; change voting thresholds/percentages or number of Lenders needed to act; release the Section 9.01 guaranty; modify pro rata provisions (including Section 2.15); or amend Section 8.01.
  - Additional consents: Agent’s written consent required for changes affecting its rights/duties; each Swing Line Lender’s written consent required for changes affecting its rights/duties.
  - Limited swing line mechanics change: Borrowing mechanics for Swing Line Advances may be amended by the Company, Agent, Sub-Agent, and Swing Line Lenders alone if other Lenders are not adversely affected.

structure.title: MISCELLANEOUS
structure.summary:
- Erroneous Payments (Section 7.11(e)-(g)):
  - An Erroneous Payment does not satisfy any Borrower obligations unless, and only to the extent, it consists of funds the Agent actually received from a Borrower for that specific payment purpose. Such errors do not increase or accelerate any Borrower’s obligations compared to what would have been due absent the error.
  - Payment Recipients may not assert rights to retain Erroneous Payments and waive defenses or claims (including discharge for value, set-off, and recoupment) against the Agent’s demand for return.
  - These obligations, agreements, and waivers survive changes to the Agent, Lenders, termination of commitments, and repayment or discharge of Borrower obligations.

- Amendments and Waivers (Article VIII, Section 8.01):
  - Amendments/waivers must be in writing and signed by the Company and Required Lenders, effective only for the specific instance.
  - Unanimous consent of affected Lenders is required to: waive Section 3.01 conditions; increase/extend a Lender’s Commitment or add obligations; reduce principal, interest, fees, or other amounts; postpone payment dates; change voting thresholds or required Lender percentages; release the guarantee in Section 9.01; modify pro rata provisions (including Section 2.15); or amend Section 8.01 itself.
  - Additional consents: the Agent must sign any change affecting its rights/duties; each Swing Line Lender must sign changes affecting its rights/duties.
  - Borrowing mechanics for Swing Line Advances may be amended by written consent of the Company, the Agent, the Sub-Agent, and the Swing Line Lenders, provided other Lenders are not adversely affected.

structure.title: Amendments, Etc.
structure.summary:
- Erroneous Payments (Section 7.11(e)-(g)):
  - An Erroneous Payment does not satisfy any borrower obligations unless (and only to the extent) it consists of funds the Agent received from a borrower specifically to pay such obligations; it does not increase or accelerate borrower obligations.
  - Payment Recipients may not assert rights to Erroneous Payments and waive defenses (including discharge for value) and any set-off/recoupment against the Agent’s demand for return, to the extent permitted by law.
  - These obligations and waivers survive changes in the Agent, Lenders, termination of commitments, and repayment/discharge of borrower obligations.

- Amendments and Waivers (Section 8.01):
  - General rule: amendments/waivers must be in writing signed by the Company and Required Lenders and are limited to the specific instance.
  - Unanimous (all affected Lenders) consent required to: waive Section 3.01 conditions; increase/extend a Lender’s commitment or obligations; reduce principal/interest/fees; postpone payment dates; change voting thresholds; release the guarantee in Section 9.01; alter pro rata provisions (Section 2.15) or amend Section 8.01.
  - Additional consents: the Agent must also sign changes affecting its rights/duties; Swing Line Lenders must sign changes affecting their rights/duties.
  - Swing Line borrowing mechanics may be adjusted with consent of the Company, Agent, Sub-Agent, and Swing Line Lenders if other Lenders are not adversely affected.
  - Error-correction mechanism: the Agent and Company may cure ambiguities, omissions, mistakes, typos, or defects without further consents unless Required Lenders object within five Business Days of notice.

- Notices and Electronic Communications (Section 8.02):
  - Notice methods: written (mail, email, fax, delivery) or as permitted in 8.02(b); specified addresses/contacts for the Company (including email/fax), Lenders (per their designated offices), Agent, and Sub-Agent; timing rules for deemed receipt; allowance for agreed electronic procedures.
  - Electronic platform: the Agent may post borrower-provided materials to Intralinks or a similar system; the Company acknowledges security/confidentiality risks; the platform and posted materials are provided “as is” with broad disclaimers of accuracy, completeness, and warranties.

structure.title: Notices, Etc.
structure.summary:
- Amendment mechanism: Agent and Company may correct ambiguities, omissions, mistakes, typos, or defects in the Agreement or any Loan Document; changes become effective unless the Required Lenders object in writing within five Business Days of notice.
- Notices (Section 8.02): Specifies permitted delivery methods (mail, hand, overnight courier, e‑mail, telecopier), addresses for Company, Lenders, Agent, and Sub‑Agent, timing for deemed receipt, and allowance for electronic communications per agreed procedures.
- Electronic platform: Agent may post “Communications” for Lenders on Intralinks or similar; Company acknowledges security and confidentiality risks; the Platform and Communications are provided “as is/as available” with broad warranty and liability disclaimers.
- Lender notice via Platform: E‑mail notice that materials are posted constitutes effective delivery; upon request, Agent will send copies by e‑mail/telecopier; Lenders must provide and maintain an effective e‑mail address.
- No waiver; remedies (Section 8.03): Failure or delay to exercise rights isn’t a waiver; partial exercise doesn’t preclude further exercise; remedies are cumulative.
- Costs and expenses (Section 8.04(a)): Company must pay reasonable enforcement costs and expenses of Agent and Lenders, including reasonable counsel fees.
- Indemnification (Section 8.04(b)): Company indemnifies Agent, Lenders, their Affiliates, and related personnel against claims, losses, liabilities, and expenses related to the Agreement, Notes, contemplated transactions, or use of proceeds, whether or not consummated, except for final, non‑appealable findings of gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad‑faith material breach.
- Liability limitations: No liability of Lender‑Related Parties for damages arising from others’ use of information via IntraLinks or similar systems; exclusion of indirect, punitive, or consequential damages among parties, except where such damages are incurred or paid to third parties by an Indemnified Party.

structure.title: No Waiver; Remedies
structure.summary:
- Electronic communications and notices: A Notice sent during a Lender’s normal business hours stating that materials are posted to the designated Platform constitutes effective delivery. Upon request, the Agent will also deliver copies by email or fax. Each Lender must provide and keep current an email address for receiving Notices.
- No waiver; cumulative remedies: Failure or delay in exercising rights under the Agreement or Loan Documents does not waive those rights; partial exercise does not preclude further exercise. All remedies are cumulative and non-exclusive.
- Costs and expenses: The Company must pay, on demand, the reasonable enforcement costs and expenses of the Agent and Lenders, including reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses related to enforcing the Agreement, Notes, and related documents.
- Indemnification: The Company agrees to indemnify the Agent, each Lender, their Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and advisors against claims, losses, liabilities, damages, and reasonable attorneys’ fees arising out of or related to the Agreement, the Notes, the contemplated transactions, or the use of Advance proceeds (including investigations and litigation), whether or not the transactions close or the Indemnified Party is a party, except to the extent finally determined to result from an Indemnified Party’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad-faith material breach.
- Limitation of liability: No Lender-Related Party is liable for damages arising from others’ use of information transmitted via IntraLinks or similar systems. No party is liable to another for indirect, punitive, or consequential damages related to the Agreement or Loan Documents or related activities, except that this does not affect such damages incurred or paid by an Indemnified Party to a third party.

structure.title: Costs and Expenses
structure.summary:
- Electronic notices and communications: Lenders agree that a Notice received during normal business hours stating that Communications have been posted to the Platform constitutes effective delivery. On request, the Agent will also send copies by email or fax. Each Lender must provide and keep current an email address, and Notices may be sent electronically.
- Section 8.03 No Waiver; Remedies: No delay or failure to exercise rights is a waiver; partial exercise does not preclude further exercise. Remedies are cumulative and not exclusive.
- Section 8.04 Costs and Expenses:
  - (a) The Company must pay on demand all reasonable enforcement costs and expenses of the Agent and Lenders, including reasonable counsel fees.
  - (b) The Company indemnifies the Agent, each Lender, and their Affiliates and related persons against claims, damages, losses, liabilities, and expenses arising out of or related to the Agreement, Notes, transactions, or use of proceeds, regardless of who brings the claim and whether or not the transactions close, except to the extent finally determined to result from the indemnified party’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material bad-faith breach. No Lender-Related Party is liable for damages from the use of information via IntraLinks or similar systems. No party is liable to another for indirect, punitive, or consequential damages relating to the Agreement or Loan Documents, except for such damages incurred or paid by an Indemnified Party to a third party.
  - (c) The Company must compensate Lenders for breakage costs resulting from early payment, conversion, or off-cycle assignment of Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advances, including costs of liquidating or reemploying funds.
  - (d) The obligations in Sections 2.11, 2.14, and 8.04 survive full payment and termination of the Agreement.
- Section 8.05 Right of Set-off: Upon an Event of Default and authorization to accelerate, each Lender and its Affiliates may set off deposits or other indebtedness they owe to any Borrower against the Borrower’s obligations, even if unmatured. A Defaulting Lender exercising setoff must promptly remit amounts to the Agent for application under Section 2.19, segregate such funds, hold them in trust, and report details to the Agent. Lenders will notify the Company after setoff. These rights are in addition to other remedies.
- Section 8.06 Binding Effect: Effective on the Effective Date; binding upon and benefiting the Company, any Borrowing Subsidiaries, the Agent, Lenders, and their successors and assigns. The Company may not assign its rights or obligations except as permitted by Section 5.02(b) with the prior written consent of all Lenders.

structure.title: Right of Set-off
structure.summary:
- Breakage/compensation: If a Borrower prepays, converts, accelerates, or assigns a Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advance on a day other than the last day of its Interest Period (including actions under specified sections or at the Company’s request), the Company must, upon a Lender’s demand (copied to the Agent), pay through the Agent all reasonable costs, losses, and expenses the Lender incurs (e.g., from liquidating or reemploying funding).
- Survival: The Company’s obligations under Sections 2.11, 2.14, and 8.04 survive full repayment of the Loans/Notes and termination of the Agreement.
- Right of set-off: Upon an Event of Default and authorization to accelerate under Section 6.01, each Lender and its Affiliates may set off any deposits or obligations owed to a Borrower against that Borrower’s obligations, even if unmatured. A Defaulting Lender exercising set-off must promptly transfer set-off amounts to the Agent for application under Section 2.19, segregate such funds pending transfer, and provide the Agent a detailed statement; Lenders must notify the Company after set-off. These rights are cumulative with other remedies.
- Binding effect/assignments: The Agreement is effective on the Effective Date and binds/benefits the Company, any Borrowing Subsidiary, the Agent, the Lenders, and their successors/assigns. The Company may not assign its rights/obligations (except as permitted by Section 5.02(b)) without the prior written consent of all Lenders.

structure.title: Binding Effect
structure.summary:
- Breakage compensation: If any Term SOFR or Eurocurrency Rate Advance is paid, converted, or assigned on a day other than the last day of its Interest Period (including due to prepayment, conversion under specified sections, acceleration, or assignment at the Company’s request), the Company must, upon a Lender’s demand (copied to the Agent), pay through the Agent all reasonable losses, costs, and expenses the Lender incurs, including funding breakage from liquidating or reemploying deposits/funds.
- Survival: The Company’s obligations under Sections 2.11, 2.14, and 8.04 survive full repayment of principal and interest, all other amounts due, and termination of the Agreement and Notes.
- Right of set-off: Upon an Event of Default and authorization under Section 6.01, each Lender and its Affiliates may, to the fullest extent permitted by law, set off any deposits or other indebtedness they owe to any Borrower against obligations under the Agreement and Notes, even if unmatured. Defaulting Lenders exercising set-off must immediately remit amounts to the Agent for application under Section 2.19, segregate such funds pending payment, and promptly provide the Agent a detailed statement; Lenders must promptly notify the Company after set-off (failure to notify does not affect validity). These rights are cumulative with other remedies.
- Binding effect and assignments: The Agreement is effective on the Effective Date and binds/benefits the Company, any Borrowing Subsidiary, the Agent, each Lender, and their successors/assigns. The Company may not assign its rights or obligations (or any interest) except as permitted by Section 5.02(b) or with prior written consent of all Lenders.

structure.title: Assignments and Participations
structure.summary:
- Section 8.07 (Assignments and Participations) sets out how Lenders may transfer or share their interests:
  - Assignments:
    - Lenders may assign all or part of their rights/obligations (including Revolving Credit and Swing Line commitments/advances) with 10 days’ notice to the Agent (and Sub-Agent for Swing Line), required consents (Company, Swing Line Lenders for Revolving Credit, not unreasonably withheld), and, if demanded by the Company under Sections 2.05(b) or 2.06(b), at least 20 Business Days’ notice.
    - Conditions include: assignment must be a constant percentage; minimum assignment size of $10,000,000 (with limited exceptions); assignee must be an Eligible Assignee; Company-arranged assignments under a Company demand must cover all of the assigning Lender’s interests (alone or concurrently with others); the assigning Lender must be paid in full (principal, accrued interest, and other amounts) at closing; execution of an Assignment and Assumption (Exhibit C), delivery of any related Note, a $3,500 processing fee, and completion of tax forms under Section 2.14 by the assignee.
    - Upon effectiveness, the assignee becomes a Lender to the extent assigned; the assignor is released to that extent (and ceases to be a party if fully assigned). The assignor’s indemnification and tax/expense rights and obligations under Sections 8.04, 2.11, and 2.14 survive.
  - SPV funding option:
    - A Lender (Granting Lender) may permit its identified SPV to fund Advances under its Commitment; no SPV funding commitment is created, and the Granting Lender remains obligated if the SPV does not fund.
    - Borrowers may enforce rights against either the Granting Lender or the SPV; SPV funding uses the Granting Lender’s Commitment.
    - Non-petition: parties agree not to initiate insolvency proceedings against an SPV until one year and one day after its commercial paper or other senior debt is paid.
    - An SPV may, without consent or fee, assign its interests to its Granting Lender or to liquidity/credit support providers (consented to by Company and Agent) and may share confidential information with certain SPV-related third parties on a confidential basis. This SPV paragraph cannot be amended without the consent of any SPV then holding Advances.
  - Representations in Assignment and Assumption:
    - Assignors make limited/no representations; assignees confirm independent credit analysis, Eligible Assignee status, acceptance of Agent’s authority, and agreement to perform Lender obligations.
  - Agent and Register:
    - Agent (as nonfiduciary agent for the Borrower) must accept proper Assignment and Assumption agreements, record them in a conclusive Register, and notify the Company.
    - Borrowers will issue replacement Notes as needed, dated the effective date of assignment, matching assigned/retained Commitments.
  - Participations:
    - Lenders may sell participations (with Company consent, not unreasonably withheld) while retaining their obligations and remaining the sole party of record; Borrowers, Agent, and Lenders deal only with the selling Lender.
    - Participants have no voting rights on amendments/waivers except as to reductions/postponements of principal, interest, or fees affecting their participation, or releases of the Company’s obligations (including Article IX).
    - Each Lender must maintain a conclusive Participant Register (in the U.S.); disclosure from the Participant Register is limited to what is necessary to establish “registered form” under U.S. Treasury Reg. §5f.103-1(c).
  - Information sharing:
    - Lenders may disclose borrower information to actual/prospective assignees/participants subject to confidentiality undertakings.
  - Pledges:
    - Lenders may create security interests in their rights (including Notes/Advances) in favor of Federal Reserve Banks or other relevant central banks.

- Section 8.08 (Confidentiality):
  - Agent and Lenders must keep Confidential Information confidential, with permitted disclosures to:
    - Affiliates and their officers/employees/agents/advisors, and actual/prospective assignees/participants (on a confidential basis).
    - As required by law/regulation/judicial process or by banking/regulatory authorities and examiners.
    - Rating agencies (subject to confidentiality undertakings).
    - In connection with exercising remedies or litigation/enforcement.
    - Data service providers (e.g., league table providers) for routine facility-identifying information only (Company name, type/amount/maturity of facility, roles/titles of arrangers/agents), excluding business-confidential details.
  - The Agent may disclose basic facility information to numbering agencies that assign standard loan identifiers (and provide a copy of the Agreement if requested), with instructions to maintain customary confidentiality and public release limited to standard identifier data.

structure.title: Confidentiality
structure.summary:
- Lenders’ information-sharing in transfers: In connection with assignments or participations (including proposed ones), a Lender may disclose Borrower information to assignees/participants, provided those recipients agree to maintain confidentiality of any Confidential Information.
- Security interests to central banks: A Lender may at any time pledge or create a security interest in its rights under the agreement (including advances and notes) in favor of a Federal Reserve Bank under Regulation A or another applicable central bank.
- Confidentiality obligations: The Agent and Lenders may not disclose Borrowers’ Confidential Information without the Company’s consent, subject to specific exceptions.
- Permitted disclosures (subject to confidentiality where applicable):
  - To Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, advisors, and actual/prospective assignees/participants on a confidential basis.
  - As required by law, regulation, or judicial process.
  - To rating agencies that agree to keep information confidential.
  - To state, federal, or foreign bank regulators and self-regulatory authorities.
  - In connection with exercising remedies, or in suits/actions/enforcement related to the agreement.
  - Routine deal data to lending-industry data services (e.g., league tables), limited to the Company’s identity, facility type/amount/maturity, and roles/titles of arrangers and agents, excluding confidential business information.
- Loan identifier disclosures: The Agent may provide basic facility information (and, if requested, a copy of the agreement) to organizations assigning standard identification numbers for loan facilities, with instructions to protect confidentiality and publicly release only customary identifier-related information.

structure.title: Governing Law
structure.summary:
- Governing law: The agreement, all other loan documents, and any related claims or disputes (contract, tort, or otherwise) are governed by New York law.
- Execution in counterparts and electronic signatures: The agreement may be signed in multiple counterparts; delivery by email/telecopy is effective. Electronic signatures, digital copies, and electronic platform executions approved by the Agent are given full legal effect under E-SIGN, New York ESRA, and similar laws.
- Jurisdiction and venue: Parties agree to bring any litigation relating to the agreement or loan documents exclusively in New York State courts in New York County or the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (including appellate courts), consent to those courts’ jurisdiction, and agree that final judgments may be enforced elsewhere. This does not limit actions to enforce judgments in other jurisdictions.
- Waivers: Parties waive objections to venue and the defense of forum non conveniens for proceedings in the specified New York courts.
- Service of process: Parties consent to service of process as provided for notices in Section 8.02, without limiting any other lawful methods of service.

structure.title: Execution in Counterparts
structure.summary:
- Governing law: The Agreement, other Loan Documents, and all related claims (contract, tort, or otherwise) are governed by New York law.
- Counterparts and electronic signatures: The Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts, including by email or fax; electronic signatures, electronic platforms, and digital copies have the same legal effect as manual signatures under ESIGN, New York’s ESRA, and UETA-like laws.
- Forum selection and jurisdiction: Parties agree not to bring actions relating to the Agreement/Loan Documents against the Agent, any Lender, or their Related Parties in any forum other than New York State courts in New York County or the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (including appellate courts), and they submit to the jurisdiction of those courts. Final judgments may be enforced in other jurisdictions, and rights to bring actions to enforce judgments elsewhere are preserved.
- Venue waivers: Parties waive objections to venue and any claim of inconvenient forum for proceedings in the designated New York courts.
- Service of process: Parties consent to service of process in the manner provided for notices in Section 8.02, without limiting any other lawful method of service.

structure.title: Jurisdiction, Etc.
structure.summary:
- Governing law: The Agreement, related Loan Documents, and any related claims (contract, tort, or otherwise) are governed by New York law, except where a specific Loan Document states otherwise.
- Counterparts and electronic execution: The Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts; emailed or faxed signature pages are effective. Electronic signatures, digital copies of manual signatures, and electronic platform contract formations approved by the Agent are valid and enforceable under applicable laws (including E-SIGN, New York ESRA, and UETA-based laws).
- Forum selection and jurisdiction: Parties agree to bring any actions relating to the Agreement or Loan Documents exclusively in New York state courts sitting in New York County or the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (including appellate courts), and submit to the jurisdiction of those courts. Final judgments there may be enforced elsewhere.
- Venue and forum waivers: Parties waive objections to venue and any claim of inconvenient forum in the specified courts.
- Service of process: Parties consent to service of process as provided for notices in Section 8.02, without limiting other lawful methods.
- Enforcement rights preserved: Parties may still bring actions in other jurisdictions to enforce judgments or against property.
- Scope: The jurisdictional covenant covers actions against the Agent, any Lender, and their Related Parties.

structure.title: WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL
structure.summary:
- Waiver of jury trial: Borrowers, the Agent, and Lenders irrevocably waive the right to a jury trial for any disputes (contract, tort, or otherwise) arising from the loan agreement, related loan documents, or the Agent’s/Lenders’ actions in negotiating, administering, performing, or enforcing them.
- USA PATRIOT Act notice: Lenders and the Agent must obtain, verify, and record identifying information about the Company (e.g., name and address) to comply with the Act’s customer identification requirements.
- No fiduciary duties: The parties acknowledge an arm’s-length, commercial relationship; the Agent, Lenders, and their Affiliates may have interests that conflict with the Company’s, and no fiduciary duties arise from the transactions or related communications.
- Bail-in acknowledgment and consent: All parties acknowledge that unsecured liabilities of any “Affected Financial Institution” under the agreement may be subject to a Resolution Authority’s write-down and conversion powers, and consent to:
  - Reduction or cancellation of such liabilities.
  - Conversion of such liabilities into equity or ownership instruments in the affected institution, its parent, or a bridge institution, which will be accepted in lieu of prior rights.

structure.title: USA PATRIOT Act Notice
structure.summary:
- Section 8.12: Mutual waiver of jury trial by the borrowers, agent, and lenders for any disputes, claims, or counterclaims (contract, tort, or otherwise) related to the agreement, other loan documents, or related actions (negotiation, administration, performance, enforcement).
- Section 8.13: USA PATRIOT Act notice that the agent and each lender must obtain, verify, and record identifying information about the company (e.g., name, address) to comply with the Act.
- Section 8.14: No fiduciary duties—parties acknowledge a purely commercial relationship; the agent, lenders, and their affiliates may have interests that conflict with the company’s, and no fiduciary obligations arise from the transactions or communications.
- Section 8.15: Acknowledgment and consent to bail-in—parties agree that unsecured liabilities of any affected financial institution under the agreement may be subject to resolution authority write-down and conversion powers, including reduction/cancellation of liabilities or conversion into equity or ownership instruments of the institution, its parent, or a bridge institution, accepted in lieu of prior rights.

structure.title: No Fiduciary Duties
structure.summary:
- Waiver of jury trial: Borrowers, the Agent, and Lenders irrevocably waive the right to a jury trial for any disputes related to the agreement, other loan documents, or the Agent/Lenders’ actions in negotiating, administering, performing, or enforcing them.
- USA PATRIOT Act notice: Lenders and the Agent must obtain, verify, and record identifying information about the Company (e.g., name, address) to comply with the Act.
- No fiduciary duties: The parties acknowledge potential conflicts of interest and agree their relationship is purely commercial, creating no fiduciary duty for the Agent, Lenders, or their affiliates.
- Bail-in acknowledgement and consent: Parties agree that unsecured liabilities of an Affected Financial Institution under the agreement may be subject to a Resolution Authority’s write-down and conversion powers, including reduction or cancellation of liabilities or conversion into equity/ownership instruments of the institution, its parent, or a bridge institution, accepted in lieu of prior rights.

structure.title: Acknowledgement and Consent to Bail-In of Affected Financial Institutions
structure.summary:
- Waiver of Jury Trial: Borrowers, the Agent, and Lenders irrevocably waive the right to a jury trial for any disputes related to the agreement, other loan documents, or related actions (contract, tort, or otherwise).
- USA PATRIOT Act Notice: Lenders and the Agent must obtain, verify, and record identifying information about the Company (e.g., name, address) to comply with the Act.
- No Fiduciary Duties: The Company acknowledges potential economic conflicts and agrees the relationship with the Agent, Lenders, and their Affiliates is purely commercial, creating no fiduciary duties.
- Bail-In Acknowledgement and Consent: All parties acknowledge that unsecured liabilities of Affected Financial Institutions may be subject to Resolution Authorities’ Write-Down and Conversion Powers (including reduction/cancellation of liabilities, conversion to equity or ownership instruments, and variation of terms). Includes detailed definitions for Affected Financial Institution, Bail-In Action, Bail-In Legislation (EEA and UK), EEA Financial Institution, EEA Member Country, EEA Resolution Authority, EU Bail-In Legislation Schedule, Resolution Authority, UK Financial Institution, UK Resolution Authority, and Write-Down and Conversion Powers. Lenders must notify the Agent (who notifies the Company) if subject to a Bail-In Action.
- Judgment and Currency Conversion: Sets the exchange rate method for converting sums between Dollars and Euros for court judgments (using Citibank London rates at 11:00 A.M. London time on the preceding Business Day). Establishes an indemnity/true-up: the Borrower must cover any shortfall caused by currency conversion from a judgment currency to the primary currency, and Lenders/Agent must remit any excess to the Borrower.

structure.title: Judgment
structure.summary:
- Defines UK Resolution Authority as the Bank of England or another UK public authority responsible for resolving UK financial institutions.
- Defines Write-Down and Conversion Powers (bail-in) for both EEA and UK contexts, allowing resolution authorities to cancel, reduce, modify, convert, or suspend liabilities, or treat contracts as if rights were exercised, under applicable Bail-In Legislation.
- Section 8.16 (Judgment): Sets currency conversion rules for court judgments:
  - Converting Dollar obligations into another currency uses the rate at which the Agent could purchase Dollars with that currency at Citibank London, 11:00 A.M. (London time), on the business day before judgment.
  - Converting Euro obligations into Dollars uses the rate at which the Agent could purchase Euros with Dollars at the same time/place.
  - Establishes “Primary Currency” vs. “Judgment Currency” mechanics: obligations are discharged only to the extent the Judgment Currency can buy the Primary Currency the next business day; the borrower indemnifies any shortfall and receives any excess.
- Article IX (Guarantee):
  - Section 9.01: The Company unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees to the Lenders and Agent the prompt payment of principal, interest, and all other amounts owed by each Borrowing Subsidiary under the agreement and its Designation Letter, paying immediately upon any default without demand, including after extensions or renewals.
  - Section 9.02: The guarantee (and any obligations assumed under Section 2.17(b)) is absolute and unconditional despite any issues with validity/enforceability, amendments, extensions, waivers, exchanges or releases of collateral/other guarantees, or other circumstances; the Company waives diligence, presentment, demand, protest, and notices; no need for the Agent/Lenders to exhaust remedies; it is a guarantee of payment, not collection.
  - Section 9.03: The guarantee is automatically reinstated if payments by a Borrowing Subsidiary are rescinded or must be restored (e.g., in bankruptcy or reorganization).

structure.title: GUARANTEE
structure.summary:
- Establishes an unconditional and irrevocable guaranty by the Company in favor of the Agent and each Lender (and their successors/assigns) for all obligations of each Borrowing Subsidiary under the agreement pursuant to its Designation Letter, including prompt payment of principal, interest, and all other amounts when due (at maturity, upon acceleration, or prepayment).
- Confirms the guaranty is one of payment (not collection): the Company must pay immediately upon a Borrowing Subsidiary’s failure to pay, without demand or notice, and regardless of extensions, renewals, amendments, or modifications.
- States the Company’s obligations under Article IX (and any obligations assumed under Section 2.17(b)) are absolute and unconditional, unaffected by the validity, legality, enforceability, modification, waiver, or release of the underlying obligations, guarantees, or collateral, or any other circumstance that might otherwise discharge a surety.
- Includes express waivers by the Company of diligence, presentment, demand, protest, and all notices, and waives any requirement that the Agent or Lenders first proceed against any Borrowing Subsidiary, other guarantor, or collateral.
- Provides for automatic reinstatement of the guaranty if any payment by or for a Borrowing Subsidiary is rescinded or must be restored (e.g., due to bankruptcy or similar proceedings).

structure.title: Guarantee
structure.summary:
- Establishes an unconditional, irrevocable guarantee by the Company in favor of each Lender and the Agent (and their successors/assigns) for the prompt, full payment of principal, interest, and all other amounts owed by each Borrowing Subsidiary under the Agreement pursuant to its Designation Letter, including amounts due at maturity, upon acceleration, or prepayment, and through any extensions or renewals.
- If a Borrowing Subsidiary fails to pay when due, the Company must promptly pay without demand or notice; the guarantee covers payment “to the extent of” Advances made to the relevant Borrowing Subsidiary.
- The Company’s obligations are absolute and unconditional, unaffected by the validity or enforceability of the underlying obligations, any amendments, extensions, waivers, releases of other guarantees or security, or any other circumstance that might otherwise discharge a guarantor; includes obligations (if any) assumed under Section 2.17(b).
- The Company waives diligence, presentment, demand, protest, and all notices, and Lenders/Agent need not exhaust remedies or proceed first against any Borrowing Subsidiary, other guarantor, or collateral; this is a guarantee of payment, not collection.
- The guarantee is automatically reinstated if payments by or on behalf of a Borrowing Subsidiary are rescinded or must be restored (e.g., in bankruptcy or reorganization).

structure.title: Obligations Unconditional
structure.summary:
- Establishes an unconditional and irrevocable parent guarantee (by the “Company”) in favor of the Agent and all Lenders (and their successors/assigns) for the “Guaranteed Obligations.”
- Guaranteed Obligations include prompt payment in full of principal and interest on Advances and related Notes of each Borrowing Subsidiary (limited to principal and interest attributable to Advances made to that Subsidiary), plus all other amounts owed under the Agreement pursuant to the Subsidiary’s Designation Letter.
- If any Borrowing Subsidiary fails to pay when due (at maturity, upon acceleration, mandatory/optional prepayment, or otherwise), the Company must promptly pay without demand or notice; this also applies after any extension or renewal, in accordance with the new terms.
- The guarantee is absolute and unconditional regardless of: validity or enforceability of the underlying obligations; amendments/modifications; extensions, waivers, or failures to enforce; changes in, exchanges of, or releases of collateral or other guarantees; or any other surety defenses.
- The Company waives diligence, presentment, demand, protest, and all notices, and waives any requirement that the Agent or Lenders first exhaust remedies or proceed against any Borrowing Subsidiary, any other person, any Designation Letter, any Note, other guarantors, or collateral.
- Clarifies this is a guarantee of payment (not merely collection), allowing direct recourse to the Company.
- The Company’s obligations also cover any obligations it assumes under Section 2.17(b) (referenced but not detailed here) on the same unconditional terms.
- Provides a reinstatement clause: if any payment by or for a Borrowing Subsidiary is rescinded or must be restored (e.g., due to bankruptcy or reorganization), the guarantee revives to the extent of such restoration.

structure.title: Reinstatement
structure.summary:
- Article IX establishes an unconditional and irrevocable guarantee by the Company in favor of the Lenders and the Agent (and their successors/assigns) for the prompt payment in full of all amounts owed by each Borrowing Subsidiary under the Agreement, including principal, interest on Advances, and other amounts per their Designation Letters and Notes.
- The guarantee is a guarantee of payment (not collection): if a Borrowing Subsidiary fails to pay when due (including at maturity, upon acceleration, prepayment, or renewal/extension), the Company must promptly pay without demand or notice.
- The Company’s obligations under Article IX—and any obligations assumed under Section 2.17(b)—are absolute and unconditional, unaffected by the validity or enforceability of the underlying obligations, amendments or modifications, extensions, waivers, failures to enforce, releases or exchanges of other guarantees or collateral, or any other circumstances that could otherwise discharge a guarantor.
- The Company waives diligence, presentment, demand, protest, and all notices, and the Lenders/Agent are not required to exhaust remedies or proceed first against any Borrowing Subsidiary, other guarantor, or collateral.
- Reinstatement: if any payment by or on behalf of a Borrowing Subsidiary is rescinded or must be restored (e.g., due to bankruptcy or reorganization), the guarantee is automatically reinstated to the extent of such payment.

structure.title: Subrogation
structure.summary:
- Outlines guarantee provisions under Article IX.
- Section 9.04: The Company irrevocably waives all rights of subrogation and contribution (including rights under the Bankruptcy Code) until the Commitments terminate and all Advances, interest, and other amounts owed to the Agent and Lenders are paid in full.
- Section 9.05: For purposes of enforcing the Company’s guarantee, the obligations of any Borrowing Subsidiary may be declared due and payable or deemed accelerated under Article VI notwithstanding any bankruptcy stay or injunction affecting the subsidiary; upon such declaration or automatic acceleration, those obligations become immediately due and payable by the Company.
- Section 9.06: The guarantee is continuing and applies to all Guaranteed Obligations whenever they arise.

structure.title: Remedies
structure.summary:

- Remedies and acceleration: For purposes of the Company’s guarantee, the obligations of any Borrowing Subsidiary may be declared due and payable or deemed automatically accelerated under Article VI despite any stay or injunction (including in bankruptcy) affecting the subsidiary; upon such declaration or acceleration, those obligations become immediately due and payable by the Company under Section 9.01.
- Continuing guarantee: The Article IX guarantee is continuing and applies to all Guaranteed Obligations whenever they arise.
